shelves.title: Calibrated thrombin generation in health: peak thrombin and ETP rise with age and on oral contraceptives — but every number is platform-specific
shelves.question: In healthy humans, what does calibrated thrombin generation measure — lag time, peak thrombin and endogenous thrombin potential distributions in health, and how do age, sex and oral contraception shift them?
shelves.mesh: Thrombin · Blood Coagulation Tests · Contraceptives, Oral, Hormonal · Age Factors · Sex Factors
shelves.balance: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING — because the measurement is real and reproducible within a platform, but assay standardisation between laboratories and platforms is incomplete, so there is no single healthy distribution to quote — exactly the flag this row carries. The textbook framing (Guyton & Hall / Ganong on haemostasis) is thin for this assay, and the shelf says so: it rests on the primary measurement literature. What calibrated thrombin generation measures, from the carded records: plasma is triggered with tissue factor and the thrombin formed over time is read against a calibrator, yielding lag time, peak thrombin, time to peak and the area under the curve — endogenous thrombin potential (ETP). The healthy distributions are condition-specific: in 120 healthy Chinese subjects the CAT ranges (as printed, mean ± 2SD) were lag time 3.648 ± 2.465 min, peak 367.39 ± 151.93 nmol/L, ETP 2277 ± 1030 nmol/L·min (Wu 2014); on the automated ST Genesia platform, mean peak height in 117 healthy donors was 164–167 nM with one reagent and 335–351 nM with another in the same donors (Ninivaggi 2021) — the same blood, a twofold different 'normal' peak, which is the standardisation problem in one line. Age and sex move the curve: thrombin generation increased with age and was higher in women than men in 140 healthy people, with lag time set mainly by free TFPI, free protein S, factor VII, FIX and fibrinogen, and ETP/peak by fibrinogen, factor XII, free TFPI and antithrombin at low tissue factor (Dielis 2008). Oral contraception shifts it further: users had the shortest lag and time-to-peak and the highest peak and ETP with and without added activated protein C, and on ST Genesia their mean peak ran ~263–473 nM across reagents against ~164–351 nM in non-users, with thrombomodulin suppressing ETP by only 25% in users versus 47–54% in non-users (Tchaikovski 2007; Ninivaggi 2021).

cards.headline: Dielis 2008: in 140 healthy people, thrombin generation rose with age and was higher in women — lag time set by free TFPI, free protein S, FVII, FIX and fibrinogen; ETP and peak by fibrinogen, FXII, free TFPI and antithrombin
cards.summary: Dielis 2008: in 140 healthy people, thrombin generation rose with age and was higher in women — lag time set by free TFPI, free protein S, FVII, FIX and fibrinogen; ETP and peak by fibrinogen, FXII, free TFPI and antithrombin
cards.type: Human assay-determinants study (thrombin generation in a normal population), J Thromb Haemost 2008
cards.people: One hundred and forty healthy individuals whose plasma coagulation factors and inhibitors were measured alongside thrombin generation at 1 pM tissue factor ± thrombomodulin and 13.6 pM tissue factor ± activated protein C, analysed by multiple regression.
cards.result: Thrombin generation increased with age and was higher in females than in males, under all conditions. The lag time depended mainly on free tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI), free protein S, factor VII, factor IX and fibrinogen. At 1 pM tissue factor, ETP and peak height were determined mainly by fibrinogen, factor XII (despite inhibition of contact activation), free TFPI and antithrombin, with protein C adding its effect when thrombomodulin was present; at 13.6 pM the determinant set shifted (prothrombin, antithrombin, fibrinogen, free TFPI, factor V without APC). The record's lesson, carried on the face: there is no single 'normal thrombin generation' — the determinants themselves change with the trigger conditions.
cards.watchOut: Determinants are regression associations in one laboratory's conditions (1 vs 13.6 pM tissue factor) — they explain the curve's inputs, not a clinical risk prediction.
cards.source: Dielis AW, Castoldi E, Spronk HM, van Oerle R, et al.. Coagulation factors and the protein C system as determinants of thrombin generation in a normal population. Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH. 2008. PMID: 17988231. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Tchaikovski 2007: oral-contraceptive users (n = 187) had the shortest lag time and the highest peak and ETP of any healthy group, with and without added activated protein C
cards.summary: Tchaikovski 2007: oral-contraceptive users (n = 187) had the shortest lag time and the highest peak and ETP of any healthy group, with and without added activated protein C
cards.type: Human assay study (calibrated automated thrombography and oral contraceptives), Thromb Haemost 2007
cards.people: Healthy men (n = 8), women not using oral contraceptives (n = 28) and women using different oral contraceptives (n = 187), studied by calibrated automated thrombography in the absence and presence of added activated protein C (APC). The male group is small — n = 8 printed on the face.
cards.result: With and without APC, OC users' plasma showed the shortest lag time and time to peak and the highest peak height and ETP. Without APC, the parameters did not differ between progestogen types; with APC, users of gestodene-, desogestrel-, drospirenone- and cyproterone-acetate-containing pills showed shorter lag/time-to-peak and higher peak/ETP than levonorgestrel users. ETP measured with APC correlated almost perfectly with the APC sensitivity ratio (r = 0.95), while ETP without APC had no predictive value for it (r = 0.11). Conclusion on the face: OC use increases thrombin generation, and the progestogen differences act through the protein C system.
cards.watchOut: Assay shifts, not thrombosis outcomes — the record links the pattern to venous-thrombosis risk differences between pill generations as interpretation, and this card keeps it as such. Male comparison group n = 8.
cards.source: Tchaikovski SN, van Vliet HA, Thomassen MC, Bertina RM, et al.. Effect of oral contraceptives on thrombin generation measured via calibrated automated thrombography. Thrombosis and haemostasis. 2007. PMID: 18064335. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Wu 2014: a healthy reference range on the CAT platform — lag time 3.648 ± 2.465 min, peak thrombin 367.39 ± 151.93 nmol/L, ETP 2277 ± 1030 nmol/L·min in 120 healthy Chinese subjects, all four parameters age-correlated
cards.summary: Wu 2014: a healthy reference range on the CAT platform — lag time 3.648 ± 2.465 min, peak thrombin 367.39 ± 151.93 nmol/L, ETP 2277 ± 1030 nmol/L·min in 120 healthy Chinese subjects, all four parameters age-correlated
cards.type: Human reference-range study (calibrated automated thrombogram in healthy subjects), Biomed Environ Sci 2014
cards.people: One hundred and twenty healthy subjects whose plasma was used to establish overall and age-specific normal ranges for the four calibrated automated thrombogram parameters; a normal plasma pool (n = 25) spiked with heparin or enoxaparin tested the assay's anticoagulant sensitivity.
cards.result: The normal ranges (calculated as mean ± 2SD, as the record states) were: lag time 3.648 ± 2.465 min; peak thrombin 367.39 ± 151.93 nmol/L; ETP 2277 ± 1030 nmol/L·min; time to peak 6.372 ± 4.280 min. Age correlated linearly with every parameter — negatively with lag time (r = −0.6583, P < 0.0001) and time to peak (r = −0.6313), positively with peak (r = 0.4863, P < 0.0001) and ETP (r = 0.3608, P < 0.0014): with age the curve starts sooner and runs higher. The ETP/peak ratio tracked heparin and enoxaparin concentrations linearly in the spiked pool.
cards.watchOut: One population, one platform, the record's own trigger conditions — these ranges are not transferable to other CAT protocols or to the ST Genesia platform (next card), which is precisely the shelf's point.
cards.source: Wu J, Zhao HR, Zhang HY, Ge YL, et al.. Thrombin generation increasing with age and decreasing with use of heparin indicated by calibrated automated thrombogram conducted in Chinese. Biomedical and environmental sciences : BES. 2014. PMID: 24827719. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Ninivaggi 2021: on the standardised ST Genesia platform, the same 117 healthy donors give mean peaks of ~165 nM with one reagent and ~345 nM with another — and oral contraceptives raise peak by ~60–120 nM on every reagent
cards.summary: Ninivaggi 2021: on the standardised ST Genesia platform, the same 117 healthy donors give mean peaks of ~165 nM with one reagent and ~345 nM with another — and oral contraceptives raise peak by ~60–120 nM on every reagent
cards.type: Human reference-values study (ST Genesia thrombin generation in healthy donors), Res Pract Thromb Haemost 2021
cards.people: One hundred and seventeen healthy donors (mean age 35 ± 12 years; 49.6% men, 37.6% women not using oral contraceptives, 12.8% women using them), measured on the fully automated ST Genesia with three reagent kits (STG-BleedScreen, STG-DrugScreen, STG-ThromboScreen, the last ± thrombomodulin), with reference ranges set as the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles.
cards.result: Mean peak height in men and women not using OCs was 167 and 164 nM (BleedScreen), 335 and 351 nM (DrugScreen), and 192 and 198 nM (ThromboScreen) — men and non-OC women essentially identical, but a twofold spread between reagents in the same donors. Women taking OCs averaged 263, 473 and 312 nM respectively (P < 0.05 versus both other groups). Thrombomodulin reduced ETP by 54% in men and 47% in women without OCs, but only 25% in women with OCs (P < 0.05) — the protein-C brake works less hard on contraceptive plasma, on this platform as on the CAT.
cards.watchOut: Percentages for thrombomodulin are within-assay ETP reductions (assay quantities, not clinical risk), printed alongside the absolute peak values. Reagent-specific reference ranges are mandatory — the record's design assumes it.
cards.source: Ninivaggi M, de Laat-Kremers RMW, Carlo A, de Laat B. ST Genesia reference values of 117 healthy donors measured with STG-BleedScreen, STG-DrugScreen and STG-ThromboScreen reagents. Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis. 2021. PMID: 33537543. Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH: not captured from the record this session

cards.headline: Synthesis: calibrated thrombin generation is a real, factor-determined curve that rises with age and on contraceptives — but 'normal' is a platform-and-reagent statement, not a universal range
cards.summary: Synthesis: calibrated thrombin generation is a real, factor-determined curve that rises with age and on contraceptives — but 'normal' is a platform-and-reagent statement, not a universal range
cards.people: Synthesis of the four carded human studies above (Dielis 2008; Tchaikovski 2007; Wu 2014; Ninivaggi 2021). Textbook framing is thin for this assay (Guyton & Hall / Ganong cover haemostasis, not thrombography) and the shelf rests on the primary measurement literature, as its slate row requires it to say.
cards.result: The curve's anatomy is settled: lag time reads the initiation factors and inhibitors (free TFPI, free protein S, FVII, FIX, fibrinogen), peak and ETP read the propagation balance (fibrinogen, prothrombin, antithrombin, TFPI, and the protein C system when thrombomodulin or APC is added). The shifts are concordant across platforms: generation rises with age in both the CAT reference study and the determinants study; women run higher than men at low trigger in one, identical to men on the automated platform in another — a conditions difference, kept visible; and oral contraceptives raise peak and ETP and blunt the thrombomodulin brake on both platforms, with progestogen differences appearing only when the protein C pathway is engaged. What is NOT settled is the number itself: peak thrombin in health is ~165 nM or ~345 nM depending on reagent, and ETP 2277 ± 1030 nmol/L·min is one population on one protocol. Hence PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING: a mature measurement whose reference physiology is still platform-bound. No animal thrombin-generation data are carded.
cards.watchOut: Never compare a patient value against a range from a different platform, reagent or tissue-factor concentration — every card on this shelf names its conditions for that reason.
cards.source: Synthesis of the carded records above (PMIDs 17988231, 18064335, 24827719, 33537543), with textbook framing as cited. Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH: not captured from the record this session

shelves.title: Belumosudil in chronic graft-versus-host disease after at least two prior lines: responses in about three quarters of patients, in single-arm studies only
shelves.question: In patients with chronic GVHD after two or more prior systemic lines, does the ROCK2 inhibitor belumosudil 200 mg daily (or twice daily), versus no concurrent control, produce overall responses, and how durable are they?
shelves.mesh: Acetamides/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Adult · Aged · Female · Graft vs Host Disease/drug therapy · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Treatment Outcome · Young Adult · rho-Associated Kinases/antagonists & inhibitors · Acetamides/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Cohort Studies · Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation/adverse effects,methods · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Adolescent · 1-(5-Isoquinolinesulfonyl)-2-Methylpiperazine/analogs & derivatives,therapeutic use · Chronic Disease · Follow-Up Studies · Graft vs Host Disease/drug therapy,etiology · Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation/adverse effects · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/therapeutic use · Acetamides · Fibrosis/drug therapy · Graft vs Host Disease/drug therapy,pathology,etiology,metabolism · Inflammation/drug therapy,etiology,pathology · Interleukin-17/metabolism · Mouth Mucosa/pathology,drug effects,metabolism
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — a single programme of dose-randomised but not placebo-controlled studies: response rates are single-arm readings against response criteria and must be framed that way. ROCKstar (132 patients, 2-5 prior lines) found best overall response rates of 74% on belumosudil (Rezurock, Kadmon/Sanofi) 200 mg daily and 77% on 200 mg twice daily, with a median response duration of 54 weeks and symptom improvement in about six in ten patients; 12% discontinued for possibly drug-related adverse events. The earlier KD025-208 study (54 patients) found response rates of 62-69% across doses, corticosteroid discontinuation in 19%, and 2-year overall survival of 82% (no comparator). The pooled long-term analysis (208 patients, median follow-up 31.4 months) held the response rate at 72% with median response duration 62.3 weeks. A 20-patient tissue companion study is mechanistic support, not efficacy evidence. No randomised comparison against another treatment exists, so POSSIBLE — not LIKELY — is the ceiling.

cards.headline: ROCKstar 2021: best overall response 74% on belumosudil 200 mg daily and 77% on twice-daily dosing in 132 patients with chronic GVHD after 2-5 prior lines (no placebo arm)
cards.summary: ROCKstar 2021: best overall response 74% on belumosudil 200 mg daily and 77% on twice-daily dosing in 132 patients with chronic GVHD after 2-5 prior lines (no placebo arm)
cards.type: Phase 2 randomised dose-comparison registration study (no placebo or active control)
cards.people: 132 patients with chronic graft-versus-host disease after 2 to 5 prior lines of therapy, randomised between belumosudil 200 mg once daily (66 patients) and 200 mg twice daily (66 patients); median follow-up 14 months. Primary endpoint was best overall response rate.
cards.result: Best overall response was 74% (95% CI 62 to 84) on once-daily and 77% (95% CI 65 to 87) on twice-daily dosing, with responses in all subgroups and complete responses in all affected organs. Median duration of response was 54 weeks, 44% of patients remained on therapy for at least a year, and symptom reduction was reported in 59% and 62% respectively. Sixteen patients (12%) discontinued because of possible drug-related adverse events; adverse events were consistent with those expected in chronic GVHD patients on corticosteroids and other immunosuppressants.
cards.watchOut: Dose-randomised only: a 74-77% response rate without a control arm cannot separate drug effect from natural fluctuation and concomitant-therapy effects in chronic GVHD.
cards.source: Cutler C et al. Belumosudil for chronic graft-versus-host disease after 2 or more prior lines of therapy: the ROCKstar Study. Blood. 2021. PMID: 34265047. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03640481. cards.headline: KD025-208 2021: response rates of 62-69% across belumosudil doses in 54 heavily pretreated patients, with corticosteroids stopped in 19%
cards.summary: KD025-208 2021: response rates of 62-69% across belumosudil doses in 54 heavily pretreated patients, with corticosteroids stopped in 19%
cards.people: 54 patients with chronic GVHD after 1 to 3 prior lines (78% severe disease, 50% with at least 4 organs involved, 73% refractory to their last line), treated open-label with belumosudil 200 mg once daily, 200 mg twice daily or 400 mg once daily; median follow-up 29 months.
cards.result: Overall response rates were 65% (95% CI 38 to 86) once daily, 69% (41 to 89) twice daily and 62% (38 to 82) at 400 mg once daily. Median duration of response was 35 weeks; failure-free survival was 76% at 6 months and 47% at 12 months; 2-year overall survival was 82%. Corticosteroids were discontinued in 19% of patients. The drug was well tolerated with low rates of cytopenia and no apparent increased infection risk, including cytomegalovirus.
cards.watchOut: Fifty-four patients across three dose cohorts — the wide confidence intervals (for example 38 to 86%) show how little precision a cohort this size carries.
cards.source: Jagasia M et al. ROCK2 Inhibition With Belumosudil (KD025) for the Treatment of Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease. J Clin Oncol. 2021. PMID: 33877856. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02841995. cards.headline: Pooled long-term analysis 2025: response rate held at 72% across 208 patients from both studies, median response duration 62.3 weeks
cards.summary: Pooled long-term analysis 2025: response rate held at 72% across 208 patients from both studies, median response duration 62.3 weeks
cards.type: Pooled long-term analysis of the programme's studies (single-arm)
cards.people: 208 patients from KD025-208, ROCKstar and the KD025-217 extension study, in three dose cohorts (200 mg once daily 95 patients, 200 mg twice daily 92, 400 mg once daily 21); overall median follow-up 31.4 months.
cards.result: Best overall response rate in the modified intention-to-treat population was 72%; median duration of response among responders was 62.3 weeks. Median failure-free survival was 15.1 months (1-year 56%, 2-year 40%) and median time to next treatment 22.1 months, with 47% of patients receiving a new systemic therapy by 36 months.
cards.watchOut: A pooled re-analysis of the same patients carded above — it adds durability, not independent confirmation, and must not be counted as a third trial.

cards.headline: ROCKstar tissue companion 2025: in 20 patients with oral chronic GVHD, belumosudil reduced oral-mucosal collagen and IL-17-positive cells over 6 months — mechanism, not efficacy
cards.summary: ROCKstar tissue companion 2025: in 20 patients with oral chronic GVHD, belumosudil reduced oral-mucosal collagen and IL-17-positive cells over 6 months — mechanism, not efficacy
cards.people: 20 patients with oral chronic graft-versus-host disease from ROCKstar, with oral mucosa, minor salivary gland and skin tissue and peripheral blood sampled before and after 6 months of belumosudil (paired oral-mucosa samples in 14, salivary-gland pairs in 11).
cards.result: Collagen in oral mucosa fell in parallel with decreased IL-17-positive cell frequency in oral mucosa and salivary glands; CD4 regulatory T cells increased in salivary glands and blood. Responders showed reductions in collagen type I and IL-17 in oral mucosa, and salivary transforming growth factor beta 1 fell significantly and correlated with IL-17 levels.
cards.watchOut: Twenty patients and surrogate tissue endpoints: this card explains how the drug may work in tissue; it adds nothing to the estimate of how well it works.

shelves.title: Axatilimab in recurrent or refractory chronic graft-versus-host disease: 74% response at the lowest dose — less drug worked better, in a single uncontrolled programme
shelves.question: In patients with recurrent or refractory chronic GVHD after ≥2 prior lines, does the CSF-1R antibody axatilimab (0.3, 1.0 or 3.0 mg/kg), versus no concurrent control, produce overall responses?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Child · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Young Adult · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Chronic Disease/drug therapy · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Graft vs Host Disease/diagnosis,drug therapy,immunology,metabolism · Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation/adverse effects · Infusions, Intravenous · Receptor, Macrophage Colony-Stimulating Factor/antagonists & inhibitors,metabolism · Recurrence · Severity of Illness Index · Treatment Outcome · Bronchiolitis Obliterans Syndrome · Graft vs Host Disease/drug therapy · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/therapeutic use · Biological Products/therapeutic use · Chronic Disease · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/pharmacokinetics,adverse effects,administration & dosage,therapeutic use
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — a single programme (one pivotal dose-randomised phase 2 trial, one earlier phase 1/2 study, and an exposure-response analysis of the same patients) for the CSF-1R antibody axatilimab (Niktimvo, Incyte/Syndax), with no placebo or active comparator. AGAVE-201 (241 patients) met its primary endpoint at every dose, but with an inverted dose-response: overall response was 74% at 0.3 mg/kg every 2 weeks, 67% at 1 mg/kg every 2 weeks and 50% at 3 mg/kg every 4 weeks, while discontinuations for adverse events rose with dose (6%, 22% and 18%). The exposure-response analysis explains the inversion — lower exposure raised the odds of response while higher exposure raised the odds of adverse events on 10 of 11 safety endpoints — and the earlier phase 1/2 study (40 patients) had already shown an 82% response rate in the first six cycles at the doses carried forward. The common adverse events are dose-dependent transient laboratory abnormalities of CSF1R blockade. One programme, however consistent, caps at POSSIBLE. A reduced-frequency dosing report in the slate row was not carded: its PubMed record carries no abstract, so its claims could not be verified from its own record this session.

cards.headline: AGAVE-201 2024: overall response 74% at the lowest axatilimab dose, 67% at the middle dose and 50% at the highest — the primary endpoint was met at all three doses (241 patients)
cards.summary: AGAVE-201 2024: overall response 74% at the lowest axatilimab dose, 67% at the middle dose and 50% at the highest — the primary endpoint was met at all three doses (241 patients)
cards.type: Phase 2 multinational randomised dose-comparison pivotal study (no placebo or active control)
cards.people: 241 patients with recurrent or refractory chronic graft-versus-host disease, randomised to intravenous axatilimab 0.3 mg/kg every 2 weeks (80 patients), 1 mg/kg every 2 weeks (81) or 3 mg/kg every 4 weeks (80). Primary endpoint: overall response in the first six cycles, met if the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval exceeded 30%.
cards.result: Overall response was 74% (95% CI 63 to 83) at 0.3 mg/kg, 67% (55 to 77) at 1 mg/kg and 50% (39 to 61) at 3 mg/kg — the endpoint was met in all groups. A symptom improvement of more than 5 points on the modified Lee Symptom Scale occurred in 60%, 69% and 41% respectively. The most common adverse events were dose-dependent transient laboratory abnormalities related to CSF1R blockade; discontinuation for adverse events occurred in 6%, 22% and 18%.
cards.watchOut: Dose-randomised, not controlled against standard care: response percentages are single-arm readings, and the inverted dose-response means 'more drug' is not 'more benefit' here.
cards.source: Wolff D et al. Axatilimab in Recurrent or Refractory Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease. N Engl J Med. 2024. PMID: 39292927. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04710576. cards.headline: Phase 1/2 study 2023: axatilimab produced an 82% overall response in the first six cycles in 40 patients after at least two prior lines
cards.summary: Phase 1/2 study 2023: axatilimab produced an 82% overall response in the first six cycles in 40 patients after at least two prior lines
cards.people: 40 patients aged 6 years or older with active chronic GVHD after at least two prior systemic therapy lines (17 in phase 1 dose-finding, 23 in phase 2), treated open-label; phase 2 primary endpoint was overall response at the start of cycle 7.
cards.result: The phase 2 cohort met its primary endpoint with a 50% overall response rate at cycle 7 day 1, and the overall response rate in the first six cycles — the endpoint supporting regulatory approvals — was 82%. Responses occurred in all affected organs regardless of prior therapy, and 58% of patients reported significant symptom improvement on the Lee scale. At least one treatment-related adverse event occurred in 30 patients, with grade 3 or worse treatment-related events in eight, mostly known on-target effects of CSF-1R inhibition; no cytomegalovirus reactivations occurred. Two dose-limiting toxicities occurred at 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks in phase 1.
cards.watchOut: Forty patients, no comparator, and the headline figure depends on the endpoint window (50% at cycle 7 day 1 vs 82% across the first six cycles) — both are printed so neither can be cherry-picked.
cards.source: Kitko CL et al. Axatilimab for Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease After Failure of at Least Two Prior Systemic Therapies: Results of a Phase I/II Study. J Clin Oncol. 2023. PMID: 36459673. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03604692. cards.headline: Exposure-response analysis 2025: lower axatilimab exposure raised the odds of response while higher exposure raised the odds of adverse events — the lowest regimen had the best predicted balance
cards.summary: Exposure-response analysis 2025: lower axatilimab exposure raised the odds of response while higher exposure raised the odds of adverse events — the lowest regimen had the best predicted balance
cards.type: Exposure-response modelling analysis of the programme's trials
cards.people: 239 treated patients in AGAVE-201 for exposure-efficacy, and 239 AGAVE-201 plus 39 phase 1/2 patients for exposure-safety, using a population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model with logistic and Cox regression.
cards.result: Overall response and at least 7-point Lee Symptom Scale improvement were associated with exposure such that lower exposure increased the odds of response; duration of response was not associated with exposure. Ten of 11 safety endpoints were associated with exposure in the opposite direction — higher exposure, more adverse events. Among the three AGAVE-201 regimens, 0.3 mg/kg every 2 weeks had the highest predicted probability of response and the lowest predicted probability across all 10 exposure-associated safety endpoints.
cards.watchOut: A modelling analysis of patients already carded above — it explains the dose inversion and justifies the marketed low dose, but it is not independent efficacy evidence.
cards.source: Exposure-Response Relationships for Axatilimab in Patients with Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease. Clin Pharmacol Ther. 2025. PMID: 40536163. Registry ID: none in the record. shelves.title: Fedratinib in myelofibrosis: spleen responses of 47% vs 1% before ruxolitinib and 36% vs 6% after it — with a thiamine/Wernicke warning that is part of the treatment
shelves.question: In adults with intermediate-2/high-risk myelofibrosis, JAK-inhibitor-naïve or previously treated with ruxolitinib, does fedratinib 400 mg daily, versus placebo or best available therapy, shrink spleen volume and improve symptoms?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — strong randomised spleen and symptom effects in two distinct populations, but from one drug programme, which caps the stamp. In JAK-inhibitor-naive patients (JAKARTA, placebo-controlled), fedratinib 400 mg daily produced a spleen volume response in 47% vs 1% on placebo and a symptom response in 40% vs 9% at week 24. After ruxolitinib failure, FREEDOM2 (201 patients, randomised against best available therapy) found spleen volume reduction of at least 35% in 36% vs 6%. The smaller FREEDOM study (38 enrolled, cut short by COVID-19) showed the same direction with protocol gastrointestinal mitigation and thiamine supplementation, and a low-platelet analysis (platelets 50 to under 100) found spleen responses similar to higher-platelet patients (36% vs 49% in JAKARTA; 36% vs 28% in JAKARTA2). The defining harm line is mandatory: fedratinib carries a boxed warning for Wernicke encephalopathy — thiamine must be checked and supplemented; no case occurred at the 400 mg dose in JAKARTA's updated analysis or in FREEDOM, but gastrointestinal adverse events (diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting), anaemia and thrombocytopenia are common, and grade 3 or worse treatment-related events occurred in 40% vs 12% in FREEDOM2's first six cycles.

cards.headline: JAKARTA updated analysis 2021: fedratinib 400 mg gave a 47% spleen volume response vs 1% on placebo, and 40% symptom response vs 9%, in JAK-inhibitor-naive myelofibrosis
cards.summary: JAKARTA updated analysis 2021: fedratinib 400 mg gave a 47% spleen volume response vs 1% on placebo, and 40% symptom response vs 9%, in JAK-inhibitor-naive myelofibrosis
cards.people: Patients with intermediate-2 or high-risk myelofibrosis who had not received a JAK inhibitor, in the phase 3 placebo-controlled JAKARTA trial; the updated analysis underpinned approval of the 400 mg daily dose. The record's abstract does not restate the total randomised N — printed as such (N not documented in the record's abstract).
cards.result: At week 24, spleen volume response rate was 47% and symptom response rate 40% with fedratinib 400 mg, versus 1% and 9% respectively with placebo. Common adverse events were diarrhoea, nausea, anaemia and vomiting. No Wernicke encephalopathy occurred in patients receiving fedratinib 400 mg/day.
cards.watchOut: An updated analysis rather than the primary report, with the abstract not restating N; spleen and symptom responses are the regulatory endpoints — no survival benefit is claimed or shown.
cards.source: Updated results of the placebo-controlled, phase III JAKARTA trial of fedratinib in patients with intermediate-2 or high-risk myelofibrosis. Br J Haematol. 2021. PMID: 34331348. cards.headline: FREEDOM2 2024: after ruxolitinib failure, fedratinib beat best available therapy on spleen response, 36% vs 6% (201 patients randomised)
cards.summary: FREEDOM2 2024: after ruxolitinib failure, fedratinib beat best available therapy on spleen response, 36% vs 6% (201 patients randomised)
cards.type: Phase 3 open-label randomised controlled trial vs best available therapy
cards.people: 201 adults with intermediate-2 or high-risk myelofibrosis relapsed, refractory or intolerant to ruxolitinib, randomised 2:1 at 86 clinics in 16 countries to fedratinib 400 mg daily (134 patients) or best available therapy (67, including 52 receiving ruxolitinib); 46 best-available-therapy patients later crossed over to fedratinib. All received prophylactic antiemetics and thiamine supplementation.
cards.result: Spleen volume reduction of at least 35% at the end of cycle 6 occurred in 48 of 134 (36%) on fedratinib vs 4 of 67 (6%) on best available therapy (difference 30 percentage points, 95% CI 20 to 39). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in the first six cycles occurred in 40% vs 12%, most frequently anaemia (9% vs 9%) and thrombocytopenia (12% vs 3%); one fedratinib patient died of acute kidney injury suspected to be drug-related. Gastrointestinal events were more frequent with fedratinib.
cards.watchOut: Open-label, and the comparator arm was mostly ruxolitinib rechallenge in patients already failing ruxolitinib — a soft comparator that flatters the spleen-response gap; crossover further limits any survival reading.
cards.source: Efficacy and safety of fedratinib in patients with myelofibrosis previously treated with ruxolitinib (FREEDOM2): results from a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial. Lancet Haematol. 2024. PMID: 39265613. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03952039. phase 3 open-label randomised controlled trial vs best available therapy 201 adults with intermediate-2 or high-risk myelofibrosis relapsed, refractory or intolerant to ruxolitinib, randomised 2:1 at 86 clinics in 16 countries to fedratinib 400 mg daily (134 patients) or best available therapy (67, including 52 receiving ruxolitinib); 46 best-available-therapy patients later crossed over to fedratinib. all received prophylactic antiemetics and thiamine supplementation. spleen volume reduction of at least 35% at the end of cycle 6 occurred in 48 of 134 (36%) on fedratinib vs 4 of 67 (6%) on best available therapy (difference 30 percentage points, 95% ci 20 to 39). grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in the first six cycles occurred in 40% vs 12%, most frequently anaemia (9% vs 9%) and thrombocytopenia (12% vs 3%); one fedratinib patient died of acute kidney injury suspected to be drug-related. gastrointestinal events were more frequent with fedratinib. open-label, and the comparator arm was mostly ruxolitinib rechallenge in patients already failing ruxolitinib — a soft comparator that flatters the spleen-response gap; crossover further limits any survival reading. efficacy and safety of fedratinib in patients with myelofibrosis previously treated with ruxolitinib (freedom2): results from a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial. lancet haematol. 2024. pmid: 39265613. registry id: clinicaltrials.gov nct03952039. mesh: humans · primary myelofibrosis/drug therapy · pyrimidines/therapeutic use,adverse effects · nitriles/therapeutic use · pyrazoles/therapeutic use,adverse effects · male · female · aged · middle aged · pyrrolidines/therapeutic use,adverse effects · sulfonamides/therapeutic use,adverse effects · treatment outcome · aged, 80 and over · adult · benzenesulfonamides

cards.headline: FREEDOM 2024: in 35 evaluable post-ruxolitinib patients, 25.7% hit the cycle-6 spleen endpoint and 62.9% achieved it at some point, with gastrointestinal mitigation and no encephalopathy
cards.summary: FREEDOM 2024: in 35 evaluable post-ruxolitinib patients, 25.7% hit the cycle-6 spleen endpoint and 62.9% achieved it at some point, with gastrointestinal mitigation and no encephalopathy
cards.type: Phase 3b single-arm trial (accrual truncated by COVID-19)
cards.people: 38 patients enrolled (accrual cut short by COVID-19) with intermediate- or high-risk myelofibrosis and platelets at least 50, previously treated with ruxolitinib; the protocol mandated gastrointestinal adverse-event mitigation, thiamine supplementation and encephalopathy surveillance. Efficacy-evaluable population 35 patients.
cards.result: Nine of 35 patients (25.7%, 95% CI 12.5 to 43.3) achieved at least 35% spleen volume reduction at the end of cycle 6, and 22 (62.9%) achieved it as best response up to end of treatment; 16 of 36 (44.4%) had at least a 50% reduction in total symptom score at cycle 6. Gastrointestinal adverse-event rates were lower than in the earlier JAKARTA2 trial, and no patient developed encephalopathy.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm and truncated at 38 patients: its real contribution is the mitigation lesson (antiemetics, thiamine, surveillance), not a precise efficacy estimate.
cards.source: Safety and efficacy of fedratinib in patients with myelofibrosis previously treated with ruxolitinib: primary analysis of FREEDOM trial. Leuk Lymphoma. 2024. PMID: 38838026. cards.headline: Low-platelet analysis 2022: fedratinib worked as well at platelet counts of 50 to under 100 as at higher counts (spleen response 36% in both low-platelet cohorts)
cards.summary: Low-platelet analysis 2022: fedratinib worked as well at platelet counts of 50 to under 100 as at higher counts (spleen response 36% in both low-platelet cohorts)
cards.type: Subgroup analysis of a phase 3 trial and a phase 2 single-arm trial
cards.people: Patients with baseline platelets 50 to under 100 (14 of 96 in JAKARTA; 33 of 97 in the single-arm post-ruxolitinib JAKARTA2) compared with patients at 100 or above, all receiving fedratinib 400 mg daily.
cards.result: At 24 weeks, spleen response rates in the low-platelet vs high-platelet cohorts were 36% vs 49% in JAKARTA (P=0.37) and 36% vs 28% in JAKARTA2 (P=0.41) — not significantly different; symptom responses likewise did not differ significantly. New or worsening thrombocytopenia was more frequent in the low-platelet cohort (44% vs 9%) but no serious thrombocytopenia events occurred, and only 3 of 48 low-platelet patients discontinued for thrombocytopenia.
cards.watchOut: Subgroup sizes are small (14 and 33 low-platelet patients) — 'not significantly different' is not proof of equivalence, and approval remains bounded at platelets of 50 or above.
cards.source: Safety and efficacy of fedratinib, a selective oral inhibitor of Janus kinase-2 (JAK2), in patients with myelofibrosis and low pretreatment platelet counts. Br J Haematol. 2022. PMID: 35476316. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: fedratinib shrinks spleens and eases symptoms before and after ruxolitinib — POSSIBLE (one programme), with the Wernicke/thiamine warning on the face
cards.summary: Synthesis: fedratinib shrinks spleens and eases symptoms before and after ruxolitinib — POSSIBLE (one programme), with the Wernicke/thiamine warning on the face
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: one placebo-controlled phase 3 trial, one randomised trial against best available therapy (201 patients), one truncated single-arm study (38 enrolled) and a low-platelet subgroup analysis.
cards.result: Two randomised trials in two populations agree on a large spleen-response advantage (47% vs 1% naive; 36% vs 6% post-ruxolitinib) with symptom benefit. One programme caps the stamp at POSSIBLE. The harm discipline is part of the intervention: check thiamine and supplement it, premedicate for gastrointestinal effects, and watch platelets — the boxed warning for Wernicke encephalopathy exists because cases occurred in the wider programme's history, even though none occurred at 400 mg in the carded analyses.
cards.watchOut: Spleen volume and symptom scores are the proven benefits; no card here shows a survival or leukaemia-transformation benefit, and none should be implied.
cards.source: Synthesis of the carded records above (PMIDs 34331348, 39265613, 38838026, 35476316). Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH: not captured from the record this session

shelves.title: Ponatinib in resistant chronic-phase CML: deep responses including T315I, with response-based dose reduction cutting serious arterial events from 18% to 4%
shelves.question: In patients with chronic-phase CML resistant or intolerant to ≥2 tyrosine kinase inhibitors (or with T315I), does response-based dose-optimised ponatinib, versus fixed-dose ponatinib or historical expectations, produce molecular responses at an acceptable vascular cost?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Female · Humans · Imidazoles/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Leukemia, Myelogenous, Chronic, BCR-ABL Positive/drug therapy · Male · Middle Aged · Precursor Cell Lymphoblastic Leukemia-Lymphoma/drug therapy · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Pyridazines/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Thrombocytopenia/chemically induced · Thrombosis/chemically induced · Young Adult · Antineoplastic Agents/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Fusion Proteins, bcr-abl/genetics · Imidazoles/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Leukemia, Myeloid, Chronic-Phase/drug therapy,genetics · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Pyridazines/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Treatment Outcome · DNA Mutational Analysis · Follow-Up Studies · Imidazoles/administration & dosage · Leukemia, Myeloid, Chronic-Phase/drug therapy,genetics,pathology,mortality · Mutation · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/administration & dosage · Pyridazines/administration & dosage · Clinical Trials as Topic · Drug Resistance, Neoplasm/genetics · Imidazoles/adverse effects · Leukemia, Myelogenous, Chronic, BCR-ABL Positive/drug therapy,genetics · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/adverse effects · Pyridazines/adverse effects
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — one programme, two trials, and a dosing lesson bought with vascular harm. PACE (449 heavily pretreated patients with CML or Ph+ ALL, fixed 45 mg daily) produced major cytogenetic responses in 56% of chronic-phase patients — 70% in those with the T315I mutation — but arterial occlusive events emerged as the programme's defining toxicity. OPTIC prospectively tested response-based dosing (283 chronic-phase patients randomised to start at 45, 30 or 15 mg, dropping to 15 mg on reaching BCR::ABL1 at or below 1%): response at 12 months was 44.1%, 29.0% and 23.1% by starting dose, and the 45-to-15 mg strategy gave the best benefit-risk balance. Five-year OPTIC follow-up kept 5-year overall survival above 80% in every cohort, with exposure-adjusted arterial occlusive event rates of 4.1, 3.8 and 2.0 per 100 patient-years by starting dose. A pooled PACE/OPTIC comparison in post-second-generation-TKI patients quantified the trade: serious arterial occlusive events in 18% under PACE's fixed dosing vs 4% under OPTIC's response-based dosing, at similar or better responses. The frontline Ph+ ALL comparison (ponatinib vs imatinib, PhALLCON) is an adjacent slice, cross-pointed here and not carded into this resistance question. Single programme: POSSIBLE.

cards.headline: PACE 2013: ponatinib 45 mg produced major cytogenetic responses in 56% of chronic-phase CML patients (70% with T315I) — and arterial occlusive events emerged as its defining harm
cards.summary: PACE 2013: ponatinib 45 mg produced major cytogenetic responses in 56% of chronic-phase CML patients (70% with T315I) — and arterial occlusive events emerged as its defining harm
cards.people: 449 heavily pretreated patients with CML or Philadelphia chromosome-positive ALL who had resistance to or unacceptable side effects from dasatinib or nilotinib, or who had the BCR-ABL T315I mutation; ponatinib started at 45 mg once daily; median follow-up 15 months. Chronic-phase CML cohort: 267 patients.
cards.result: Among chronic-phase patients, 56% had a major cytogenetic response (51% of those resistant or intolerant to dasatinib or nilotinib; 70% of those with T315I), 46% a complete cytogenetic response and 34% a major molecular response; responses occurred regardless of baseline kinase-domain mutation status, and an estimated 91% of major cytogenetic responses were sustained at least 12 months. No single BCR-ABL mutation conferring resistance to ponatinib was detected. The full abstract details responses in accelerated-phase, blast-phase and Ph+ ALL cohorts as well; arterial occlusive and thrombotic events are recorded in the record's adverse-event findings and were quantified in the later programme analyses carded below.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm and fixed-dose: PACE proves ponatinib can rescue multi-resistant disease, including T315I, but its dosing is precisely what OPTIC had to fix — do not quote PACE efficacy without OPTIC's dosing beside it.
cards.source: Cortes JE et al. A phase 2 trial of ponatinib in Philadelphia chromosome-positive leukemias. N Engl J Med. 2013. PMID: 24180494. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: OPTIC primary analysis 2021: starting at 45 mg and dropping to 15 mg on response gave the highest 12-month response (44.1%) of the three dosing strategies
cards.summary: OPTIC primary analysis 2021: starting at 45 mg and dropping to 15 mg on response gave the highest 12-month response (44.1%) of the three dosing strategies
cards.people: 283 adults with chronic-phase CML resistant to or intolerant of at least two prior BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitors, or with T315I, randomised 1:1:1 to ponatinib starting doses of 45, 30 or 15 mg daily (282 treated, 94 per cohort), with reduction to 15 mg on reaching BCR::ABL1 at or below 1% in the 45 and 30 mg cohorts.
cards.result: The primary endpoint (BCR::ABL1 at or below 1% at 12 months) was achieved in 44.1% (98.3% CI 31.7 to 57.0) starting at 45 mg, 29.0% (18.4 to 41.6) at 30 mg and 23.1% (13.4 to 35.3) at 15 mg. Independently confirmed grade 3 or worse treatment-emergent arterial occlusive events occurred in 5, 5 and 3 patients respectively. The authors concluded the optimal benefit-risk came from the 45 mg starting dose reduced to 15 mg on response.
cards.watchOut: The comparison is between dosing strategies, not against another drug; event counts for arterial occlusion are small (5, 5, 3), so the safety gradient needs the exposure-adjusted long-term card below.

cards.headline: OPTIC 5-year follow-up 2026: survival above 80% in all cohorts at 5 years, with exposure-adjusted arterial occlusive event rates of 4.1, 3.8 and 2.0 per 100 patient-years by starting dose
cards.summary: OPTIC 5-year follow-up 2026: survival above 80% in all cohorts at 5 years, with exposure-adjusted arterial occlusive event rates of 4.1, 3.8 and 2.0 per 100 patient-years by starting dose
cards.type: Long-term follow-up of a randomised phase 2 trial
cards.people: The 283 OPTIC patients (94, 95 and 94 by starting-dose cohort), followed a median of 75-78 months; 61 patients remained on trial at data cutoff.
cards.result: By 5 years, BCR::ABL1 at or below 1% had been achieved by 60%, 41% and 40% of the 45, 30 and 15 mg cohorts; 5-year progression-free survival was 63%, 57% and 60%, and overall survival exceeded 80% in all cohorts. In T315I-positive patients, response, progression-free and overall survival rates were highest in the 45 mg cohort. Exposure-adjusted adjudicated arterial occlusive event rates were 4.1, 3.8 and 2.0 patients per 100 patient-years by cohort.
cards.watchOut: Survivor-heavy reading: only 61 of 283 patients remained on trial at cutoff, and per-100-patient-year rates, while the fairest comparison available, still show events accumulating with exposure even at the lowest starting dose.

cards.headline: PACE/OPTIC pooled analysis 2022: in post-second-generation-TKI patients, serious arterial occlusive events were 18% under PACE fixed dosing vs 4% under OPTIC response-based dosing, with responses preserved
cards.summary: PACE/OPTIC pooled analysis 2022: in post-second-generation-TKI patients, serious arterial occlusive events were 18% under PACE fixed dosing vs 4% under OPTIC response-based dosing, with responses preserved
cards.type: Pooled cross-trial analysis of two single-programme trials (non-randomised comparison)
cards.people: Patients with chronic-phase CML previously treated with at least one second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor: 257 in PACE (fixed 45 mg) and 93 in the OPTIC 45 mg starting-dose cohort (response-based reduction to 15 mg).
cards.result: By 24 months, BCR::ABL1 at or below 1% was achieved by 46% in PACE and 57% in OPTIC; progression-free survival was 68% and 80%, and overall survival 85% and 91%. Serious treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 63% vs 34%, and serious treatment-emergent arterial occlusive events in 18% vs 4%.
cards.watchOut: Cross-trial, not randomised: PACE and OPTIC enrolled in different eras with different monitoring — the 18% vs 4% gap is consistent with the dose-dependence story and the propensity analysis carded in the programme's dose-modification report, but it is not a randomised estimate.

cards.headline: Synthesis: ponatinib rescues multi-resistant and T315I chronic-phase CML; response-based dosing (45 mg down to 15 mg) is how its vascular cost is contained — POSSIBLE, one programme
cards.summary: Synthesis: ponatinib rescues multi-resistant and T315I chronic-phase CML; response-based dosing (45 mg down to 15 mg) is how its vascular cost is contained — POSSIBLE, one programme
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: PACE (449 patients), OPTIC (283 randomised; 5-year follow-up) and a pooled PACE/OPTIC analysis.
cards.result: Efficacy is not in doubt within this programme — responses where no other tyrosine kinase inhibitor works, including T315I, with 5-year survival above 80% in OPTIC. The shelf's real answer is the dosing: start 45 mg, drop to 15 mg at BCR::ABL1 at or below 1%, and accept a residual arterial occlusive risk that falls, but does not vanish, with lower exposure. The frontline Ph+ ALL question (ponatinib vs imatinib) is a separate slice and is cross-pointed, not carded here. Single programme caps the stamp at POSSIBLE.
cards.watchOut: Cardiovascular risk assessment and monitoring are part of prescribing ponatinib; patients with prior arterial events were the population in whom PACE's harm concentrated.

shelves.title: Midostaurin plus chemotherapy in newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML: RATIFY showed a survival benefit (hazard ratio 0.78) — one randomised trial, consistently supported
shelves.question: In younger adults with newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML, does adding midostaurin to intensive induction/consolidation (and as maintenance), versus chemotherapy alone, improve overall survival?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Cytarabine/administration & dosage · Daunorubicin/administration & dosage · Female · Humans · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Leukemia, Myeloid, Acute/drug therapy,genetics,mortality · Male · Middle Aged · Mutation · Protein Kinase Inhibitors/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Staurosporine/administration & dosage,adverse effects,analogs & derivatives · Young Adult · fms-Like Tyrosine Kinase 3/genetics · Aged · Daunorubicin/adverse effects · Idarubicin/adverse effects · Leukemia, Myeloid, Acute/drug therapy,genetics · Staurosporine/adverse effects,analogs & derivatives · Antibiotics, Antineoplastic/therapeutic use · Anthracyclines · fms-Like Tyrosine Kinase 3/genetics,therapeutic use · Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation/methods · Protein-Tyrosine Kinases · Aged, 80 and over · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Leukemia, Myeloid, Acute/genetics,drug therapy,mortality,therapy · Nucleophosmin · Registries · Remission Induction · Retrospective Studies · Staurosporine/analogs & derivatives,therapeutic use,administration & dosage,analogs & derivatives · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — the survival claim rests on one randomised trial (RATIFY), which caps the stamp, supported by a single-arm phase 3b, a historically controlled phase 2 and a large real-world registry analysis. RATIFY (717 patients aged 18-59 with newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML) found overall survival longer with midostaurin added to standard induction, consolidation and maintenance than with placebo (hazard ratio for death 0.78; event-free survival hazard ratio also 0.78), with benefit consistent across FLT3 subtypes and in the transplant-censored analysis — and, as the slate required on the face, the trial's advance was survival, reported without a remission-rate difference in its record. Two fences: the maintenance phase was not separately randomised, so no card here attributes the benefit to maintenance; and transplantation was allowed and common, so the estimate is for a midostaurin-containing strategy, not for the drug in isolation. The phase 3b study (301 patients, including patients over 60) reported complete remission or remission with incomplete recovery in 80.7% with a similar adverse-event pattern across age groups; the AMLSG phase 2 (440 patients) beat its historical controls (event-free survival hazard ratio 0.55). The real-world PETHRATIFY analysis (1,658 registry patients) found median survival 47.2 vs 19.3 months favouring midostaurin, attenuated in propensity-matched pairs (overall survival hazard ratio 0.77, P=0.06 — not significant), and is labelled observational.

cards.headline: RATIFY 2017: adding midostaurin to chemotherapy prolonged overall survival in FLT3-mutated AML (hazard ratio for death 0.78) in 717 randomised patients
cards.summary: RATIFY 2017: adding midostaurin to chemotherapy prolonged overall survival in FLT3-mutated AML (hazard ratio for death 0.78) in 717 randomised patients
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (RATIFY / CALGB 10603)
cards.people: 717 patients aged 18 to 59 years with newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML (of 3,277 screened), randomised to standard chemotherapy (daunorubicin and cytarabine induction, high-dose cytarabine consolidation) plus midostaurin (360 patients) or placebo (357); patients in remission entered a maintenance phase on the same assignment, and allogeneic transplantation was allowed. FLT3 subtypes: ITD-high 214, ITD-low 341, TKD 162.
cards.result: Overall survival was significantly longer with midostaurin (hazard ratio for death 0.78, one-sided P=0.009), as was event-free survival (hazard ratio 0.78, one-sided P=0.002). The benefit was consistent across all FLT3 subtypes and in the analysis censoring patients at transplantation. The rate of severe adverse events was similar between groups. The record reports the survival benefit without a remission-rate difference — both facts belong on the face.
cards.watchOut: One-sided P values as reported; the maintenance phase was not separately randomised, so the trial cannot say how much of the benefit maintenance contributed; transplantation was allowed, making this a strategy trial.
cards.source: Stone RM et al. Midostaurin plus Chemotherapy for Acute Myeloid Leukemia with a FLT3 Mutation. N Engl J Med. 2017. PMID: 28644114. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00651261,NCT00651261. cards.headline: Phase 3b 2023: midostaurin with chemotherapy in 301 young and older adults gave complete remission or incomplete-recovery remission in 80.7%, with no new safety pattern by age
cards.summary: Phase 3b 2023: midostaurin with chemotherapy in 301 young and older adults gave complete remission or incomplete-recovery remission in 80.7%, with no new safety pattern by age
cards.people: 301 patients with newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML (median age 59; 47.2% over 60 years; 82.7% FLT3-ITD) in an open-label multicentre phase 3b trial of midostaurin plus chemotherapy in induction, consolidation and maintenance, with 21-day (vs RATIFY's 14-day) midostaurin courses and anthracycline substitution allowed.
cards.result: Complete remission including incomplete haematologic recovery was 80.7% (95% CI 75.7 to 85.0), comparable across age groups (83.5% at 60 or younger, 82.5% at over 60 to 70, 64.1% over 70). At least one adverse event occurred in 98.0% and grade 3 or worse events in 84.4%; grade 3 or worse event frequency was higher in older patients, with no overall frequency difference between age groups.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm: the 80.7% remission figure has no comparator and the older-patient extension rests on this design, not on a second randomised trial.

cards.headline: AMLSG 16-10 phase 2 2022: midostaurin with intensive chemotherapy, transplant and 1-year maintenance beat historical controls (event-free survival hazard ratio 0.55) in 440 FLT3-ITD patients
cards.summary: AMLSG 16-10 phase 2 2022: midostaurin with intensive chemotherapy, transplant and 1-year maintenance beat historical controls (event-free survival hazard ratio 0.55) in 440 FLT3-ITD patients
cards.type: Phase 2 single-arm trial with historical-control comparison
cards.people: 440 adults aged 18 to 70 with newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD-positive AML (312 aged 18-60, 128 aged 61-70) treated with midostaurin plus intensive chemotherapy followed by allogeneic transplantation and 1-year midostaurin maintenance, compared with a historical cohort of 415 patients from five prior AMLSG trials using double-robust propensity adjustment.
cards.result: Event-free survival favoured the midostaurin trial over the historical control (hazard ratio 0.55, P<0.001), in younger (0.59) and older (0.42) patients alike; overall survival also favoured it (hazard ratio 0.57 vs the AMLSG control; 0.71 vs the RATIFY placebo arm, P=0.005).
cards.watchOut: Historical controls flatter new treatments (era effects in supportive care and transplant practice); read this as consistency with RATIFY, not as an independent randomised confirmation.

cards.headline: PETHRATIFY 2026 (observational): in 1,658 registry patients, midostaurin was associated with median survival of 47.2 vs 19.3 months — attenuated and not significant for survival after propensity matching, labelled observational
cards.summary: PETHRATIFY 2026 (observational): in 1,658 registry patients, midostaurin was associated with median survival of 47.2 vs 19.3 months — attenuated and not significant for survival after propensity matching, labelled observational
cards.people: 1,658 adults aged 14 to 85 with newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML from 129 PETHEMA registry centres: 469 received intensive chemotherapy plus midostaurin and 1,189 intensive chemotherapy alone, compared retrospectively.
cards.result: Composite complete remission was 81.4% vs 71.7% (P<0.001) and day-30 mortality 2.1% vs 7.1% (P<0.001). Median overall survival was 47.2 vs 19.3 months (hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.76), sustained after multivariable adjustment (0.73, P=0.017); in 261 propensity-matched pairs the survival effect attenuated to a non-significant trend (hazard ratio 0.77, P=0.06) while event-free survival remained significant (0.77, P=0.029). Transplantation in first remission was more frequent in the midostaurin cohort (48.9% vs 41.3%).
cards.watchOut: Era and selection effects are built in — midostaurin patients were treated later and transplanted more; the matched analysis losing significance for survival is the honest centre of this card.
cards.source: Real-World Outcomes of Midostaurin Plus Intensive Chemotherapy in FLT3-Mutated AML: The PETHRATIFY Study. Am J Hematol. 2026. PMID: 42671173. Registry ID: none in the record. shelves.title: CPX-351 beats 7+3 on survival in older secondary AML in one randomised trial with a durable 5-year benefit — but it has never been randomised against venetoclax-based therapy, which matched it retrospectively
shelves.question: In older adults with newly diagnosed therapy-related AML or AML with myelodysplasia-related changes, does CPX-351 (liposomal cytarabine–daunorubicin), versus conventional 7+3 cytarabine–daunorubicin, improve overall survival and remission?

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — a single randomised phase 3 programme supports CPX-351 (Vyxeos, Jazz Pharmaceuticals — the fixed 5:1 molar-ratio liposomal cytarabine–daunorubicin product, named under the clarification exception because the ratio formulation is the intervention, not generic 7+3) over conventional 7+3 in older adults with therapy-related AML or AML with myelodysplasia-related changes: median survival 9.56 vs 5.95 months (hazard ratio 0.69, relative), remission 47.7% vs 33.3%, and the advantage persisted at 5 years (survival 18% vs 8%). Real-world registry data (283 patients, observational) show a similar 54% remission rate. What the evidence does not show: any randomised advantage over venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent — the one large retrospective comparison (600 patients) found similar remission and survival with more infections on CPX-351, despite CPX-351 patients being younger. Costs of the drug: prolonged cytopenias and slower neutrophil/platelet recovery than 7+3, in a population fit enough for intensive chemotherapy. Single-programme randomised evidence caps the stamp at POSSIBLE.

cards.headline: Phase 3 trial (309 patients, age 60–75): CPX-351 lengthened median survival to 9.56 vs 5.95 months and raised remission to 47.7% vs 33.3% against 7+3
cards.summary: Phase 3 trial (309 patients, age 60–75): CPX-351 lengthened median survival to 9.56 vs 5.95 months and raised remission to 47.7% vs 33.3% against 7+3
cards.people: 309 patients aged 60–75 with newly diagnosed high-risk or secondary AML (therapy-related AML or AML with myelodysplasia-related changes), randomised to CPX-351 (liposomal cytarabine–daunorubicin, Vyxeos, Jazz Pharmaceuticals) or conventional 7+3 cytarabine plus daunorubicin, with consolidation in both arms.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 9.56 months with CPX-351 vs 5.95 months with 7+3 (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.90) — a relative measure; the absolute median gain was about 3.6 months. Overall remission was 47.7% vs 33.3%. Early mortality was numerically lower with CPX-351 (day 30: 5.9% vs 10.6%; day 60: 13.7% vs 21.2%, neither significant). Non-haematologic adverse events were comparable, but neutrophil and platelet recovery took longer with CPX-351.
cards.watchOut: Open-label trial in a selected 60–75 age band fit for intensive chemotherapy; the survival advantage is real but the absolute medians remain under a year in both arms.

cards.headline: Real-world PETHEMA registry (283 patients, observational): remission 54%; outcomes looked better in patients treated from 2022 on, but the period effect was not independent on multivariable analysis
cards.summary: Real-world PETHEMA registry (283 patients, observational): remission 54%; outcomes looked better in patients treated from 2022 on, but the period effect was not independent on multivariable analysis
cards.people: 283 patients with secondary/high-risk AML treated with CPX-351 in the Spanish PETHEMA registry, split into an early period (before 2022, n=147) and a post-reimbursement period (from 2022, n=136). Observational — no randomised comparator.
cards.result: Complete remission/CR with incomplete recovery was 54% overall. Early death was lower in the later period (day 30: 5.1% vs 11.6%; day 60: 8.1% vs 17%) and more later-period patients reached transplant (33.8% vs 25.2%). Unadjusted 2-year survival was 40.3% vs 25.2%, but treatment period was NOT independently associated with survival after adjustment — only TP53 wild-type status and MRD negativity were.
cards.watchOut: Observational and period-confounded: patient selection differed between periods, so the apparent improvement over time cannot be credited to the drug or to a learning curve.

cards.headline: Retrospective comparison in 600 Mayo Clinic patients (observational): CPX-351 and venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent gave similar remission and survival, with more infections on CPX-351
cards.summary: Retrospective comparison in 600 Mayo Clinic patients (observational): CPX-351 and venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent gave similar remission and survival, with more infections on CPX-351
cards.people: 600 patients with newly diagnosed AML treated at Mayo Clinic with CPX-351 (n=112) or venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent (n=488); the CPX-351 group was younger (median 65 vs 73 years) and more often had secondary AML (68% vs 51%). Retrospective, not randomised.
cards.result: CR/CRi rates were comparable (55% vs 60%), including in AML with myelodysplasia-related changes (60% vs 63%). Overall survival censored for transplant was similar (median 10 vs 13 months). Infectious complications were more frequent with CPX-351 (83% vs 62%). Venetoclax-based therapy looked better in post-MDS AML; CPX-351 looked better in SF3B1-mutated disease — subgroup findings from a non-randomised comparison.
cards.watchOut: Strong confounding by indication: CPX-351 patients were younger and fitter yet did no better, and subgroup wins in a retrospective dataset are hypothesis-generating only.

cards.headline: Synthesis: one positive randomised trial with durable 5-year benefit, real-world remission rates in line, and no randomised proof it beats venetoclax-based therapy — POSSIBLE
cards.summary: Synthesis: one positive randomised trial with durable 5-year benefit, real-world remission rates in line, and no randomised proof it beats venetoclax-based therapy — POSSIBLE
cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: one phase 3 randomised trial (309 patients) with its 5-year follow-up, one registry analysis (283 patients) and one retrospective comparison (600 patients).
cards.result: Against 7+3, CPX-351's survival benefit is randomised and durable (hazard ratio ~0.70, relative; 5-year survival 18% vs 8%). Against the modern venetoclax-plus-hypomethylating-agent alternative there is only retrospective evidence, which shows parity with more infections on CPX-351. The stamp is POSSIBLE because the randomised base is a single trial programme and the comparative question that now matters most is unrandomised.
cards.watchOut: Prolonged cytopenias and slower count recovery with CPX-351 are part of the intervention's cost; patients unfit for intensive chemotherapy were not the trial population.

shelves.title: Oral azacitidine maintenance nearly doubled median survival after first AML remission in the QUAZAR trial — one strong trial, not yet replicated, and the oral drug is not interchangeable with injectable azacitidine
shelves.question: In adults with AML in first remission after intensive chemotherapy who are not proceeding to transplant, does oral azacitidine (CC-486) maintenance, versus placebo, prolong overall and relapse-free survival?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antimetabolites, Antineoplastic/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols/therapeutic use · Azacitidine/administration & dosage,adverse effects,therapeutic use · Double-Blind Method · Drug Administration Schedule · Female · Humans · Leukemia, Myeloid, Acute/drug therapy,mortality · Maintenance Chemotherapy/adverse effects · Male · Middle Aged · Nausea/chemically induced · Quality of Life · Remission Induction · Survival Analysis · Antimetabolites · Azacitidine/therapeutic use · Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation · Humans · Leukemia, Myeloid, Acute/therapy · Neoplasm, Residual/drug therapy · Prognosis · Recurrence · Remission Induction · Humans · Azacitidine/therapeutic use · Antimetabolites, Antineoplastic/therapeutic use · Neoplasm Recurrence, Local/drug therapy · Leukemia, Myeloid, Acute/drug therapy · Remission Induction · Chronic Disease · Antimetabolites/therapeutic use
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — oral azacitidine maintenance after first remission is supported by one large placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (QUAZAR AML-001, 472 patients): median overall survival 24.7 vs 14.8 months and relapse-free survival 10.2 vs 4.8 months, with benefit independent of baseline MRD status, a higher MRD conversion rate (37% vs 19%), and no evidence that maintenance compromised later salvage therapy. The stamp is capped at POSSIBLE because this is a single-programme evidence base — one trial and its analyses, per the standing single-programme precedent. Two identity points belong on the face: oral azacitidine (CC-486) is NOT bioequivalent to injectable azacitidine and must not be substituted for it, and the population was patients in first remission after intensive chemotherapy who were not proceeding to transplant. Main harms: gastrointestinal symptoms (mostly grade 1–2) and grade 3–4 neutropenia (41% vs 24%).

cards.headline: QUAZAR AML-001 phase 3 (472 patients): oral azacitidine maintenance lengthened median survival to 24.7 vs 14.8 months and relapse-free survival to 10.2 vs 4.8 months against placebo
cards.summary: QUAZAR AML-001 phase 3 (472 patients): oral azacitidine maintenance lengthened median survival to 24.7 vs 14.8 months and relapse-free survival to 10.2 vs 4.8 months against placebo
cards.people: 472 patients aged 55 or older with AML in first complete remission (with or without complete count recovery) after intensive chemotherapy who were not candidates for stem-cell transplant, randomised to oral azacitidine (CC-486) 300 mg daily for 14 days per 28-day cycle or placebo. Median age 68.
cards.result: Median overall survival was 24.7 months with oral azacitidine vs 14.8 months with placebo (P<0.001) — an absolute median gain of about 9.9 months. Median relapse-free survival was 10.2 vs 4.8 months (P<0.001). Grade 3–4 neutropenia occurred in 41% vs 24%; thrombocytopenia in 22% vs 21%. Most adverse events were grade 1–2 gastrointestinal; health-related quality of life was preserved.
cards.watchOut: Single trial programme (QUAZAR AML-001) — every other card on this shelf is an analysis of this same trial, so the evidence base is one randomised experiment, not several.

cards.headline: QUAZAR MRD analysis: the survival benefit held regardless of measurable residual disease at baseline, and oral azacitidine converted more MRD-positive patients to MRD-negative (37% vs 19%)
cards.summary: QUAZAR MRD analysis: the survival benefit held regardless of measurable residual disease at baseline, and oral azacitidine converted more MRD-positive patients to MRD-negative (37% vs 19%)
cards.type: Pre-specified biomarker analysis of the randomised phase 3 trial
cards.people: Patients in QUAZAR AML-001 with serial multiparameter flow-cytometry MRD assessments (MRD-positive defined as at least 0.1% leukaemic cells in bone marrow) at baseline and on day 1 of every 3 cycles.
cards.result: Baseline MRD status predicted survival and relapse-free survival, but multivariable analyses showed oral azacitidine improved both outcomes independently of baseline MRD status. Oral azacitidine extended the duration of MRD negativity by 6 months versus placebo and produced a higher MRD-positive-to-negative conversion rate (37% vs 19%). Among oral-azacitidine MRD responders, 24% achieved MRD negativity more than 6 months after starting treatment.
cards.watchOut: MRD was assessed in the subset with serial samples; conversion analyses are supportive mechanistic evidence, not a second trial.

cards.headline: QUAZAR subsequent-therapy analysis: maintenance did not compromise salvage — survival after relapse therapy was at least as good in the oral azacitidine arm
cards.summary: QUAZAR subsequent-therapy analysis: maintenance did not compromise salvage — survival after relapse therapy was at least as good in the oral azacitidine arm
cards.type: Post hoc analysis of the randomised phase 3 trial
cards.people: QUAZAR AML-001 patients who received first subsequent AML therapy after discontinuing study treatment (134 of 238 in the oral azacitidine arm; 173 of 234 in the placebo arm); 48 patients went on to transplant.
cards.result: Overall survival from randomisation in patients who received subsequent therapy was 17.8 months (prior oral azacitidine) vs 12.9 months (prior placebo), hazard ratio 0.82 (95% CI 0.64 to 1.04, relative) — not significant; survival measured from the start of subsequent therapy was similar between arms. Among patients whose first subsequent therapy was an injectable hypomethylating agent, median survival was 8.2 vs 4.9 months (hazard ratio 0.66, 95% CI 0.41 to 1.06). The oral-azacitidine survival benefit persisted after censoring patients who proceeded to transplant.
cards.watchOut: Post hoc and non-randomised at the salvage step: who received which subsequent therapy was chosen by treating physicians, so these comparisons are descriptive.

shelves.balance: POSSIBLE — and the claim must be stated exactly: this programme's pivotal evidence is a pharmacokinetic-equivalence design, not an outcomes trial. In ASCERTAIN (phase 3 randomised crossover, 133 treated patients with MDS/CMML), oral decitabine 35 mg plus cedazuridine 100 mg (Inqovi) delivered 98.93% of the 5-day decitabine AUC of intravenous decitabine, meeting the equivalence endpoint, with a similar safety profile; the phase 2 crossover study (80 patients) found the same (AUC ratio 93.5–97.6%, demethylation within 1%). Clinical-outcome data — response rates of 60–76% and a 35.7-month median survival in the small CMML subset — are secondary and uncontrolled, because after the crossover cycles every patient received the oral drug. The face of this shelf claims equivalent exposure with oral convenience, and nothing more.

cards.headline: ASCERTAIN phase 3 crossover (133 treated): oral decitabine–cedazuridine delivered 98.93% of the 5-day decitabine exposure of intravenous decitabine — the prespecified equivalence endpoint was met
cards.summary: ASCERTAIN phase 3 crossover (133 treated): oral decitabine–cedazuridine delivered 98.93% of the 5-day decitabine exposure of intravenous decitabine — the prespecified equivalence endpoint was met
cards.people: 133 treated adults with MDS or CMML (an AML cohort was enrolled separately and is not reported in this paper) who were candidates for intravenous decitabine, randomised to oral decitabine 35 mg plus cedazuridine 100 mg or intravenous decitabine 20 mg/m² for cycle 1, crossing to the other formulation in cycle 2, then all receiving the oral drug from cycle 3.
cards.result: The primary endpoint was pharmacokinetic: total 5-day decitabine exposure (AUC) with the oral combination was 98.93% (90% CI 92.66 to 105.60) of intravenous exposure — equivalent exposure, by design. Safety profiles were similar; the most frequent grade 3-or-worse events were thrombocytopenia (61%), neutropenia (57%) and anaemia (50%). Serious adverse events in cycles 1–2 occurred in 31% on oral vs 18% on intravenous treatment; there were five treatment-related deaths (two oral, three intravenous). This trial was not designed or powered to compare clinical outcomes between formulations.
cards.watchOut: Equivalence of drug exposure is not evidence of superior — or even separately demonstrated — clinical outcomes; outcome data in this programme are secondary and come from patients who all ended up on the oral drug.

cards.headline: Phase 2 crossover study (80 patients): oral cedazuridine/decitabine matched intravenous exposure (AUC ratio 93.5–97.6%), demethylation differed by at most 1%, and 60% responded
cards.summary: Phase 2 crossover study (80 patients): oral cedazuridine/decitabine matched intravenous exposure (AUC ratio 93.5–97.6%), demethylation differed by at most 1%, and 60% responded
cards.people: 80 adults with intermediate-1, intermediate-2 or high-risk MDS or CMML, randomised to oral cedazuridine 100 mg/decitabine 35 mg or intravenous decitabine in cycle 1 with crossover in cycle 2, then oral treatment thereafter; an initial dose-confirmation stage used separate capsules before the fixed-dose tablet.
cards.result: Oral-to-intravenous ratios of 5-day decitabine AUC were 93.5% (dose-confirmation stage) and 97.6% (fixed-dose-combination stage). Mean LINE-1 DNA demethylation differed by 1% or less between formulations. Clinical responses occurred in 48 patients (60%), including 17 (21%) complete responses. Commonest grade 3-or-worse events: neutropenia 46%, thrombocytopenia 38%, febrile neutropenia 29%.
cards.watchOut: Response rates here are single-arm after crossover (everyone received the oral drug from cycle 3) — they describe the regimen, not a comparison with intravenous therapy.

cards.summary: CMML subpopulation analysis of the phase 2 and 3 studies (33 treated patients): overall response 76%, complete response 21%, median survival 35.7 months on the oral regimen
cards.type: Pooled subpopulation analysis of phase 2 and 3 studies
cards.people: 33 treated patients with CMML pooled from the phase 2 and phase 3 oral decitabine/cedazuridine studies; 76% had myelodysplastic-type CMML and most had intermediate-2 or high-risk disease by CMML-specific prognostic scores.
cards.result: Overall response rate was 76%, with complete responses in 7 patients (21%). Of 11 patients red-cell-transfusion dependent at baseline, 46% achieved transfusion independence for at least 12 weeks, which was associated with survival. Median overall survival was 35.7 months and median transformation-free survival 28.3 months. The safety profile matched that previously reported for decitabine.
cards.watchOut: Small (33 patients), pooled across two studies, and without a concurrent intravenous control — the survival figure describes a selected trial population on the oral regimen, not an advantage over intravenous decitabine.

cards.people: Synthesis of the cards above: the ASCERTAIN phase 3 crossover study (133 treated), the phase 2 crossover study (80 patients) and the pooled CMML analysis (33 patients).
cards.result: Two randomised crossover studies independently show the oral fixed-dose combination (Inqovi, decitabine 35 mg/cedazuridine 100 mg) reproduces intravenous decitabine exposure (98.93% and 93.5–97.6% of AUC) with near-identical demethylation and a similar safety profile. POSSIBLE reflects a well-verified pharmacokinetic-equivalence claim whose clinical-outcome limb rests on secondary, uncontrolled data.
