shelves.title: Blinatumomab added to consolidation in MRD-negative adult B-ALL (E1910, one trial): 3-year survival 85% vs 68% — with more neuropsychiatric events
shelves.question: In adults aged 30–70 with BCR::ABL1-negative B-cell precursor ALL in measurable-residual-disease-negative complete remission after induction and intensification chemotherapy, does adding four cycles of blinatumomab to consolidation chemotherapy, versus consolidation chemotherapy alone, prolong overall and relapse-free survival? (Single programme: the E1910 trial.)
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Antibodies, Bispecific · Antineoplastic Agents · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Consolidation Chemotherapy · Disease-Free Survival · Induction Chemotherapy · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Neoplasm, Residual · Precursor B-Cell Lymphoblastic Leukemia-Lymphoma · Recurrence · Remission Induction · Survival Analysis
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on a single programme — one trial (E1910), with an FDA approval summary and a small single-centre integration series as companions. In adults aged 30–70 with BCR::ABL1-negative B-cell precursor ALL already in MRD-negative complete remission after induction and intensification, adding four cycles of blinatumomab to consolidation chemotherapy improved survival: 3-year overall survival 85% versus 68% (hazard ratio for death 0.41 — a relative measure, printed with the absolute rates) and 3-year relapse-free survival 80% versus 64% (hazard ratio 0.53, relative), at a median follow-up of 43 months. Only 224 of 488 enrolled patients reached the MRD-negative randomisation — the benefit applies to that selected, deep-remission population, and the population boundary is the question: this shelf must not borrow the relapsed/refractory TOWER result (pack #7368) or the MRD-positive literature. The cost on the face: a higher incidence of neuropsychiatric events with blinatumomab. The FDA summary records the same trial (hazard ratio 0.42 in the FDA analysis population) and notes that one paediatric consolidation trial in the approval package (AALL1331) did not meet its primary objectives — context, not adult evidence.

cards.headline: E1910 phase 3 primary report (Litzow 2024): adding blinatumomab to consolidation in MRD-negative remission — 3-year overall survival 85% versus 68% (hazard ratio 0.41, relative) and relapse-free survival 80% versus 64%
cards.summary: E1910 phase 3 primary report (Litzow 2024): adding blinatumomab to consolidation in MRD-negative remission — 3-year overall survival 85% versus 68% (hazard ratio 0.41, relative) and relapse-free survival 80% versus 64%
cards.type: Phase 3 randomised trial (E1910, ECOG-ACRIN), blinatumomab + consolidation chemotherapy vs consolidation chemotherapy alone, MRD-negative B-cell precursor ALL
cards.people: Adults 30 to 70 years of age with BCR::ABL1-negative B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukaemia in MRD-negative complete remission (under 0.01% leukaemic cells on flow cytometry) after induction and intensification chemotherapy: of 488 enrolled patients, 395 (81%) achieved complete remission with or without full count recovery and 224 MRD-negative patients were randomised (112 per group) to four cycles of blinatumomab plus four cycles of consolidation chemotherapy or four cycles of consolidation chemotherapy alone.
cards.result: At a median follow-up of 43 months, overall survival at 3 years was 85% with blinatumomab versus 68% with chemotherapy alone (hazard ratio for death 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.73; P=0.002 — a relative measure, printed with the absolute rates), and 3-year relapse-free survival was 80% versus 64% (hazard ratio for relapse or death 0.53; 95% CI 0.32 to 0.87 — relative). A higher incidence of neuropsychiatric events was reported in the blinatumomab group than in the chemotherapy-only group. Results were reported after the data and safety monitoring committee reviewed the third efficacy interim analysis and recommended reporting.
cards.watchOut: Single-programme evidence, reported at an interim analysis on the monitoring committee's recommendation, and a selected population: only 224 of 488 enrolled patients (those reaching MRD-negative remission) were randomised, so the result governs intensification for patients already in deep remission — not initial therapy for all-comers.

cards.summary: FDA approval summary (Rabik 2025): approval of blinatumomab in consolidation rested on E1910 (overall-survival hazard ratio 0.42 in the FDA analysis population, relative) plus two paediatric trials — one of which, AALL1331, did not meet its primary objectives
cards.type: Regulatory approval summary (FDA) covering E1910 and the paediatric consolidation trials — context for the E1910 card, not independent adult evidence
cards.people: The FDA review (approval June 14, 2024) of blinatumomab in the consolidation phase for CD19-positive, Philadelphia chromosome-negative B-cell precursor ALL, covering three randomised trials: E1910 in adults with newly diagnosed disease without measurable residual disease, Study 20120215 in paediatric high-risk first relapse, and AALL1331 in paediatric and young-adult first relapse — a regulatory summary, not a new trial.
cards.result: For E1910, the FDA analysis showed a significant overall-survival improvement (hazard ratio 0.42; 95% CI 0.24 to 0.75; P=0.003 — a relative measure). Study 20120215's support was primarily descriptive (overall-survival hazard ratio 0.35; 95% CI 0.17 to 0.7, and post hoc relapse-free-survival hazard ratio 0.38; 95% CI 0.22 to 0.66 — relative measures). AALL1331 did not meet its primary objectives in either its high/intermediate-risk or its low-risk randomisation. A meta-analysis of overall survival across these studies and an infant study was consistent with a treatment effect of blinatumomab during consolidation, and the safety profile was consistent with previous studies.
cards.watchOut: A regulator's summary of the same E1910 data (its hazard ratio 0.42 differs slightly from the journal report's 0.41 because the analysis population differs) plus paediatric trials; the mixed paediatric record (AALL1331 negative on its primary objectives) belongs in context only and neither adds to nor subtracts from the adult randomised result carded above.
cards.source: Rabik CA et al. FDA Approval Summary: Blinatumomab for the Treatment of B-Cell Precursor Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia in the Consolidation Phase of Multiphase Chemotherapy. Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research. 2025. PMID: 40828516. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Single-centre integration series (Tinajero 2025): adding blinatumomab consolidation to the CALGB 10403 regimen was feasible — 31 adults, cytokine-release syndrome 9.7% and neurological/psychiatric events 19.4%, no permanent discontinuation for toxicity (uncontrolled)
cards.summary: Single-centre integration series (Tinajero 2025): adding blinatumomab consolidation to the CALGB 10403 regimen was feasible — 31 adults, cytokine-release syndrome 9.7% and neurological/psychiatric events 19.4%, no permanent discontinuation for toxicity (uncontrolled)
cards.type: Single-centre uncontrolled case series (n=31) of blinatumomab consolidation integrated into the CALGB 10403 regimen — feasibility evidence only
cards.people: 31 adults with B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukaemia in MRD-negative remission at a single centre (median age 31 years; 64.5% male; 83.9% Hispanic; Philadelphia-like subtype 45.2%), treated by institutional consensus with blinatumomab consolidation integrated into the paediatric-inspired CALGB 10403 regimen, with median follow-up of 13.7 months.
cards.result: Median overall survival was not reached; one death occurred after allogeneic transplant and one relapse (3.2%) occurred. All-grade cytokine-release syndrome occurred in 9.7% and treatment-related neurological/psychiatric adverse events in 19.4%; no patient permanently discontinued blinatumomab because of toxicity, and 84.6% of patients received over half of their planned pegaspargase doses. The authors concluded incorporation of blinatumomab consolidation into CALGB 10403 is safe and feasible.
cards.watchOut: Uncontrolled, single-centre, 31 patients with 13.7 months of median follow-up: it can speak to feasibility and toxicity of one integration schedule and to nothing about efficacy; the survival claim on this shelf rests entirely on E1910.
cards.source: Tinajero J et al. cards.headline: Synthesis: one randomised trial — in MRD-negative frontline remission, adding blinatumomab to consolidation improved 3-year survival from 68% to 85% (hazard ratio 0.41, relative), at the cost of more neuropsychiatric events; the companions add regulatory context and one small feasibility series, not further efficacy evidence
cards.summary: Synthesis: one randomised trial — in MRD-negative frontline remission, adding blinatumomab to consolidation improved 3-year survival from 68% to 85% (hazard ratio 0.41, relative), at the cost of more neuropsychiatric events; the companions add regulatory context and one small feasibility series, not further efficacy evidence
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (a single programme: the E1910 trial, the FDA approval summary covering it, and a 31-patient integration series). Blinatumomab in relapsed/refractory adult disease (TOWER) is pack #7368 — a different setting, not carded here.
cards.result: E1910 randomised 224 MRD-negative patients from 488 enrolled: 3-year overall survival 85% versus 68% (hazard ratio 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.73 — relative, with absolute rates alongside) and 3-year relapse-free survival 80% versus 64% (hazard ratio 0.53, relative). This is a treatment-intensification benefit in patients already in deep remission — framed as improved survival under the intensified strategy, in the population that reached MRD-negative remission. The FDA summary (hazard ratio 0.42 in its population) confirms the regulatory read and records the mixed paediatric consolidation record as context. The CALGB 10403 series (n=31) addresses only how to give the drug within a paediatric-inspired regimen.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Brexucabtagene autoleucel in relapsed/refractory adult B-ALL (ZUMA-3, single-arm): remission 71–73%, median survival 25.6 months at 3 years — uncontrolled, with grade 3+ CRS/neurotoxicity in ~25–31%
shelves.question: In adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukaemia with more than 5% marrow blasts, does a single infusion of the CD19 CAR T-cell therapy brexucabtagene autoleucel (1 x 10^6 CAR T cells/kg), versus no concurrent control, produce complete remissions and prolong survival, and with what cytokine-release and neurotoxicity cost? (Single-arm trial evidence plus one real-world cohort; no randomised comparator exists.)
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Female · Humans · Immunotherapy, Adoptive · Male · Middle Aged · Precursor B-Cell Lymphoblastic Leukemia-Lymphoma · Receptors, Chimeric Antigen · Recurrence · Survival Analysis · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — the ceiling for a single-arm base, with the uncontrolled base stated: no randomised comparator exists for brexucabtagene autoleucel (Tecartus, Kite/Gilead) in relapsed or refractory adult B-cell ALL. In the single-arm phase 2 ZUMA-3 trial, complete remission or remission with incomplete recovery occurred in 39 of 55 infused patients (71%; complete remission 56%), with median overall survival 18.2 months at the primary analysis; the 3-year analysis of the pooled treated population (N=78) found remission in 73% (complete remission 60%) and median overall survival 25.6 months (38.9 months in responders). A US real-world cohort (189 infused) found 151 complete remissions, 79% of them MRD-negative, and median progression-free survival 9.5 months — but 42% were treated in morphologic remission and would have been ZUMA-3-ineligible, so the trial and cohort populations differ and their rates are not pooled. The toxicity cost is substantial: grade 3-or-worse cytokine-release syndrome in 24% and grade 3-or-worse neurological events in 25% in the trial; grade 3–4 cytokine-release syndrome 11% and grade 3–4 neurotoxicity (ICANS) 31% in the real-world cohort. Brexucabtagene in mantle cell lymphoma (ZUMA-2) is homed at pack #7026 and obecabtagene in R/R B-ALL at pack #7027 — different questions/products, cross-pointed in prose only.

cards.headline: ZUMA-3 phase 2 primary report (Shah 2021): single-arm — complete remission or remission with incomplete recovery in 39 of 55 infused (71%), complete remission 56%, median overall survival 18.2 months; grade 3+ cytokine-release syndrome 24% and grade 3+ neurological events 25%
cards.summary: ZUMA-3 phase 2 primary report (Shah 2021): single-arm — complete remission or remission with incomplete recovery in 39 of 55 infused (71%), complete remission 56%, median overall survival 18.2 months; grade 3+ cytokine-release syndrome 24% and grade 3+ neurological events 25%
cards.type: Single-arm open-label phase 2 trial (ZUMA-3), brexucabtagene autoleucel (KTE-X19), relapsed/refractory adult B-cell ALL — no concurrent control
cards.people: Adults 18 or older with relapsed or refractory B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukaemia and more than 5% marrow blasts at 25 sites in the USA, Canada and Europe: 71 enrolled and leukapheresed, the product was manufactured for 65 (92%) and infused in 55 (77%) as a single infusion of 1 x 10^6 CAR T cells/kg after conditioning chemotherapy; median age of treated patients was 40 years. There was no concurrent control group.
cards.result: At median follow-up of 16.4 months, 39 of 55 patients (71%; 95% CI 57 to 82) had complete remission or complete remission with incomplete haematological recovery, and 31 (56%) reached complete remission. Median duration of remission was 12.8 months, median relapse-free survival 11.6 months, and median overall survival 18.2 months; among responders median overall survival was not reached, and 38 responders (97%) were MRD-negative. Ten patients (18%) received allogeneic transplant consolidation after infusion. The most common grade 3-or-worse adverse events were anaemia (49%) and pyrexia (36%); grade 3-or-worse infections occurred in 25%. Two grade 5 product-related events occurred (brain herniation and septic shock). Cytokine-release syndrome of grade 3 or worse occurred in 13 patients (24%) and neurological events of grade 3 or worse in 14 (25%).
cards.watchOut: Uncontrolled: every rate on this card is a within-arm proportion with no comparator, and 16 of 71 leukapheresed patients never received the product, so the infused population is selected. Survival figures cannot be compared directly with chemotherapy-era controls.
cards.source: Shah BD et al. KTE-X19 for relapsed or refractory adult B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia: phase 2 results of the single-arm, open-label, multicentre ZUMA-3 study. Lancet (London, England). 2021. PMID: 34097852. Registry ID: NCT02614066. cards.headline: ZUMA-3 three-year analysis (Shah 2025): pooled treated population N=78 — remission 73%, complete remission 60%, median overall survival 25.6 months (38.9 months in responders); no secondary T-cell malignancies reported
cards.summary: ZUMA-3 three-year analysis (Shah 2025): pooled treated population N=78 — remission 73%, complete remission 60%, median overall survival 25.6 months (38.9 months in responders); no secondary T-cell malignancies reported
cards.type: Three-year follow-up analysis of the ZUMA-3 trial (same programme as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: The pooled ZUMA-3 treated population (N=78, including the phase 1/2 treated patients) with median follow-up of 41.6 months as of July 23, 2022 — a longer-follow-up report of the same trial programme as the primary card, not a new trial.
cards.result: The overall complete remission / remission with incomplete recovery rate was 73% and the complete remission rate 60%. Median overall survival was 25.6 months overall and 38.9 months in responders (n=58), with 9 patients in ongoing remission without subsequent therapies. Five deaths (none deemed product-related) occurred since the prior data cut. Benefit was maintained regardless of age, prior therapies and subsequent allogeneic transplant, and subsequent transplant was not associated with a survival benefit among responders versus responders without it. No secondary T-cell malignancies were reported with long-term follow-up.
cards.watchOut: The denominator changed between reports (55 infused in the phase 2 primary analysis; 78 in the pooled treated population), which is why the median overall survival figures differ (18.2 vs 25.6 months) — the two reports are one programme at two maturities, not two estimates to average. Still uncontrolled.
cards.source: Shah BD et al. Three-year analysis of adult patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia treated with brexucabtagene autoleucel in ZUMA-3. Leukemia. 2025. PMID: 40108332. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: US real-world cohort (Roloff 2025): 189 infused as standard therapy — 151 complete remissions (79% of them MRD-negative), median progression-free survival 9.5 months; grade 3–4 cytokine-release syndrome 11% and grade 3–4 ICANS 31%; 42% were treated in remission and would have been ZUMA-3-ineligible
cards.summary: US real-world cohort (Roloff 2025): 189 infused as standard therapy — 151 complete remissions (79% of them MRD-negative), median progression-free survival 9.5 months; grade 3–4 cytokine-release syndrome 11% and grade 3–4 ICANS 31%; 42% were treated in remission and would have been ZUMA-3-ineligible
cards.type: Retrospective multicentre real-world cohort (n=189 infused), brexucabtagene autoleucel as standard therapy — observational, no comparator
cards.people: Adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell ALL treated with brexucabtagene autoleucel outside a clinical trial at 31 US centres (October 2021 to October 2023): 204 underwent apheresis and 189 were infused, with median follow-up of 11.4 months. Toxicities were graded by ASTCT criteria. Forty-two percent received the product in morphologic remission.
cards.result: After infusion, 151 patients achieved complete remission, of which 79% were MRD-negative remissions. Median progression-free survival was 9.5 months and median overall survival was not reached. Grade 3–4 cytokine-release syndrome occurred in 11% and grade 3–4 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) in 31%. In multivariable analysis, patients receiving consolidative haematopoietic cell transplantation after brexu-cel had superior progression-free survival compared with those receiving no consolidation or maintenance (hazard ratio 0.34; 95% CI 0.14 to 0.85 — a relative measure from observational data).
cards.watchOut: A different population from the trial — 42% were infused in morphologic remission, who would have been ineligible for ZUMA-3 (which required more than 5% marrow blasts) — so its remission and survival figures must not be pooled with the trial's. The transplant-consolidation hazard ratio is observational and confounded by selection for transplant.
cards.source: Roloff GW et al. Outcomes After Brexucabtagene Autoleucel Administered as a Standard Therapy for Adults With Relapsed/Refractory B-Cell ALL. Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology. 2025. PMID: 39418622. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: uncontrolled evidence throughout — ZUMA-3 remission rates of 71–73% with median survival of 18.2 months (primary, n=55) to 25.6 months (3-year pooled, N=78), a consistent real-world remission signal in a broader population, and grade 3+ cytokine-release/neurotoxicity in roughly a quarter to a third of patients

shelves.title: Nivolumab-AVD vs brentuximab vedotin-AVD in advanced classic Hodgkin lymphoma (S1826, one trial): 2-year PFS 92% vs 83%, with the largest gains and least harm in older patients
shelves.question: In patients aged 12 years and older with newly diagnosed stage III–IV classic Hodgkin lymphoma, does nivolumab plus doxorubicin–vinblastine–dacarbazine (N-AVD), versus brentuximab vedotin plus AVD (BV-AVD), prolong progression-free survival, and with what comparative toxicity — including in older patients and adolescents? (Single programme: the SWOG S1826 trial.)
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Child · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Young Adult · Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols · Brentuximab Vedotin · Dacarbazine · Doxorubicin · Hodgkin Disease · Intention to Treat Analysis · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Neoplasm Staging · Nivolumab · Progression-Free Survival · Vinblastine · Aged, 80 and over · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on a single programme — one trial (S1826), three reports. In patients 12 years and older with newly diagnosed stage III–IV classic Hodgkin lymphoma, nivolumab plus AVD beat brentuximab vedotin plus AVD — an active modern standard, not ABVD — on progression-free survival: 2-year progression-free survival 92% versus 83% (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.45 — a relative measure, printed with the absolute rates). The tolerability split carries as much weight as the efficacy split: brentuximab vedotin was associated with more treatment discontinuation, and in patients 60 and older (n=99) the differences were stark — 2-year progression-free survival 89% versus 64% (hazard ratio 0.24, relative), 2-year overall survival 96% versus 85% (hazard ratio 0.16, relative), non-relapse mortality 16% versus 6%, and six cycles delivered without dose reduction in 69% versus 26%. In adolescents (n=240), 3-year progression-free survival was 93% versus 82% (hazard ratio 0.37, relative), with grade 2-or-worse sensory neuropathy 7% versus 14% and thyroid dysfunction in 7% on nivolumab-AVD. Overall survival for the whole population was immature at the primary report — survival claims on this shelf are confined to the older-patient subset. Brentuximab vedotin plus AVD versus ABVD (ECHELON-1) is homed at pack #3444 and is not re-carded here.

cards.headline: S1826 phase 3 primary report (Herrera 2024): 2-year progression-free survival 92% with nivolumab-AVD versus 83% with brentuximab vedotin-AVD (hazard ratio 0.45, relative); only 7 patients received radiotherapy
cards.summary: S1826 phase 3 primary report (Herrera 2024): 2-year progression-free survival 92% with nivolumab-AVD versus 83% with brentuximab vedotin-AVD (hazard ratio 0.45, relative); only 7 patients received radiotherapy
cards.type: Phase 3 multicentre open-label randomised trial (SWOG S1826), nivolumab-AVD vs brentuximab vedotin-AVD, advanced-stage classic Hodgkin lymphoma
cards.people: 994 patients at least 12 years of age with newly diagnosed stage III or IV classic Hodgkin lymphoma, randomised to brentuximab vedotin with doxorubicin, vinblastine and dacarbazine (BV-AVD) or nivolumab with the same chemotherapy (N-AVD); 970 were included in the intention-to-treat efficacy population. Prespecified patients could receive radiation to residual metabolically active lesions.
cards.result: At the second planned interim analysis (median follow-up 12.1 months) the efficacy threshold was crossed: progression-free survival was significantly improved with N-AVD (hazard ratio for disease progression or death 0.48; 99% CI 0.27 to 0.87; P=0.001 — relative). With longer follow-up (median 2.1 years), 2-year progression-free survival was 92% (95% CI 89 to 94) with N-AVD versus 83% (95% CI 79 to 86) with BV-AVD (hazard ratio 0.45; 95% CI 0.30 to 0.65 — relative, printed with the absolute rates). Overall, 7 patients received radiation therapy. Immune-related adverse events were infrequent with nivolumab; brentuximab vedotin was associated with more treatment discontinuation.
cards.watchOut: Single-programme evidence (one trial), and the primary report's overall survival was immature — the proven whole-population benefit is progression-free survival against an already-effective comparator; do not import BV-AVD figures from ECHELON-1 (pack #3444), a different comparison.
cards.source: Herrera AF et al. Nivolumab+AVD in Advanced-Stage Classic Hodgkin's Lymphoma. The New England journal of medicine. 2024. PMID: 39413375. Registry ID: NCT03907488. cards.headline: S1826 older-patients subset (Rutherford 2025): age 60+ (n=99) — 2-year progression-free survival 89% versus 64% (hazard ratio 0.24, relative), overall survival 96% versus 85% (hazard ratio 0.16, relative), non-relapse mortality 6% versus 16%
cards.summary: S1826 older-patients subset (Rutherford 2025): age 60+ (n=99) — 2-year progression-free survival 89% versus 64% (hazard ratio 0.24, relative), overall survival 96% versus 85% (hazard ratio 0.16, relative), non-relapse mortality 6% versus 16%
cards.type: Older-patients (age 60+) subset analysis of the S1826 trial (same trial as the primary card — not independent evidence)
cards.people: 99 eligible patients aged 60 years or older (of 103 enrolled) within the S1826 trial (50 nivolumab-AVD, 49 brentuximab vedotin-AVD), randomised to six cycles of either regimen — a prespecified-age subset analysis of the trial carded above, not a separate trial.
cards.result: At median follow-up of 2.1 years, 2-year progression-free survival was 89% after N-AVD versus 64% after BV-AVD (hazard ratio 0.24; 95% CI 0.09 to 0.63 — relative) and 2-year overall survival was 96% versus 85% (hazard ratio 0.16; 95% CI 0.03 to 0.75 — relative). Six cycles were delivered without dose reduction in 69% on N-AVD versus 26% on BV-AVD; 55% discontinued brentuximab vedotin and 14% discontinued nivolumab. Non-relapse mortality was 16% with BV-AVD versus 6% with N-AVD. Despite more neutropenia with N-AVD, febrile neutropenia, sepsis, infections and peripheral neuropathy were all higher with BV-AVD, and patient-reported outcomes confirmed the improved toxicity profile of N-AVD.
cards.watchOut: A 99-patient subset: the hazard ratios are large but imprecise (overall-survival hazard ratio 0.16 with 95% CI 0.03 to 0.75), and this subset is the only place on the shelf where an overall-survival difference is reported — it must not be generalised to the whole trial population, whose survival data were immature.
cards.source: Rutherford SC et al. Nivolumab-AVD Versus Brentuximab Vedotin-AVD in Older Patients With Advanced-Stage Classic Hodgkin Lymphoma Enrolled on S1826. cards.headline: S1826 adolescent 3-year follow-up (Castellino 2026): ages 12–17 (n=240) — 3-year progression-free survival 93% versus 82% (hazard ratio 0.37, relative); grade 2+ sensory neuropathy 7% versus 14%; thyroid dysfunction 7% with nivolumab-AVD
cards.summary: S1826 adolescent 3-year follow-up (Castellino 2026): ages 12–17 (n=240) — 3-year progression-free survival 93% versus 82% (hazard ratio 0.37, relative); grade 2+ sensory neuropathy 7% versus 14%; thyroid dysfunction 7% with nivolumab-AVD
cards.type: Adolescent-cohort (ages 12–17) 3-year analysis of the S1826 trial (same trial as above — not independent evidence)
cards.people: 240 patients aged 12–17 years (24% of the 994 enrolled) within the S1826 trial, randomised to nivolumab-AVD or brentuximab vedotin-AVD for newly diagnosed advanced-stage classic Hodgkin lymphoma — an age-cohort analysis of the trial carded above, not a separate trial.
cards.result: Three-year progression-free survival was 93% (95% CI 87 to 96) in the N-AVD group versus 82% (95% CI 73 to 88) in the BV-AVD group (hazard ratio 0.37; 95% CI 0.17 to 0.80 — relative, printed with the absolute rates). One N-AVD and two BV-AVD patients received protocol-specified residual-site radiotherapy. Febrile neutropenia and sepsis rates were low in both groups; severe immune-related adverse events were infrequent, although thyroid dysfunction was seen in 7% with N-AVD. Sensory neuropathy of grade 2 or worse was more frequent with BV-AVD (14% vs 7%) by clinician report. Premature discontinuation was reported in 12 N-AVD and 4 BV-AVD patients, with no progression-free-survival events noted in the N-AVD group among them, and patient-reported outcomes indicated less toxicity with N-AVD.
cards.watchOut: An age-cohort subset of the same trial at longer follow-up — supportive consistency in the youngest patients, not independent replication; the discontinuation pattern in adolescents (more premature discontinuation on N-AVD) runs opposite to the older subset and is printed as reported.

cards.headline: Synthesis: one trial, three reports — nivolumab-AVD beat brentuximab vedotin-AVD on progression-free survival in advanced classic Hodgkin lymphoma (2-year 92% vs 83%; hazard ratio 0.45, relative), with the widest gaps in older patients and a consistent tolerability advantage (less neuropathy, discontinuation and non-relapse mortality)
cards.summary: Synthesis: one trial, three reports — nivolumab-AVD beat brentuximab vedotin-AVD on progression-free survival in advanced classic Hodgkin lymphoma (2-year 92% vs 83%; hazard ratio 0.45, relative), with the widest gaps in older patients and a consistent tolerability advantage (less neuropathy, discontinuation and non-relapse mortality)
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (a single programme: the S1826 trial, its older-patient subset and its adolescent cohort). Brentuximab vedotin-AVD versus ABVD (ECHELON-1) is pack #3444 — not carded here.
cards.result: Whole population: 2-year progression-free survival 92% versus 83% (hazard ratio 0.45; 95% CI 0.30 to 0.65 — relative, with absolute rates alongside); radiotherapy was almost eliminated (7 patients). Older patients (n=99): progression-free survival 89% versus 64%, overall survival 96% versus 85%, non-relapse mortality 6% versus 16%, full-dose delivery 69% versus 26%. Adolescents (n=240): 3-year progression-free survival 93% versus 82% (hazard ratio 0.37, relative). Overall survival for the whole population was immature at the primary report, so the shelf's survival claim is confined to the older subset. The question answered is which AVD partner — nivolumab or brentuximab vedotin — and on this trial the answer favours nivolumab on both efficacy and tolerability.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Carotid IMT reference intervals by method and population: UK 97.5th percentile 0.60 mm at 35-39 rising to 0.81 mm at 60+; Chinese IMT rises 5.5-5.8 micrometres/year
shelves.question: In healthy adults, what is common carotid intima-media thickness — its mean, spread and age-, sex- and ethnicity-specific reference intervals / percentiles measured by B-mode ultrasound (manual, semiautomated and echotracking methods) — and how much do measurement method and population move the values that define 'increased' cIMT?
shelves.mesh: Carotid Intima-Media Thickness · Reference Values · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Adult · Aged · Risk Factors · Ultrasonography/methods · Vascular Stiffness/physiology · China · Peru
shelves.balance: Textbook framing: Boron & Boulpaep, vascular physiology / arterial wall mechanics — the framing is general, and this shelf rests chiefly on the primary normative imaging literature, and says so. Four primary datasets, carded PER METHOD and PER POPULATION as the measurement demands: echotracking in 24,871 pooled individuals (healthy sub-population 4,234) generating age- and sex-specific percentile equations; B-mode ultrasound in 1,448 Andean-Hispanic adults (healthy reference sample 472) with age- and sex-dependent 95th percentiles; semiautomated border detection in 137 strictly healthy UK adults, whose 97.5th-percentile common carotid limits rise from 0.60 mm at age 35-39 to 0.81 mm at age 60+ (bifurcation limits are higher, to 1.05 mm); and radiofrequency-signal ultrasound in 3,053 healthy Han Chinese adults, with IMT rising 5.5 micrometres/year in women and 5.8 in men. Near-wall vs far-wall and mean vs maximum IMT are different numbers, and ethnicity-specific intervals are content, not caveat. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED.

cards.headline: Echotracking reference intervals (Engelen 2013): pooled 24,871 individuals from 24 centres; percentile equations built in 4,234 healthy people — risk factors shift a person's Z-score independently of age and sex
cards.summary: Echotracking reference intervals (Engelen 2013): pooled 24,871 individuals from 24 centres; percentile equations built in 4,234 healthy people — risk factors shift a person's Z-score independently of age and sex
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (echotracking common carotid IMT reference intervals, pooled multicentre)
cards.people: Common carotid IMT data obtained by echotracking on 24,871 individuals (53% men; age range 15-101 years) from 24 research centres worldwide. Individuals without cardiovascular disease, cardiovascular risk factors or blood-pressure-, lipid- or glucose-lowering medication formed the healthy sub-population (n=4,234) used to establish sex-specific percentile equations across age; a broader no-CVD/no-treatment sub-population numbered 14,609.
cards.result: Age- and sex-specific percentiles of common carotid IMT were estimated in the healthy population, allowing an observed value to be expressed as a Z-score against the value predicted for a person of the same age and sex. In the no-CVD/no-treatment sub-population, IMT Z-scores were independently associated with systolic blood pressure (standardised beta 0.19 in men, 0.18 in women), smoking (0.25 and 0.11), diabetes (0.19 and 0.19), total-to-HDL cholesterol ratio (0.07 and 0.05) and body mass index (0.14 and 0.07). The fetched record does not print the percentile values in millimetres, and this card claims none.
cards.watchOut: Method-bound: echotracking values are the reference for that technique, not interchangeable with conventional B-mode measurements (cards below); the healthy percentile population (4,234) is a selected subset of the 24,871 pooled individuals.

cards.headline: Prevencion Study (Pastorius 2010): normative cIMT in 1,448 Andean-Hispanic adults — 95th-percentile values in the 472-person healthy reference sample were age- and sex-dependent
cards.summary: Prevencion Study (Pastorius 2010): normative cIMT in 1,448 Andean-Hispanic adults — 95th-percentile values in the 472-person healthy reference sample were age- and sex-dependent
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (population-based B-mode cIMT normative values, Andean-Hispanic)
cards.people: 1,448 adults enrolled in a population-based study in Peru (the Prevencion Study), with carotid IMT and plaque measured by high-resolution ultrasonography. A healthy reference sample (n=472) with no cardiovascular disease, normal weight and normal metabolic parameters was selected to establish normative values.
cards.result: In the reference sample, 95th-percentile cIMT values were both age- and gender-dependent (the fetched record does not print the millimetre cut-offs, and this card claims none). In the whole population, predictors of increasing cIMT were older age, impaired fasting glucose, diabetes, higher systolic blood pressure, higher LDL cholesterol, smoking and male sex; predictors of carotid plaque were older age, male sex, higher systolic and lower diastolic pressure and higher LDL cholesterol. HDL cholesterol and C-reactive protein were not associated with cIMT or plaque.
cards.watchOut: Ethnicity-specific by design: these are Andean-Hispanic reference values from Peru and should not be applied as universal limits; plaque and IMT are reported together in the source but are different measurements.
cards.source: Pastorius CA et al. Normative values and correlates of carotid artery intima-media thickness and carotid atherosclerosis in Andean-Hispanics: The Prevencion Study. cards.headline: UK semiautomated B-mode norms (Lim 2008): in 137 strictly healthy adults, 97.5th-percentile common carotid IMT rose from 0.60 mm (age 35-39) to 0.81 mm (age 60+); bifurcation limits were higher, to 1.05 mm
cards.summary: UK semiautomated B-mode norms (Lim 2008): in 137 strictly healthy adults, 97.5th-percentile common carotid IMT rose from 0.60 mm (age 35-39) to 0.81 mm (age 60+); bifurcation limits were higher, to 1.05 mm
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (semiautomated B-mode carotid IMT normal values, UK)
cards.people: 453 asymptomatic men and women aged 35 to 75 years without clinical atherosclerosis underwent B-mode carotid duplex ultrasound (Sonos 7500, Philips) with mean far-wall IMT measured by semiautomated edge-detection software (Q-lab 4, Philips). The healthy population (n=137) had no cardiovascular disease, diabetes or hypertension, body mass index below 30 kg/m2, serum cholesterol below 6 mmol/L (approx. 232 mg/dL) and no carotid plaque.
cards.result: IMT at the bifurcation was significantly higher than at the common carotid artery, and IMT at both sites increased significantly with age. The upper limits (97.5th percentile) of IMT at the common carotid artery for ages 35-39, 40-49, 50-59 and 60+ were 0.60, 0.64, 0.71 and 0.81 mm respectively, whereas at the bifurcation they were 0.83, 0.77, 0.85 and 1.05 mm respectively.
cards.watchOut: The strictly healthy denominator is small (137 of 453 screened) and the measurement is mean far-wall IMT by one semiautomated system; bifurcation values must never be read against common-carotid limits, and vice versa.
cards.source: Lim TK et al. Normal value of carotid intima-media thickness--a surrogate marker of atherosclerosis: quantitative assessment by B-mode carotid ultrasound. Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography. 2008. PMID: 17764896. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Nationwide Chinese RF-ultrasound references (Xing 2024): 3,053 healthy Han Chinese adults — carotid IMT rose 5.5 micrometres/year in women and 5.8 in men; women had thinner IMT but larger augmentation pressure and index
cards.summary: Nationwide Chinese RF-ultrasound references (Xing 2024): 3,053 healthy Han Chinese adults — carotid IMT rose 5.5 micrometres/year in women and 5.8 in men; women had thinner IMT but larger augmentation pressure and index
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (radiofrequency-ultrasound carotid IMT and stiffness reference values, nationwide Chinese)
cards.people: 3,053 healthy Han Chinese adults (1,922 women) aged 18-79 years enrolled at 28 tertiary centres across China (2021-2022); common carotid walls were tracked in real time by a radiofrequency-signal ultrasound system, which automatically reported IMT, diameter, compliance coefficient, beta stiffness, local pulse wave velocity, local systolic pressure, augmented pressure and augmentation index.
cards.result: All carotid parameters showed significantly age-related trajectories. Women had thinner IMT, smaller carotid diameter and larger augmented pressure and augmentation index than men; beta stiffness and local PWV were higher in men before the forties and higher in women after. The increase rate of carotid IMT was 5.5 micrometres/year in women and 5.8 micrometres/year in men, and diameter rose 0.03 mm/year in both sexes. Blood pressure, body mass index and triglyceride levels were the major clinical determinants after adjustment for age and sex. The fetched record does not print the age-band reference tables in millimetres, and this card claims none beyond the rates above.
cards.watchOut: A single-population (Han Chinese), single-technology (RF-signal) reference set: its stiffness and wave-reflection values belong to this carotid-local method and are not carotid-femoral PWV values (a different shelf).
cards.source: Xing C et al. Reference values of carotid intima-media thickness and arterial stiffness in Chinese adults based on ultrasound radio frequency signal: A nationwide, multicenter study. Chinese medical journal. 2024. PMID: 38958034. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: carotid IMT reference values are established per method and per population — age and sex move them in every dataset, and the segment measured (common carotid vs bifurcation) changes the limit by up to about 0.24 mm
cards.summary: Synthesis: carotid IMT reference values are established per method and per population — age and sex move them in every dataset, and the segment measured (common carotid vs bifurcation) changes the limit by up to about 0.24 mm
cards.people: Synthesis of the four primary datasets carded above.
cards.result: Framed by Boron & Boulpaep (vascular physiology / arterial wall mechanics; the framing is general, and this shelf rests chiefly on the primary normative imaging literature). Echotracking percentiles from 4,234 healthy people within a 24,871-person pool (Engelen 2013) express IMT as age- and sex-specific Z-scores; B-mode norms in 472 healthy Andean-Hispanics (Prevencion 2010) are age- and sex-dependent at the 95th percentile; semiautomated far-wall limits in 137 strictly healthy UK adults (Lim 2008) rise from 0.60 mm at 35-39 years to 0.81 mm at 60+ at the common carotid, with higher bifurcation limits (to 1.05 mm); and RF-ultrasound values in 3,053 healthy Han Chinese adults (Xing 2024) rise 5.5-5.8 micrometres/year. What counts as 'increased' cIMT is therefore a statement about method, segment, age, sex and population together — never a single universal cut-off.
cards.watchOut: Never pool values across the three ultrasound methods or across segments; where a dataset's record does not print millimetre tables, this shelf claims none.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Blood-pressure response to exercise: treadmill maxima plateau after the sixth decade; bicycle SBP/watt slope 0.52 (women) vs 0.41 (men) mmHg/watt; athlete ceilings 220/200 mmHg
shelves.question: In healthy adults, what is the blood-pressure response to maximal and submaximal exercise — peak systolic pressure percentiles and upper limits of normal by age, sex, exercise mode (treadmill vs bicycle) and workload (including workload-indexed systolic pressure, mmHg per MET or per watt) — and what counts as an exaggerated response?
shelves.mesh: Blood Pressure/physiology · Exercise Test · Exercise/physiology · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Adult · Reference Standards · Reference Values · Workload · Athletes · Hypertension/ethnology/physiopathology/diagnosis
shelves.balance: Textbook framing: Guyton & Hall, ch. 84 (sports physiology), and Boron & Boulpaep, exercise physiology — the framing is brief, and this shelf rests chiefly on the primary exercise-testing literature, and says so. Four datasets, carded PER MODE as the measurement demands (treadmill and bicycle values are not interchangeable): maximal treadmill testing in 2,917 apparently healthy US adults (FRIEND), where peak systolic pressure rises with age to the sixth decade then plateaus; submaximal treadmill norms in 2,544 multiethnic NHANES participants aged 12-49, with exaggerated responses defined at the 90th percentile; workload-indexed bicycle values in 3,839 healthy Swedes drawn from 12,976 tests (peak systolic 188 +/- 24 mmHg in women vs 202 +/- 22 in men, but workload-indexed slopes higher in women: 0.52 vs 0.41 mmHg/watt); and maximal bicycle values in 1,876 Olympic athletes (upper reference 220 mmHg systolic in men, 200 in women) — a separate athlete limb, never merged into general-population norms. Unindexed peak pressure rises with achieved workload, so the workload-indexed limb is core content. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED.

cards.headline: FRIEND registry (Sabbahi 2018): peak treadmill pressures in 2,917 apparently healthy US adults — peak systolic rose with age to the sixth decade then plateaued; peak diastolic trajectories differed by sex
cards.summary: FRIEND registry (Sabbahi 2018): peak treadmill pressures in 2,917 apparently healthy US adults — peak systolic rose with age to the sixth decade then plateaued; peak diastolic trajectories differed by sex
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (maximal treadmill exercise BP reference standards, FRIEND registry)
cards.people: 2,917 maximal (peak respiratory exchange ratio at least 1.00) treadmill cardiopulmonary exercise tests from apparently healthy men and women aged 20-79 years without cardiovascular disease, contributed by four US laboratories to the FRIEND registry (tests from 1986 to 2015); percentiles of maximal systolic and diastolic pressure were determined for each decade.
cards.result: Peak systolic pressure continued to increase with age in both men and women to the sixth decade, followed by a plateau between the sixth and seventh decades. The trajectory of peak diastolic pressure with age differed between the sexes: men showed an increase in peak systolic pressure until the fifth decade, plateauing by the seventh, whereas women showed a continued increase in peak diastolic pressure across each decade. The fetched record does not print the decade percentile tables in mmHg, and this card claims none.
cards.watchOut: Maximal treadmill values only: they cannot be applied to bicycle or submaximal tests (cards below), and peak pressure depends on the workload actually achieved.
cards.source: Sabbahi A et al. Peak Blood Pressure Responses During Maximum Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing: Reference Standards From FRIEND (Fitness Registry and the Importance of Exercise: A National Database). Hypertension (Dallas, Tex. : 1979). 2018. PMID: 29255072. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: NHANES submaximal norms (Maroco 2025): 2,544 multiethnic participants aged 12-49 — each 5 mmHg higher stage-1 exercise systolic pressure carried 15% higher relative odds of hypertension; exaggerated responses defined at the 90th percentile
cards.summary: NHANES submaximal norms (Maroco 2025): 2,544 multiethnic participants aged 12-49 — each 5 mmHg higher stage-1 exercise systolic pressure carried 15% higher relative odds of hypertension; exaggerated responses defined at the 90th percentile
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (submaximal treadmill exercise BP norms, multiethnic NHANES)
cards.people: 2,544 NHANES participants aged 12-49 years (women: 467 White, 324 Black, 439 Hispanic; men: 493 White, 351 Black, 470 Hispanic) who underwent treadmill exercise testing in NHANES cycles that included it; age-, sex- and race-specific percentiles of the submaximal blood-pressure response were estimated.
cards.result: Regardless of race, sex, workload and clinical/socioeconomic characteristics, a 5-mmHg increase in systolic pressure during stage 1 of exercise testing was associated with 15% higher relative odds of hypertension (adjusted odds ratio 1.15, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.21) and a 5-mmHg increase in diastolic pressure with 31% higher relative odds (adjusted odds ratio 1.31, 95% CI 1.22 to 1.40). Exaggerated systolic responses were defined as readings at or above the 90th percentile and by receiver-operating-characteristic-derived cut-offs; Black males had the highest proportion of exaggerated responses (44%, 95% CI 36 to 53%) under the ROC-derived definition.
cards.watchOut: Submaximal stage-1 values in a young-to-middle-aged sample (which includes adolescents from age 12): not maximal-exercise limits, and the hypertension associations are cross-sectional relative odds, not prospective risk.
cards.source: Marôco JL et al. Multiethnic norms for blood pressure response to submaximal exercise testing in young-to-middle adulthood and associations with hypertension: The NHANES dataset. Journal of human hypertension. 2025. PMID: 39988582. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Workload-indexed bicycle references (Hedman 2021): 3,839 healthy subjects from 12,976 tests — peak systolic 188 +/- 24 mmHg (women) vs 202 +/- 22 (men), but SBP/watt slope higher in women (0.52 vs 0.41 mmHg/watt)
cards.summary: Workload-indexed bicycle references (Hedman 2021): 3,839 healthy subjects from 12,976 tests — peak systolic 188 +/- 24 mmHg (women) vs 202 +/- 22 (men), but SBP/watt slope higher in women (0.52 vs 0.41 mmHg/watt)
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (workload-indexed bicycle exercise BP reference values and equations)
cards.people: 12,976 subjects aged 18-85 years who performed a bicycle ergometer test at one Swedish centre (2005-2016); after excluding prevalent cardiovascular disease, comorbidities, cardiac risk factors and medications, the final healthy sample was 3,839 subjects (1,620 women), with systolic pressure, heart rate and workload extracted at three or more time points per test.
cards.result: Women had lower mean peak systolic pressure than men (188 +/- 24 vs 202 +/- 22 mmHg; P<0.001) but markedly higher workload-indexed measures: SBP/watt-slope 0.52 +/- 0.21 versus 0.41 +/- 0.15 mmHg/watt (P<0.001) and peak SBP/watt-ratio 1.35 +/- 0.34 versus 0.90 +/- 0.21 mmHg/watt (P<0.001). Age- and sex-specific means, standard deviations and 90th and 95th percentiles were determined, and reference equations derived from sex, age, workload, resting systolic pressure and anthropometric variables. The authors suggest the higher workload-relative pressure in women may imply greater peripheral vascular resistance during exercise.
cards.watchOut: Bicycle ergometry at a single Swedish centre, retrospectively derived: the workload-indexed values answer a different question from raw peak pressure and must not be interchanged with treadmill maxima.
cards.source: Hedman K et al. Age- and gender-specific upper limits and reference equations for workload-indexed systolic blood pressure response during bicycle ergometry. European journal of preventive cardiology. 2021. PMID: 34647584. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Olympic athletes (Caselli 2016): 1,876 elite athletes — upper reference values at maximal bicycle exercise were 220 mmHg systolic in men and 200 in women (diastolic 85 and 80); 7.5% exceeded the 95th percentile
cards.summary: Olympic athletes (Caselli 2016): 1,876 elite athletes — upper reference values at maximal bicycle exercise were 220 mmHg systolic in men and 200 in women (diastolic 85 and 80); 7.5% exceeded the 95th percentile
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (maximal bicycle exercise BP upper normal values, elite athletes)
cards.people: 1,876 healthy, normotensive elite athletes (mean age 25 +/- 6 years; 64% men) who underwent comprehensive clinical evaluation including a maximal bicycle exercise test.
cards.result: At maximum exercise, systolic pressure rose by 69 +/- 18 mmHg (P<.001) while diastolic pressure changed minimally (+1 +/- 7 mmHg; P=.001). The upper reference values were 220 mmHg in male and 200 mmHg in female athletes for systolic pressure, and 85 mmHg in male and 80 mmHg in female athletes for diastolic pressure. A subgroup of 142 athletes (7.5%) showed a high blood-pressure response (above the 95th percentile), associated with endurance and mixed sport disciplines, body mass index and baseline systolic pressure, in the absence of target-organ disease or metabolic abnormalities.
cards.watchOut: Athlete limb only: elite athletes aged about 25 achieving very high workloads — these upper values (220/200 mmHg) must never be merged into or applied as general-population norms.
cards.source: Caselli S et al. Upper normal values of blood pressure response to exercise in Olympic athletes. American heart journal. 2016. PMID: 27297857. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: exercise blood-pressure norms exist per mode and per population — treadmill maxima plateau after the sixth decade, workload-indexed bicycle slopes are higher in women, and athlete ceilings (220/200 mmHg) sit above general-population values by design
cards.summary: Synthesis: exercise blood-pressure norms exist per mode and per population — treadmill maxima plateau after the sixth decade, workload-indexed bicycle slopes are higher in women, and athlete ceilings (220/200 mmHg) sit above general-population values by design
cards.people: Synthesis of the four primary datasets carded above.
cards.result: Framed by Guyton & Hall ch. 84 and Boron & Boulpaep (exercise physiology; framing brief — this shelf rests chiefly on the primary exercise-testing literature). Maximal treadmill percentiles in 2,917 healthy US adults (FRIEND 2018) rise to the sixth decade then plateau; submaximal treadmill percentiles in 2,544 multiethnic NHANES participants (2025) define exaggerated responses at the 90th percentile; workload-indexed bicycle references in 3,839 healthy Swedes (2021) show lower raw peak systolic pressure in women (188 vs 202 mmHg) but higher pressure per watt (slope 0.52 vs 0.41 mmHg/watt); and maximal bicycle ceilings in 1,876 Olympic athletes (2016) reach 220 mmHg (men) and 200 mmHg (women). An 'exaggerated' response is therefore only definable against the mode-, workload-, age-, sex- and population-matched reference — the neighbouring heart-rate and gas-exchange norm shelves are cross-points, not re-carded here.
cards.watchOut: Never apply one mode's limits to another mode's test, and never read an unindexed peak pressure without the workload achieved.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Central BP and augmentation-index references per device: indexes not equivalent across site or technique; Omani SphygmoCor mean AIx 13 +/- 11%, aortic PWV 6.7 +/- 1.6 m/s
shelves.question: In healthy adults, what are central (aortic) systolic pressure, central pulse pressure and augmentation index — their means, spreads and age-, sex- and height-specific reference values by applanation tonometry and oscillometric devices — how far does central pressure sit below brachial pressure (pressure amplification), and how do device and recording site move the values?
shelves.mesh: Blood Pressure · Pulse Wave Analysis/instrumentation · Reference Values · Adult · Aged · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Vascular Stiffness/physiology · Mexico
shelves.balance: Textbook framing: Boron & Boulpaep, arterial pulse / wave reflection, and Guyton & Hall, arterial system chapters (framing). Four primary datasets, carded PER DEVICE as the measurement demands — transfer-function-derived aortic pressures are device-specific and no device's central values are presented here as universal: carotid/radial tonometry plus brachial oscillometry profiles in 1,688 healthy subjects aged 2-84 (indexes were NOT equivalent across recording site or technique, so reference intervals were defined per site and technique); Mobil-O-Graph office references in 867 rigorously healthy adults (with a 5,632-person risk-factor comparison group); Arteriograph values in 1,009 Mexican adults, whose central pressures ran higher than previously reported populations, especially in women, older and obese subjects; and SphygmoCor values in just 120 healthy Omani Arabs (mean central augmentation index 13 +/- 11%; aortic PWV 6.7 +/- 1.6 m/s). Augmentation index is heart-rate-dependent and AIx and AIx@75 are stated separately as published. The stamp is graded down because every value is device-bound, one dataset is very small (N=120), and the healthy denominators are modest. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING. Cross-points: pack #6297 (pulse-pressure mechanism) and pack #7065 (carotid-femoral PWV) — neither gives central-pressure reference values, and neither is re-carded here.

cards.headline: Tonometry/oscillometry profiles (Zocalo 2021): 1,688 healthy subjects aged 2-84 — waveform indexes were NOT equivalent across carotid vs radial recording or tonometry vs oscillometry, so reference intervals were defined per site and technique
cards.summary: Tonometry/oscillometry profiles (Zocalo 2021): 1,688 healthy subjects aged 2-84 — waveform indexes were NOT equivalent across carotid vs radial recording or tonometry vs oscillometry, so reference intervals were defined per site and technique
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (central pressure waveform index profiles and reference intervals by technique/site)
cards.people: 3,619 subjects aged 3-90 years were included, of whom 1,688 were healthy (aged 2-84 years). Augmentation pressure, augmentation index (AIx), heart-rate-corrected AIx (AIx@75), forward (Pf) and backward (Pb) pressure components, reflection magnitude and reflection index were obtained by carotid and radial applanation tonometry and brachial oscillometry/plethysmography, and analysed by pulse wave analysis and wave separation analysis.
cards.result: Waveform-derived indexes were not equivalent: for a specific index there were systematic and proportional differences associated with the recording site (carotid vs radial) and the technique (tonometry vs oscillometry). Whether sex-, height- or age-specific reference intervals were needed depended on the index and the age considered. Reference intervals were defined for each index taking the site and technique differences into account, with equations for the age-related profiles enabling an individual's expected values to be determined. The fetched record does not print the numeric interval tables, and this card claims none.
cards.watchOut: The cohort spans childhood to old age (healthy n=1,688 aged 2-84): only the adult limb answers this shelf's question, and the central lesson is non-interchangeability — a carotid-tonometry AIx is not a radial-tonometry or oscillometric AIx.
cards.source: Zócalo Y et al. Central Pressure Waveform-Derived Indexes Obtained From Carotid and Radial Tonometry and Brachial Oscillometry in Healthy Subjects (2-84 Y): Age-, Height-, and Sex-Related Profiles and Analysis of Indexes Agreement. cards.headline: Mobil-O-Graph office references (Paiva 2020): central BP, PWV and AIx by age and sex in 867 adults free of all major risk factors, against 5,632 with at least one
cards.summary: Mobil-O-Graph office references (Paiva 2020): central BP, PWV and AIx by age and sex in 867 adults free of all major risk factors, against 5,632 with at least one
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (Mobil-O-Graph office central BP / PWV / AIx reference values)
cards.people: 867 apparently healthy individuals (mean age 46.0 +/- 15.5 years; 39% men) free of obesity, hypertension, active smoking, dyslipidaemia and diabetes, and 5,632 individuals (mean age 57.0 +/- 14.7 years; 44% men) with at least one of those risk factors; office central blood pressure, pulse wave velocity and augmentation index were recorded with the Mobil-O-Graph PWA monitor.
cards.result: Reference values for central BP, PWV and AIx were provided for both groups stratified by age and sex (the fetched record does not print the numeric tables, and this card claims none). PWV and AIx rose curvilinearly with age, and age interacted with sex for central systolic pressure and PWV in both groups. In the whole sample (n=6,499), obesity was directly associated with central BP, diabetes directly with PWV, alcohol intake directly with central BP, and physical activity inversely with AIx.
cards.watchOut: Device-specific oscillometric estimates (Mobil-O-Graph) from a retrospective cross-section: the healthy reference group (867) is much smaller than the risk-factor comparison group, and its values must not be quoted as tonometry values.
cards.source: Paiva AMG et al. Reference values of office central blood pressure, pulse wave velocity, and augmentation index recorded by means of the Mobil-O-Graph PWA monitor. Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension. 2020. PMID: 32533101. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Mexican population values (Cossio-Aranda 2020): 1,009 apparently healthy adults (Arteriograph) — central BP and central pulse pressure ran higher than in previously reported populations, especially in women, the elderly and the obese
cards.summary: Mexican population values (Cossio-Aranda 2020): 1,009 apparently healthy adults (Arteriograph) — central BP and central pulse pressure ran higher than in previously reported populations, especially in women, the elderly and the obese
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (Arteriograph central BP and stiffness values, Mexican population)
cards.people: 1,009 apparently healthy subjects recruited 2015-2016 at the Instituto Nacional de Cardiologia Ignacio Chavez (72% women; mean age 47 +/- 12 years; 26% normal weight, 43% overweight, 30% obese). Central blood pressure, central pulse pressure, aortic PWV and augmentation index were acquired with the Arteriograph (TensioMed) oscillometric device.
cards.result: The reference values were higher than those reported in other populations. Aortic PWV and augmentation index were always higher in females. A central-brachial pressure gradient was observed in subjects under 40 years, with lower central than brachial pressure (pressure amplification, described qualitatively in the record without printed mmHg values). Body mass index correlated directly and positively with central BP (P<0.001) but did not modify aortic PWV or augmentation index. The fetched record does not print the numeric age/sex tables, and this card claims none.
cards.watchOut: A clinic-recruited, predominantly female sample in which 73% were overweight or obese despite being 'apparently healthy': its higher central values are population- and device-specific content, not a correction to other populations' references.
cards.source: Cossío-Aranda JE et al. Central blood pressure and vascular stiffness in Mexican population. Archivos de cardiologia de Mexico. 2020. PMID: 31996862. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Omani Arab references (Al-Hashmi 2014, N=120 printed on the face): mean central AIx 13 +/- 11% (women 17% vs men 10%) and aortic PWV 6.7 +/- 1.6 m/s by SphygmoCor applanation tonometry
cards.summary: Omani Arab references (Al-Hashmi 2014, N=120 printed on the face): mean central AIx 13 +/- 11% (women 17% vs men 10%) and aortic PWV 6.7 +/- 1.6 m/s by SphygmoCor applanation tonometry
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (SphygmoCor arterial stiffness / central index reference values, Omani Arab)
cards.people: 120 healthy subjects recruited randomly from a normal population in Oman (mean age 38 years for men, 35 for women; ages 20-53), in whom central augmentation index, aortic pulse wave velocity and central pulse pressure were recorded with a SphygmoCor applanation tonometry device; reference ranges were set by the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles for men and women separately.
cards.result: The overall mean central augmentation index was 13 +/- 11% and aortic PWV 6.7 +/- 1.6 m/s. Central AIx was higher in women than men (17 vs 10%; P<0.001), whereas aortic PWV was higher in men (7.1 vs 6.3 m/s; P=0.003). Reference values for central pulse pressure, central AIx and aortic PWV were obtained by sex and age decade (tables not printed in the fetched record beyond the means above).
cards.watchOut: N=120 — the smallest dataset on this shelf, spanning only ages 20-53: its percentile ranges are correspondingly imprecise and are supportive, not load-bearing; the authors themselves state the results should be interpreted in the context of the study's limitations.
cards.source: Al-Hashmi KM et al. Reference values for arterial stiffness indices in an Omani Arab population. Saudi medical journal. 2014. PMID: 25399214. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: central pressure and augmentation-index references exist, but only per device and per population — the four datasets agree that site, technique, age, sex and height all move the values, which is why this shelf is EMERGING, not ESTABLISHED
cards.summary: Synthesis: central pressure and augmentation-index references exist, but only per device and per population — the four datasets agree that site, technique, age, sex and height all move the values, which is why this shelf is EMERGING, not ESTABLISHED
cards.people: Synthesis of the four primary datasets carded above.
cards.result: Framed by Boron & Boulpaep (arterial pulse / wave reflection) and Guyton & Hall (arterial system chapters). Zocalo 2021 (1,688 healthy, ages 2-84) shows the same index differs systematically by recording site and technique, so intervals are defined per site/technique; Paiva 2020 supplies Mobil-O-Graph office references from 867 rigorously healthy adults; Cossio-Aranda 2020 (1,009 Mexican adults, Arteriograph) finds higher central values than other reported populations with amplification (central below brachial) under age 40; and Al-Hashmi 2014 (120 Omani adults, SphygmoCor) gives mean central AIx 13 +/- 11% and aortic PWV 6.7 +/- 1.6 m/s. Downgrade reasons, on the face: every number is bound to its device/transfer method, healthy denominators are modest (867 and 120 in two datasets), and no dataset's numeric tables are printed in its fetched record beyond the Omani means — so the existence and structure of the references are established, but a universal central-pressure limit is not. Cross-points: pulse-pressure mechanism (#6297) and carotid-femoral PWV references (#7065) are different shelves and are not re-carded here.

shelves.title: 24-h ABPM normal values vs outcome thresholds: normotensive 95th percentiles 129/80 (24-h), 137/88 (day), 121/72 (night); IDACO hypertension thresholds 130/80, 140/85, 120/70
shelves.question: In adults without hypertension, what are normal 24-hour ambulatory blood-pressure values — daytime, night-time and 24-hour means and upper reference limits (95th percentiles) — how large is the normal night-time dip, and how do statistically derived reference limits compare with outcome-driven ambulatory thresholds?
shelves.mesh: Blood Pressure Monitoring, Ambulatory · Reference Values · Blood Pressure/physiology · Circadian Rhythm · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Adult · Aged · Hypertension/diagnosis/epidemiology · Risk Factors
shelves.balance: Textbook framing: Guyton & Hall, long-term blood-pressure control chapters — the framing is brief, and this shelf rests chiefly on the primary population-monitoring literature, and says so. Two KINDS of number are carded and never presented as interchangeable: (1) statistical reference limits from normotensive population samples — the Belgian Population Study (1,057 people; normotensive 95th percentiles 129/80 mmHg over 24 hours, 137/88 daytime, 121/72 night-time) and a normal British sample (282 people; awake mean 115/72, asleep mean 97/58, with 2-standard-deviation upper limits of 136/86 awake and 121/73 asleep — a normal night-time dip of about 18/14 mmHg between the printed means); and (2) outcome-driven thresholds from IDACO (5,682 participants), whose rounded ambulatory-hypertension thresholds (130/80 for 24 hours, 140/85 daytime, 120/70 night-time) sit close to, but are derived differently from, the statistical limits. A companion subject-level analysis (5,018 untreated participants) found home/conventional thresholds did not need to differ by sex or age. The row's third-dataset stop condition is MET: alongside PAMELA and IDACO, the Belgian Population Study was verified from its fetched record this session as a third primary reference dataset (the British sample is a fourth). The PAMELA card is transparent that its fetched record is the study's design report and prints no values. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED.

cards.headline: Belgian Population Study (Staessen 1996): 1,057 randomly sampled adults — in normotensive participants the 95th percentiles were 129/80 mmHg (24-hour), 137/88 (daytime) and 121/72 (night-time)
cards.summary: Belgian Population Study (Staessen 1996): 1,057 randomly sampled adults — in normotensive participants the 95th percentiles were 129/80 mmHg (24-hour), 137/88 (daytime) and 121/72 (night-time)
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (population-based 24-hour ABPM reference distributions, Belgian Population Study) — third primary reference dataset verified at build
cards.people: A random population sample of 1,057 persons aged 20-88 years in a geographically defined area of Belgium (328 hypertensive by conventional pressure above 140/90 mmHg or treatment; 729 normotensive), with 24-hour ambulatory pressure recorded at 20-minute intervals from 0800 to 2200 h and 45-minute intervals overnight, plus conventional pressures at home and (in 532) at a clinic.
cards.result: In the whole sample, 24-hour, daytime and night-time pressures averaged 119/71, 125/77 and 108/62 mmHg respectively. In the normotensive subgroup, the 95th percentiles of the 24-hour, daytime and night-time pressures were 129/80, 137/88 and 121/72 mmHg respectively; restricting to the 275 participants normotensive both at home and at the clinic barely moved them (127/79, 135/87 and 118/72 mmHg). Pooling with other large cohorts, the authors placed the likely normotension-to-hypertension transition at 130-135/80-85 (24-hour), 135-140/85-90 (daytime) and 120-125/70-75 mmHg (night-time), while noting these percentile-based definitions still needed outcome validation.
cards.watchOut: Statistical (percentile) limits from a 1990s Belgian sample with its own day/night definitions: they describe a distribution, not a risk threshold — the outcome-driven numbers are the IDACO card below, and the two kinds must not be interchanged.
cards.source: Staessen JA et al. An epidemiological approach to ambulatory blood pressure monitoring:the Belgian Population Study. Blood pressure monitoring. 1996. PMID: 10226197. Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH: none in the record

cards.headline: Normal British sample (Manning 1998): 282 people without hypertension — awake mean 115/72 and asleep mean 97/58 mmHg; 2-standard-deviation upper limits 136/86 awake, 121/73 asleep, 131/82 overall
cards.summary: Normal British sample (Manning 1998): 282 people without hypertension — awake mean 115/72 and asleep mean 97/58 mmHg; 2-standard-deviation upper limits 136/86 awake, 121/73 asleep, 131/82 overall
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (24-hour ABPM levels and upper limits in a normal British population sample)
cards.people: 282 Caucasian subjects with no known hypertension or cardiovascular disease, recruited from local light industry and a general practice population in Britain, with office and 24-hour ambulatory blood pressures measured.
cards.result: Mean office pressure was 120/75 mmHg, ambulatory mean awake pressure 115/72 and mean asleep pressure 97/58 mmHg — the printed means imply a normal asleep dip of about 18 mmHg systolic and 14 mmHg diastolic below awake values. Men had slightly higher office and awake pressures, with no sex difference asleep. Age was the best predictor of variation but explained only a small amount of it. The two-standard-deviation upper limits for this population were 136/86 mmHg (awake), 121/73 (asleep) and 131/82 (overall).
cards.watchOut: A convenience sample of 282 (light industry and one general practice), all Caucasian: supportive beside the larger population studies, and its upper limits are mean + 2 standard deviations — a different construction from the Belgian 95th percentiles.
cards.source: Manning G et al. Twenty-four hour ambulatory blood pressure: a sample from a normal British population. Journal of human hypertension. 1998. PMID: 9504353. cards.headline: IDACO outcome-driven thresholds (Kikuya 2007): 5,682 participants — rounded thresholds for ambulatory hypertension were 130/80 mmHg (24-hour), 140/85 (daytime) and 120/70 (night-time); optimal 115/75, 120/80 and 100/65
cards.summary: IDACO outcome-driven thresholds (Kikuya 2007): 5,682 participants — rounded thresholds for ambulatory hypertension were 130/80 mmHg (24-hour), 140/85 (daytime) and 120/70 (night-time); optimal 115/75, 120/80 and 100/65
cards.type: Primary human physiology / outcomes study (outcome-driven ABPM diagnostic thresholds, IDACO consortium)
cards.people: 5,682 participants (mean age 59.0 years; 43.3% women) with 24-hour ambulatory monitoring in prospective population studies in Copenhagen (Denmark), Noorderkempen (Belgium), Ohasama (Japan) and Uppsala (Sweden), followed for a median 9.7 years, during which 814 cardiovascular endpoints occurred (377 strokes, 435 cardiac events).
cards.result: Thresholds were derived to yield 10-year cardiovascular risks equivalent to office pressures of 120/80 (optimal), 130/85 (normal) and 140/90 mmHg (high). Unrounded systolic/diastolic thresholds for ambulatory hypertension were 131.0/79.4 mmHg (24-hour), 138.2/86.4 (daytime) and 119.5/70.8 (night-time). After rounding, optimal ambulatory pressure was 115/75 (24-hour), 120/80 (daytime) and 100/65 (night-time); normal was 125/75, 130/85 and 110/70; and ambulatory hypertension was 130/80, 140/85 and 120/70 mmHg respectively. The authors note these outcome-driven thresholds for optimal and normal pressure are lower than those proposed by then-current guidelines.
cards.watchOut: These are risk-equivalence thresholds anchored to office-pressure risk levels — a different kind of number from the statistical percentile limits above, even where the values nearly coincide; the derivation cohorts were older (mean 59) population samples, not screened normotensive volunteers.
cards.source: Kikuya M et al. Diagnostic thresholds for ambulatory blood pressure monitoring based on 10-year cardiovascular risk. Circulation. 2007. PMID: 17420350. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Companion thresholds (Nomura 2014): subject-level meta-analysis of 5,018 untreated participants from 5 populations — home and conventional BP thresholds did not differ significantly by sex or by age (under 60 vs 60+)
cards.summary: Companion thresholds (Nomura 2014): subject-level meta-analysis of 5,018 untreated participants from 5 populations — home and conventional BP thresholds did not differ significantly by sex or by age (under 60 vs 60+)
cards.type: Supporting limb: subject-level meta-analysis of outcome-driven conventional and home BP thresholds by sex and age
cards.people: 5,018 people untreated for hypertension, randomly recruited from 5 populations (56.7% women; 42.3% aged 60 or over), followed for a median 8.3 years with 414 cardiovascular events; conventional and home blood-pressure thresholds were derived from each other by outcome equivalence, stratified by sex and age.
cards.result: Sex differences between derived thresholds were all nonsignificant (P at least 0.24), ranging from -4.6 to 3.6 mmHg systolic and -4.3 to 2.1 mmHg diastolic; age differences were likewise nonsignificant (P at least 0.08) except for home thresholds derived from conventional levels of 140 mmHg systolic and 80 mmHg diastolic. The authors conclude outcome-driven criteria support single blood-pressure thresholds applied in both sexes and across the age range.
cards.watchOut: A companion-threshold study of conventional and HOME pressure, not a 24-hour ABPM reference dataset: it is carded as the supporting limb named in the row, for the sex/age question only, and contributes no ambulatory limits.
cards.source: Nomura K et al. Thresholds for conventional and home blood pressure by sex and age in 5018 participants from 5 populations. Hypertension (Dallas, Tex. : 1979). 2014. PMID: 24980664. shelves.question: In healthy adults, what is brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity — its distribution and age- and sex-specific reference ranges — and how do its values relate to (without being interchangeable with) carotid-femoral PWV?

shelves.balance: Textbook framing: Boron & Boulpaep, arterial mechanics (framing). Three primary datasets, all East-Asian and all using volume-plethysmographic baPWV devices, carded per dataset: 21,094 Chinese subjects whose healthy subgroup (no cardiovascular disease or risk factors) averaged 1,389.9 +/- 288.4 cm/s (13.90 m/s), with discrimination cut-offs of 1,450-1,566 cm/s; 12,517 Japanese subjects without medication or cardiovascular history, from whom 7,881 healthy subjects showed baPWV lower in women than men until age 60 and converging thereafter, rising on a quadratic curve with age; and — the third dataset whose verification the row made a build condition, VERIFIED from its fetched record this session — 974 healthy Northern Chinese subjects with decade upper limits rising from 1,394/1,264 cm/s (men/women, twenties) to 1,798/1,915 cm/s (sixties). baPWV includes a long peripheral muscular-artery path and runs systematically higher than carotid-femoral PWV (the aortic measure, pack #7065): the two scales must never be interchanged, and that contrast is this shelf's core teaching point. The stamp is graded down because every dataset is East-Asian and one device family — reference ranges outside those populations are not established by this base. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING.

cards.headline: Chinese distribution study (Wu 2012): 21,094 subjects — healthy subgroup baPWV averaged 1,389.9 +/- 288.4 cm/s (13.90 m/s); a cut-off of 1,450 cm/s discriminated cardiovascular disease or risk factors
cards.summary: Chinese distribution study (Wu 2012): 21,094 subjects — healthy subgroup baPWV averaged 1,389.9 +/- 288.4 cm/s (13.90 m/s); a cut-off of 1,450 cm/s discriminated cardiovascular disease or risk factors
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (baPWV distribution and age/sex reference ranges, Chinese population)
cards.people: 21,094 subjects recruited in a cross-sectional study in China (June 2007 to June 2008), divided into subgroup 1 (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease), subgroup 2 (atherosclerotic risk factors) and subgroup 3 ('healthy subjects' with neither).
cards.result: Mean baPWV was 1,724.3 +/- 429.1 cm/s (17.24 m/s) in subgroup 1, 1,603.5 +/- 358.8 cm/s (16.04 m/s) in subgroup 2 and 1,389.9 +/- 288.4 cm/s (13.90 m/s) in healthy subgroup 3; baPWV was not normally distributed in either sex and rose significantly with age in both. In healthy subgroup 3 baPWV was lower in women than men (the reverse held in subgroup 2, and there was no sex difference in subgroup 1). Receiver-operating analysis gave a baPWV of 1,450 cm/s (14.50 m/s) to discriminate either cardiovascular disease or risk factors (sensitivity 62.1%, specificity 69.5%), 1,551 cm/s for cardiovascular disease and 1,566 cm/s for disease or chronic kidney disease.
cards.watchOut: A mixed clinical population: only subgroup 3 is a healthy reference group, and the 1,450-1,566 cm/s figures are discrimination cut-offs against disease/risk status, not upper reference limits — do not quote them as normal limits.
cards.source: Wu L et al. Distribution of brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity values and optimal cut-off in distinguishing subjects with clinical condition in Chinese population. International angiology : a journal of the International Union of Angiology. 2012. PMID: 22634980. Registry ID: none in the record.
