cards.headline: Japanese survey (Tomiyama 2003): 12,517 subjects without medication or cardiovascular history — in 7,881 healthy subjects baPWV was lower in women until age 60, then converged; the age relation was quadratic and steeper in women
cards.summary: Japanese survey (Tomiyama 2003): 12,517 subjects without medication or cardiovascular history — in 7,881 healthy subjects baPWV was lower in women until age 60, then converged; the age relation was quadratic and steeper in women
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (baPWV age and sex influences, Japanese population survey)
cards.people: 12,517 subjects with no medication and no history of cardiovascular disease; from them, 7,881 'healthy subjects' (4,488 men and 3,393 women, aged 25-87 years) without any atherogenic risk factors were extracted and analysed in 5-year age intervals.
cards.result: Multiple regression showed age, blood pressure, body mass index, triglycerides, blood glucose and uric acid were significant variables for baPWV in both sexes. In healthy subjects, baPWV was lower in women than in men until age 60 and became similar in both sexes over age 60; the effect of age on baPWV (both the explained variance and the regression coefficient) was larger in women than in men, and the age-baPWV relation followed a quadratic curve in both sexes. The authors suggest menopause is the crucial phenomenon behind the augmented rise in arterial stiffness with ageing in women. The fetched record does not print the 5-year-interval values in cm/s, and this card claims none.
cards.watchOut: The oldest dataset on this shelf (2003, first-generation baPWV devices): its age/sex pattern is the content here, and its absolute values should be read beside the later Chinese datasets rather than pooled with them.
cards.source: Tomiyama H et al. Influences of age and gender on results of noninvasive brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity measurement--a survey of 12517 subjects. Atherosclerosis. 2003. PMID: 12535743. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Northern Chinese reference values (Wang 2009) — third dataset verified at build: 974 healthy subjects; upper limits by decade rose from 1,394/1,264 cm/s (men/women in their twenties) to 1,798/1,915 cm/s in their sixties
cards.summary: Northern Chinese reference values (Wang 2009) — third dataset verified at build: 974 healthy subjects; upper limits by decade rose from 1,394/1,264 cm/s (men/women in their twenties) to 1,798/1,915 cm/s in their sixties
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (baPWV reference values by age and sex, Northern Chinese) — third primary dataset verified at build under the row's stop condition
cards.people: 974 identified healthy subjects recruited in an epidemiological study in north China, with baPWV measured noninvasively with an automatic (volume-plethysmographic) device; mean baPWV was higher in men overall (P<0.001), higher in men than women below age 50 but not in the older group.
cards.result: Multiple regression showed age and systolic blood pressure were positively associated with baPWV in both sexes (P<0.001), and the effect of age on baPWV augmentation was greater in women. The upper limits of baPWV for healthy men/women at 10-year intervals (age range 20-70 years) were 1,394/1,264 cm/s (13.94/12.64 m/s), 1,435/1,361, 1,552/1,433, 1,597/1,609 and 1,798/1,915 cm/s (17.98/19.15 m/s) — women overtaking men in the oldest bands, consistent with the Japanese pattern above.
cards.watchOut: The smallest of the three datasets (974 healthy subjects) and, like the others, East-Asian and single-device-family: these upper limits are references for comparable populations and devices, not universal baPWV limits.
cards.source: Wang X et al. Reference values of brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity for Northern Chinese. Chinese medical journal. 2009. PMID: 19781292. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: baPWV rises with age on a curve that steepens in women after midlife — healthy means near 13.9 m/s and decade upper limits to about 19 m/s in the oldest band — and baPWV is NOT carotid-femoral PWV
cards.summary: Synthesis: baPWV rises with age on a curve that steepens in women after midlife — healthy means near 13.9 m/s and decade upper limits to about 19 m/s in the oldest band — and baPWV is NOT carotid-femoral PWV
cards.people: Synthesis of the three primary datasets carded above.
cards.result: Framed by Boron & Boulpaep (arterial mechanics). The three datasets agree: baPWV increases with age in both sexes (quadratically in the Japanese survey of 7,881 healthy subjects), is lower in women than men until about age 60 and then converges or overtakes (Northern Chinese upper limits 1,798 cm/s in men vs 1,915 cm/s in women in the sixties band), and is driven by age and systolic pressure above other factors. Absolute scale: the healthy Chinese subgroup averaged 1,389.9 cm/s (13.90 m/s). The row's stop condition was discharged at build: a third primary adult dataset (Wang 2009, PMID 19781292) was verified from its fetched record. Downgrade reason, on the face: all three datasets are East-Asian and use volume-plethysmographic baPWV devices, so ranges are EMERGING beyond those populations. Cross-point: carotid-femoral PWV reference values (pack #7065) measure the aortic path only and run systematically lower — never card baPWV values on cfPWV scales.
cards.watchOut: Device must be named per dataset; a baPWV in cm/s converted to m/s is the same measurement, but a baPWV is never a cfPWV.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Coagulation screening intervals: a common adult interval fits PT/INR, thrombin time and fibrinogen — minor age/sex variation in 1.78M data-mined samples — but aPTT is reagent- and analyser-specific
shelves.question: In healthy non-pregnant adults, what are the reference intervals for the coagulation screening tests — prothrombin time / INR, activated partial thromboplastin time, thrombin time and fibrinogen — by age (including older adults), sex, analyser and reagent, and how much do data-mined (indirect) intervals agree with directly recruited healthy-volunteer intervals?

shelves.balance: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED. Textbook framing: Guyton & Hall, haemostasis chapters, and Boron & Boulpaep, blood sections (framing brief — this shelf rests chiefly on the primary reference-interval literature, and says so). Four datasets converge on the same practical picture: directly and indirectly derived intervals for PT/INR, aPTT, thrombin time and fibrinogen show only minor age and sex variation, supporting a common adult interval (Zierk 2019: 1,778,738 samples from 116,754 patients, data-mined; Wu 2025: 630,946 records, cross-platform), BUT aPTT intervals are batch-, reagent- and analyser-specific to a degree unusual among routine tests, so no universal aPTT range is printed here. In healthy people over 60 a proportion of aPTT and TEG results fell outside adult intervals while derived fibrinogen stayed inside them (Donkin 2020, n=60), and in 121 healthy young female athletes the fibrinogen interval ran higher (1.9–4.4 g/L (190–440 mg/dL)) than the national non-athlete interval (1.8–3.5 g/L (180–350 mg/dL)) while PT and aPTT-ratio intervals were confirmed (HemSter 2021). Pregnancy-specific intervals are a separate literature and are NOT this shelf.

cards.headline: Data-mined intervals from 1,778,738 samples (116,754 adults): age- and sex-specific PT, INR, aPTT, thrombin time and fibrinogen intervals show only minor age/sex variation — a common adult interval is supported (Zierk 2019)
cards.summary: Data-mined intervals from 1,778,738 samples (116,754 adults): age- and sex-specific PT, INR, aPTT, thrombin time and fibrinogen intervals show only minor age/sex variation — a common adult interval is supported (Zierk 2019)
cards.type: Primary physiology / reference-interval study (indirect data-mining, single university hospital)
cards.people: Measurements of aPTT, PT, INR, thrombin time and fibrinogen performed during clinical care at University Hospital Erlangen, Germany — 1,778,738 samples from 116,754 adult patients (45,577–509,859 samples per analyte); the healthy proportion was identified statistically with the Reference Limit Estimator.
cards.result: Age- and sex-specific reference intervals were established for all five tests, plus batch- and reagent-specific aPTT intervals, and the sensitivity of the aPTT intervals for detecting factor VIII, IX, XI and XII deficiencies was evaluated. The established intervals showed only minor variation with sex and age, supporting a common reference interval for adult women and men. The authors stress the intervals are specific to the population, analytical framework and reagent examined. The fetched record does not print the numeric interval limits, and this card claims none.
cards.watchOut: Indirect method: intervals are modelled out of routine clinical samples, not measured in recruited healthy volunteers, and are explicitly reagent- and framework-specific — especially for aPTT.
cards.source: Zierk J et al. Data mining of reference intervals for coagulation screening tests in adult patients. Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry. 2019. PMID: 31513787. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Healthy donors over 60 (n=60): all derived-fibrinogen results fell inside adult intervals (higher in women), but a proportion of aPTT and TEG 6s results fell outside them (Donkin 2020)
cards.summary: Healthy donors over 60 (n=60): all derived-fibrinogen results fell inside adult intervals (higher in women), but a proportion of aPTT and TEG 6s results fell outside them (Donkin 2020)
cards.type: Primary physiology / reference-interval verification study (healthy donors over 60)
cards.people: Healthy blood donors aged over 60 years (30 men, 30 women), tested by TEG 6s, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time and derived fibrinogen, compared against adult reference intervals with no upper age limit.
cards.result: All older-donor derived fibrinogen results were within the adult reference intervals, although levels were significantly higher in females. A proportion of TEG 6s and aPTT results were NOT within the reference intervals. The authors question whether older adults require age-specific coagulation reference intervals.
cards.watchOut: Small verification sample (n=60) and a proportion-outside finding without printed percentages in the fetched record — it raises the age-specific question, it does not settle new elderly limits.
cards.source: Donkin R et al. Investigating Age Appropriate Coagulation Reference Intervals to Support Patient Blood Management in the Elderly: A Verification Study. cards.headline: 630,946 Chinese records, 11 indirect algorithms, two platforms: Z-Score and Tukey performed best for 8 coagulation parameters; sex stratification unnecessary, age stratification needed for D-dimer at ≥60 years (Wu 2025)
cards.summary: 630,946 Chinese records, 11 indirect algorithms, two platforms: Z-Score and Tukey performed best for 8 coagulation parameters; sex stratification unnecessary, age stratification needed for D-dimer at ≥60 years (Wu 2025)
cards.type: Primary physiology / reference-interval study (indirect multi-algorithm framework, cross-platform)
cards.people: 630,946 coagulation test records from Shenzhen Hospital of Southern Medical University, analysed retrospectively with eleven outlier-detection algorithms; validated across Mindray CX-9000 and Stago STA R Max platforms against manufacturer standards.
cards.result: Z-Score and Tukey algorithms showed optimal performance for 8 coagulation parameters, yielding intervals with minimal deviation from manufacturer standards. Sex differences were minimal (standard deviation ratio <0.40, Cohen's d <0.50), eliminating the need for sex stratification. Age stratification WAS required for D-dimer (≥60-year subgroup: SDR 0.62, Cohen's d 0.54). Cross-platform consistency confirmed the algorithms generalise.
cards.watchOut: An algorithm-comparison study: its 'universal' claim is about the derivation method, not about one set of limits fitting every analyser — D-dimer is carded here only as the age-stratification limb of the panel, not as a standalone D-dimer norms claim.
cards.source: Wu Y et al. An integrated framework for universal coagulation test reference intervals: Cross-platform validation of eleven indirect algorithms and age-specific hierarchical optimization. Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry. 2025. PMID: 40499770. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: HemSter verification in 121 healthy young female athletes: PT and aPTT-ratio intervals confirmed, but fibrinogen ran higher — 1.9–4.4 g/L (190–440 mg/dL) vs the national 1.8–3.5 g/L (180–350 mg/dL) (Radišić Biljak 2021)
cards.summary: HemSter verification in 121 healthy young female athletes: PT and aPTT-ratio intervals confirmed, but fibrinogen ran higher — 1.9–4.4 g/L (190–440 mg/dL) vs the national 1.8–3.5 g/L (180–350 mg/dL) (Radišić Biljak 2021)
cards.type: Supporting limb: reference-interval verification study (healthy young female athletes)
cards.people: 121 female athletes aged 16–34 from water polo, handball, volleyball, football and basketball; fasting morning samples before activity; intervals determined per CLSI EP28-A3C and compared with common national reference intervals.
cards.result: Calculated intervals for white cell count, prothrombin time and aPTT ratio accorded with the common national intervals. The fibrinogen interval was higher (1.9–4.4 g/L (190–440 mg/dL)) than the available interval (1.8–3.5 g/L (180–350 mg/dL)); the CRP interval was lower (<2.9 mg/L vs a <5.0 mg/L healthy cut-off) and the D-dimer cut-off derived was 852 µg/L FEU, above the proposed 500 µg/L FEU for venous thromboembolism exclusion — a value the authors say needs extensive verification before use in athletes.
cards.watchOut: A young athletic female population is not the general adult population: the fibrinogen and D-dimer departures describe athletes, and the D-dimer figure must never be used as a general VTE-exclusion cut-off.
cards.source: Radišić Biljak V et al. Women in sports: the applicability of common national reference intervals for inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers (HemSter Study). Biochemia medica. 2021. PMID: 33380889. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: coagulation screening intervals are a common adult interval in practice — minor age/sex variation across 1.78 million data-mined samples and 630,946 algorithm-derived records — with aPTT bound to its reagent and analyser, and fibrinogen running higher in older women and in young athletes
cards.summary: Synthesis: coagulation screening intervals are a common adult interval in practice — minor age/sex variation across 1.78 million data-mined samples and 630,946 algorithm-derived records — with aPTT bound to its reagent and analyser, and fibrinogen running higher in older women and in young athletes
cards.people: All datasets carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Framed by Guyton & Hall (haemostasis) and Boron & Boulpaep (blood) — framing brief; the shelf rests on the primary interval literature. Zierk 2019 and Wu 2025, the two very large indirect datasets, agree that sex partitioning is unnecessary and age effects are minor for the screening panel (D-dimer excepted at ≥60 years in Wu). Donkin 2020 (n=60 over-60s) is the caution: a proportion of aPTT results fell outside adult intervals in healthy older donors. HemSter 2021 confirms PT and aPTT-ratio intervals in athletes while fibrinogen runs higher. Fibrinogen is carded only as one limb of this screening panel, on the strength of these panel datasets. PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED for the panel structure and the common-adult-interval conclusion; no universal numeric aPTT range is asserted, because aPTT is reagent- and analyser-specific.
cards.watchOut: Never print one platform's aPTT limits as universal, and never merge directly recruited healthy-volunteer intervals with data-mined indirect intervals without labelling the method — the two approaches are carded separately here by design.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Probucol: SPLIT record — events trend not significant in PROSPECTIVE (n=876), femoral imaging null in PQRST, carotid IMT −13.9% and events 2.4% vs 13.6% in FAST; HDL falls ≈24% relative
shelves.question: In patients with hypercholesterolaemia or established coronary heart disease, does the antioxidant lipid-lowering agent probucol, compared with placebo, control therapy or a statin, slow atherosclerosis progression and reduce cardiovascular events — and at what cost to HDL cholesterol?

shelves.balance: SPLIT. Withdrawn / restricted product history leads this shelf: probucol was withdrawn from the US market (1995) and remains in use chiefly in Japan — the regulatory history as stated in the commissioning row, printed here on the face. The three anchor trials answer three DIFFERENT endpoint levels and are never merged into one 'works' claim. Events: PROSPECTIVE (876 Japanese patients with coronary heart disease) found the primary cerebrovascular/cardiovascular composite incidence showed a trend to be lower with probucol 500 mg/day added to conventional therapy — a trend, NOT statistically significant, despite reduced HDL cholesterol and without serious adverse events. Femoral imaging: PQRST (303 randomised, 274 analysed, all on diet plus cholestyramine) was NULL on its primary — no significant difference in femoral-artery lumen-volume change — while probucol lowered total cholesterol 17%, LDL cholesterol 12% and HDL cholesterol 24% relative to control; that HDL lowering is the drug's paradox and is printed, not buried. Carotid imaging: FAST (246 patients) found carotid IMT fell 13.9% on probucol and 13.9% on pravastatin while the diet-only control thickened 23.2%, with cardiac events 2.4% on probucol vs 13.6% on control (P = 0.0136) — absolute rates as printed. One positive small imaging trial with an events signal, one null imaging trial, one large events trial with a non-significant trend: that is a SPLIT record.

cards.headline: PROSPECTIVE secondary-prevention trial (876 patients with coronary heart disease): probucol 500 mg/day added to conventional therapy showed a TREND — not statistically significant — to fewer cerebrovascular/cardiovascular events, despite lowering HDL cholesterol (Yamashita 2021)
cards.summary: PROSPECTIVE secondary-prevention trial (876 patients with coronary heart disease): probucol 500 mg/day added to conventional therapy showed a TREND — not statistically significant — to fewer cerebrovascular/cardiovascular events, despite lowering HDL cholesterol (Yamashita 2021)
cards.type: Multicentre randomised secondary-prevention trial (PROSPECTIVE: probucol add-on vs conventional therapy alone)
cards.people: 876 Japanese patients with coronary heart disease and dyslipidaemia (LDL cholesterol ≥140 mg/dL untreated, or on lipid-lowering drugs), randomised to conventional lipid-lowering therapy alone (n=438) or with probucol 500 mg/day added (n=438), stratified by LDL level, diabetes and hypertension, and followed for more than 3 years. The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death including sudden death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, hospitalisation for unstable angina or heart failure, or coronary revascularisation; carotid IMT was a secondary endpoint in a subset.
cards.result: The incidence of the primary endpoint showed a trend to be lower in the probucol group than the control group, despite reduced HDL cholesterol, and without serious adverse events. There was NO statistical significance between the groups — the fetched record prints no event rates or hazard ratio, and this card claims none. The authors attribute any anti-atherogenic effect to probucol's potent antioxidative function and enhancement of reverse cholesterol transport, and conclude further outcome studies are necessary. Trial registration as printed in the record: UMIN000003307.
cards.watchOut: A non-significant trend is not a benefit: this is the largest and most clinically relevant trial on the shelf, and its primary result is null by significance testing — the shelf's stamp rests on that fact.
cards.source: Yamashita S et al. Probucol Trial for Secondary Prevention of Atherosclerotic Events in Patients with Coronary Heart Disease (PROSPECTIVE). Journal of atherosclerosis and thrombosis. 2021. PMID: 32336695. Registry ID: UMIN000003307. cards.headline: PQRST (303 randomised, 274 analysed): probucol lowered total cholesterol 17%, LDL 12% and HDL 24% relative to control — with NO significant difference in femoral-artery lumen-volume change, a null imaging primary (Walldius 1994)
cards.summary: PQRST (303 randomised, 274 analysed): probucol lowered total cholesterol 17%, LDL 12% and HDL 24% relative to control — with NO significant difference in femoral-artery lumen-volume change, a null imaging primary (Walldius 1994)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind trial (PQRST: probucol vs placebo, both on diet + cholestyramine; femoral arteriographic primary)
cards.people: 303 patients with visible femoral atherosclerosis (mean age 55 years in the 274 analysed; 158 men; 17% with intermittent claudication, 24% with angina) randomised to probucol 0.5 g twice daily or placebo for 3 years; ALL patients received diet plus cholestyramine 8–16 g/day. Twenty-nine patients were excluded for inadequate primary-endpoint measurements. The primary endpoint was change in femoral-artery lumen volume by quantitative arteriography.
cards.result: After 3 years, probucol-treated patients had 17% lower serum cholesterol, 12% lower LDL cholesterol, 24% lower total HDL cholesterol and 34% lower HDL2 cholesterol than controls — all relative differences, highly significant throughout. There was NO statistically significant change in lumen volume between probucol and control, and no differences in arterial edge roughness, aorto-femoral atherosclerosis amount, exercise-test ST depressions or ankle/arm blood pressure. In the control group, lumen volume increased (P < 0.001) and femoral roughness decreased (P < 0.05). The fetched abstract is truncated at 250 words in the record, as published.
cards.watchOut: The background therapy (cholestyramine in everyone) and a femoral — not carotid or coronary — arterial bed limit generalisation; and the 24% relative HDL lowering on this card is the same drug property the other cards must be read against.
cards.source: Walldius G et al. The effect of probucol on femoral atherosclerosis: the Probucol Quantitative Regression Swedish Trial (PQRST). The American journal of cardiology. 1994. PMID: 7977117. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: FAST (246 asymptomatic hypercholesterolaemic patients): carotid IMT fell 13.9% on probucol and 13.9% on pravastatin while controls thickened 23.2% — cardiac events 2.4% on probucol vs 13.6% on control (P = 0.0136) (Sawayama 2002)
cards.summary: FAST (246 asymptomatic hypercholesterolaemic patients): carotid IMT fell 13.9% on probucol and 13.9% on pravastatin while controls thickened 23.2% — cardiac events 2.4% on probucol vs 13.6% on control (P = 0.0136) (Sawayama 2002)
cards.type: Randomised trial (FAST: probucol vs pravastatin vs diet-only control; carotid IMT primary, cardiac events secondary)
cards.people: 246 asymptomatic hypercholesterolaemic patients in Fukuoka, Japan (mean age 66 years), randomised to probucol 500 mg/day (n=82), pravastatin 10 mg/day (n=83) or diet-only control (n=81) for 2 years. The primary endpoint was change in common carotid artery IMT; major cardiovascular events were the secondary measure.
cards.result: Over 2 years, LDL cholesterol fell 36% on pravastatin, 29% on probucol and 12% on control (relative reductions as printed; P < 0.0001, P < 0.0001 and P < 0.05 respectively). Carotid IMT fell significantly in both active groups (−13.9% and −13.9%; P < 0.01 each) while the control group thickened significantly (+23.2%; P < 0.05). Probucol reduced the rate of IMT increase independently of its LDL or HDL cholesterol reduction. Cardiac events were significantly fewer on probucol (2.4%) than control (13.6%) (P = 0.0136) — absolute rates as printed.
cards.watchOut: The events difference rests on a small secondary endpoint (2.4% of 82 patients is 2 events vs 13.6% of 81) in an imaging trial — it is a signal inside a 246-patient study, not an outcomes trial, and the control was diet only, not placebo.
cards.source: Sawayama Y et al. Effects of probucol and pravastatin on common carotid atherosclerosis in patients with asymptomatic hypercholesterolemia. Fukuoka Atherosclerosis Trial (FAST). Journal of the American College of Cardiology. 2002. PMID: 11849859. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: probucol's record splits by endpoint level — a non-significant events trend in the one large secondary-prevention trial, a null femoral-imaging primary, and a positive carotid-imaging trial with a small events signal — all while lowering HDL cholesterol by about a quarter
cards.summary: Synthesis: probucol's record splits by endpoint level — a non-significant events trend in the one large secondary-prevention trial, a null femoral-imaging primary, and a positive carotid-imaging trial with a small events signal — all while lowering HDL cholesterol by about a quarter
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: PROSPECTIVE (n=876, events) trends without significance; PQRST (n=274 analysed, femoral imaging) is null on its primary despite 17%/12% relative total/LDL cholesterol lowering; FAST (n=246, carotid imaging) is positive on IMT (−13.9% vs +23.2% control thickening) with fewer cardiac events (2.4% vs 13.6%, absolute). The constant across all three is HDL lowering (24% relative in PQRST), the paradox at the centre of this drug. Probucol was withdrawn from the US market in 1995 and remains in use chiefly in Japan. PROPOSED STAMP: SPLIT — the endpoint levels genuinely disagree, and no single 'works / does not work' claim survives all three trials.
cards.watchOut: Do not cite FAST's event rates as outcomes-trial evidence and do not cite PROSPECTIVE's trend as a benefit: the two errors are mirror images, and this shelf exists to keep them apart.

shelves.title: Molsidomine in stable angina: exercise capacity improved and anginal attacks and nitrate use fell vs placebo in three crossover trials (largest n=533) — symptoms only, no outcomes trial
shelves.question: In adults with stable angina pectoris, does the nitric-oxide donor molsidomine, compared with placebo, improve exercise capacity and reduce anginal attacks and sublingual nitrate use?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Angina Pectoris · Blood Pressure · Cross-Over Studies · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Double-Blind Method · Exercise Test · Exercise Tolerance · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Molsidomine · Nitric Oxide Donors · Patient Compliance · Quality of Life · Time Factors · Treatment Outcome · Vasodilator Agents
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) on exercise capacity and anginal symptoms, on three randomised double-blind crossover placebo-controlled trials (90, 533 and 50 patients): total work performance and exercise duration improved significantly vs placebo for up to 8–12 hours after dosing, effects were maintained after 2–6 weeks with no attenuation, and anginal-attack frequency and sublingual nitrate consumption fell significantly. This is an exercise-capacity/symptom trial base — no outcomes trial exists. Molsidomine is a European-market agent, not FDA-approved; the tested formulations are named exactly on the cards. Hypotension was significantly more frequent on the 16 mg once-daily formulation than placebo; headache is the other harm-side item. A further single-dose add-on-to-atenolol trial (n=12) is carded as programme support only, not as an anchor.

cards.headline: Crossover RCT (Messin 1998): molsidomine and molsidomine retard significantly improved total work performance vs placebo up to 8–12 hours after dosing, maintained after 6 weeks, with fewer anginal attacks and less sublingual nitrate use
cards.summary: Crossover RCT (Messin 1998): molsidomine and molsidomine retard significantly improved total work performance vs placebo up to 8–12 hours after dosing, maintained after 6 weeks, with fewer anginal attacks and less sublingual nitrate use
cards.type: Multicentre randomised double-blind crossover placebo-controlled trial, molsidomine 4 mg three times daily and molsidomine retard 8 mg twice daily
cards.people: 90 isosorbide-dinitrate responders with stable angina, in a multicentre randomised double-blind crossover placebo-controlled study comparing molsidomine retard 8 mg twice daily with molsidomine 4 mg three times daily, each for 6 weeks.
cards.result: Total work performance (workload × min) was significantly improved, compared with baseline and placebo, until 8 hours after molsidomine and 12 hours after molsidomine retard administration. ST-segment depression decreased significantly under both treatments at 60 W and at maximal exercise. All effects remained significant after 6 weeks of treatment, with only the ST segment showing a nonsignificant tendency to improvement at maximal work. The frequency of anginal attacks and of sublingual nitroderivative-tablet consumption decreased significantly with both formulations; molsidomine retard reduced myocardial ischaemia more efficiently at submaximal exercise, with a more prolonged effect on exercise tolerance.
cards.watchOut: A crossover trial in isosorbide-dinitrate responders — a selected population — measuring exercise and symptom endpoints over 6 weeks; no clinical-outcomes data.

cards.headline: Prolonged-release crossover RCT (Messin 2005): both 16 mg once-daily and 8 mg twice-daily molsidomine significantly improved exercise-test parameters vs placebo acutely and after 2 weeks, and reduced anginal attacks and nitrate use; hypotension was significantly more frequent on 16 mg
cards.summary: Prolonged-release crossover RCT (Messin 2005): both 16 mg once-daily and 8 mg twice-daily molsidomine significantly improved exercise-test parameters vs placebo acutely and after 2 weeks, and reduced anginal attacks and nitrate use; hypotension was significantly more frequent on 16 mg
cards.type: Multicentre randomised double-blind double-dummy crossover trial, prolonged-release molsidomine 16 mg once daily vs 8 mg twice daily vs placebo
cards.people: 533 patients with stable angina pectoris, in a randomised multicentre double-blind double-dummy crossover trial comparing prolonged-release molsidomine 16 mg once daily with 8 mg twice daily and placebo, acutely and after 2 weeks of treatment, after a 7-day placebo run-in.
cards.result: Both formulations significantly improved exercise-test parameters compared with placebo, after acute intake and after 2 weeks, independently of spontaneous diurnal variation in exercise tolerance. Non-inferiority of 16 mg once daily vs 8 mg twice daily was demonstrated, with statistically significant superiority of the 16 mg formulation from 14 to 24 hours post-intake. Both treatments reduced the incidence of anginal attacks and the use of sublingual isosorbide dinitrate tablets. The incidence of drug-related headache was not significantly different from placebo; only hypotension was significantly more frequent with molsidomine 16 mg than with placebo.
cards.watchOut: The largest trial of the base (533 patients) but still a 2-week crossover exercise-endpoint study; patients who developed hypotension on the 16 mg formulation had significantly lower pretrial diastolic blood pressure than those who did not.
cards.source: Messin R et al. Efficacy and safety of molsidomine once-a-day in patients with stable angina pectoris. International journal of cardiology. 2005. PMID: 15676171. cards.headline: Retard crossover study (Messin 1995): molsidomine retard 8 mg significantly improved total exercise duration and work performance vs placebo at all time points to 10 hours, with no attenuation after 14 days and significantly fewer anginal attacks
cards.summary: Retard crossover study (Messin 1995): molsidomine retard 8 mg significantly improved total exercise duration and work performance vs placebo at all time points to 10 hours, with no attenuation after 14 days and significantly fewer anginal attacks
cards.type: Double-blind placebo-controlled crossover study, molsidomine retard (extended release) 8 mg
cards.people: 50 patients with ischaemic heart disease and stable angina, in a double-blind placebo-controlled crossover study of molsidomine extended release (retard) 8 mg, with exercise testing at baseline and 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 hours after intake.
cards.result: Total duration of exercise and total work performance (workload × min) were significantly improved in the molsidomine retard group, compared with baseline and with placebo, at all time points. ST-segment depression at 60 W and at maximal exercise improved similarly until 10 hours after molsidomine retard. No attenuation of the effects was observed after 14 days of treatment. The number of anginal attacks and the consumption of sublingual nitroderivates were significantly reduced with molsidomine retard 8 mg compared with placebo.
cards.watchOut: A 50-patient crossover study with exercise endpoints measured over a single day and after 14 days; it supports duration of effect, not clinical outcomes.

cards.headline: Programme support only — single-dose add-on to atenolol (De Backer 1985, n=12): a single dose of molsidomine on top of atenolol improved mean exercise time to angina from 330 to 420 seconds (not an anchor of this shelf)
cards.summary: Programme support only — single-dose add-on to atenolol (De Backer 1985, n=12): a single dose of molsidomine on top of atenolol improved mean exercise time to angina from 330 to 420 seconds (not an anchor of this shelf)
cards.type: Programme support only: randomised double-blind placebo-controlled single-dose add-on trial (n=12) — not an anchor
cards.people: 12 patients with chronic stable effort angina on long-term atenolol 100 mg daily, in a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial of a single dose of molsidomine added to atenolol. N = 12, printed on the face: this report is programme support only and is NOT an anchor of this shelf.
cards.result: The mean exercise time to produce angina improved significantly from 330 ± 38 seconds (mean ± SEM) after atenolol plus placebo to 420 ± 36 seconds after atenolol plus molsidomine. Similar significant improvements were seen in ST-segment changes at an identical exercise duration, in maximal heart rate and in maximal exercise duration; the increased anginal threshold was not explained by changes in the rate-pressure product at submaximal levels.
cards.watchOut: Twelve patients and a single dose: this card shows an add-on effect exists on top of a beta-blocker and nothing more; the shelf's claim rests on the three anchor trials above, never on this report.

cards.headline: Synthesis: three crossover anchor trials (90, 533 and 50 patients) consistently show molsidomine improving exercise capacity and reducing anginal attacks and nitrate use vs placebo, with effects maintained over 2–6 weeks; the n=12 single-dose report is support only
cards.summary: Synthesis: three crossover anchor trials (90, 533 and 50 patients) consistently show molsidomine improving exercise capacity and reducing anginal attacks and nitrate use vs placebo, with effects maintained over 2–6 weeks; the n=12 single-dose report is support only
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Across the three anchors, total work performance, exercise duration and ST-segment depression all improved significantly vs placebo, anginal attacks and sublingual nitrate consumption fell significantly, and no attenuation was seen over 2–6 weeks. The endpoints are exercise capacity and symptoms — no trial in this base measured death, myocardial infarction or hospitalisation. Molsidomine is a European-market nitric-oxide donor, not FDA-approved; the formulations tested were molsidomine 4 mg three times daily, molsidomine retard 8 mg twice daily and prolonged-release molsidomine 16 mg once daily. Headache and hypotension are the harm side, hypotension significantly more frequent on the 16 mg formulation than placebo in the 533-patient trial.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Oral fasudil in stable angina (FLOOR-RISK — exactly 2 publications / 3 trials): time to ST depression prolonged vs placebo, exercise duration not significantly — surrogate endpoints only
shelves.question: In adults with stable (effort) angina, does the oral Rho-kinase inhibitor fasudil, compared with placebo, improve exercise time and time to ischaemic ST-segment depression?
shelves.mesh: 1-(5-Isoquinolinesulfonyl)-2-Methylpiperazine · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Angina Pectoris · Enzyme Inhibitors · Exercise · Female · Humans · Intracellular Signaling Peptides and Proteins · Japan · Male · Middle Aged · Protein Serine-Threonine Kinases · Signal Transduction · rho-Associated Kinases
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit), on a FLOOR-RISK base stated on the face: exactly 2 publications reporting 3 component trials (the phase IIa dose-escalation studies, the phase IIb double-blind dose-ranging trial, and the US double-blind placebo-controlled phase 2 trial). Time to at least 1 mm ST-segment depression increased by 172.1 seconds on fasudil vs 44.0 seconds on placebo at peak (P = 0.001) in the US trial, whose exercise duration was numerically, not significantly, greater and which found no significant differences in angina frequency or nitroglycerin use; the Japanese programme prolonged maximum exercise time and time to ST depression with a significant dose–response for the exercise tolerance index (P = 0.006). These are surrogate exercise endpoints only. The intracoronary fasudil studies in vasospastic and microvascular angina are a different route and different questions — they are NOT counted or merged here. Fasudil is approved in Japan for cerebral vasospasm, not for angina anywhere.

cards.headline: US phase 2 RCT (Vicari 2005): time to at least 1 mm ST-segment depression increased by 172.1 s on fasudil vs 44.0 s on placebo at peak (P = 0.001); exercise duration was numerically, not significantly, greater
cards.summary: US phase 2 RCT (Vicari 2005): time to at least 1 mm ST-segment depression increased by 172.1 s on fasudil vs 44.0 s on placebo at peak (P = 0.001); exercise duration was numerically, not significantly, greater
cards.type: Multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled randomised phase 2 trial, oral fasudil vs placebo (one of the 2 publications of this shelf's base)
cards.people: 84 patients with stable angina and reproducible exercise times (of 206 screened), randomised 1:1 to oral fasudil or placebo in a multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled trial; fasudil was force-titrated over 8 weeks, nitroglycerin as needed and a beta- or calcium-channel blocker were allowed, and symptom-limited exercise testing was performed after two, four, six and eight weeks.
cards.result: Time to at least 1 mm ST-segment depression was increased with fasudil at both peak (172.1 s vs 44.0 s, P = 0.001) and trough (92.8 s vs 26.4 s, P = 0.02) compared with placebo. Exercise duration was significantly improved at all visits in both groups and was numerically greater on fasudil than placebo — not significantly. Fasudil improved Seattle Angina Questionnaire scores. No significant differences in Canadian Cardiovascular Society class, time to angina, or frequency of angina or nitroglycerin use were noted between groups. Fasudil did not affect heart rate or blood pressure and was well tolerated.
cards.watchOut: The only placebo-controlled trial of the base, and its patient-centred measures (angina frequency, nitroglycerin use) did NOT differ significantly — the positive result is the ischaemic-threshold exercise endpoint. One of exactly two publications on this shelf.
cards.source: Vicari RM et al. Efficacy and safety of fasudil in patients with stable angina: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial. Journal of the American College of Cardiology. 2005. cards.headline: Programme report, component trial 1 of 2 — phase IIa dose-escalation studies (Shimokawa 2002): fasudil significantly prolonged maximum exercise time and time to 1-mm ST depression (both P < 0.01) in 45 patients, with similar results at higher doses in a further 22
cards.summary: Programme report, component trial 1 of 2 — phase IIa dose-escalation studies (Shimokawa 2002): fasudil significantly prolonged maximum exercise time and time to 1-mm ST depression (both P < 0.01) in 45 patients, with similar results at higher doses in a further 22
cards.type: Component trial of a programme publication: phase IIa dose-escalation studies (45 + 22 patients) reported within PMID 12409984 — one of the 2 publications of this shelf's base
cards.people: Patients with stable effort angina in the phase IIa studies of a multicentre phase II programme: 45 patients received increasing doses of fasudil (5, 10 and 20 mg three times daily, each for 2 weeks) after a 2-week washout of anti-anginal drugs; higher doses (20 and 40 mg three times daily) were subsequently tested in a further 22 patients in the same manner. This card and the next are the two component trials of ONE publication — not two publications.
cards.result: Fasudil treatment significantly prolonged the maximum exercise time and the time to the onset of 1-mm ST-segment depression on treadmill exercise testing (both P < 0.01), whereas blood pressure and heart rate during exercise were unchanged before and after treatment. The higher-dose study in 22 patients gave similar positive results. Fasudil was well tolerated without any serious adverse reactions.
cards.watchOut: Open dose-escalation studies without a placebo group: they show a within-patient exercise effect and tolerability, not a controlled comparison. Carded separately only so the 3-component-trial structure of the 2-publication base is visible on the face.
cards.source: Shimokawa H et al. Anti-anginal effect of fasudil, a Rho-kinase inhibitor, in patients with stable effort angina: a multicenter study. Journal of cardiovascular pharmacology. 2002. cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Base, stated exactly: publication 1 (PMID 16286163) is the US double-blind placebo-controlled phase 2 trial (84 randomised) — time to ST depression significantly prolonged, exercise duration only numerically greater, angina frequency and nitroglycerin use not significantly different. Publication 2 (PMID 12409984) reports the Japanese phase IIa dose-escalation studies (45 + 22 patients) and the phase IIb double-blind dose-ranging trial (125 patients) — exercise time and time to ST depression prolonged, with a significant dose–response. That is the entire oral stable-angina base: 2 publications, 3 component trials. The intracoronary fasudil studies in vasospastic and microvascular angina (PMIDs 11927519, 12570938, 17414222) are a different route and different questions; they are not counted here and have not been merged into this shelf. Fasudil is approved in Japan for cerebral vasospasm, not for angina anywhere. All endpoints are surrogate exercise measures.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Omapatrilat vs enalapril (DISCONTINUED programme): better blood-pressure lowering and non-inferior heart-failure outcomes, at angioedema 2.17% vs 0.68% — never marketed
shelves.question: In adults with hypertension or chronic heart failure, does the vasopeptidase (ACE + neutral-endopeptidase) inhibitor omapatrilat, compared with enalapril, lower blood pressure and reduce death or heart-failure hospitalisation — and what is its angioedema cost?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Angioedema · Antihypertensive Agents · Double-Blind Method · Enalapril · Female · Humans · Hypertension · Male · Metalloendopeptidases · Middle Aged · Pyridines · Thiazepines · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: SPLIT — a discontinued, never-marketed programme whose efficacy and harm are both real. OVERTURE (5,770 heart-failure patients): the primary composite of death or heart-failure hospitalisation occurred in 914 patients on omapatrilat vs 973 on enalapril (hazard ratio 0.94, 95% CI 0.86 to 1.03, P = 0.187) — prespecified non-inferiority met, superiority not met. OCTAVE (25,302 hypertension patients): omapatrilat lowered systolic blood pressure 3.6 mm Hg more than enalapril at week 8, with less adjunctive therapy by week 24 (19% vs 27%) — but angioedema occurred in 2.17% on omapatrilat vs 0.68% on enalapril, the risk that ended the programme. A single-dose haemodynamic study is carded as mechanism support only. Omapatrilat was never marketed; its development was abandoned over the angioedema risk OCTAVE quantifies, and that history leads this shelf.

cards.headline: OVERTURE (Packer 2002): death or heart-failure hospitalisation in 914 patients on omapatrilat vs 973 on enalapril (hazard ratio 0.94, P = 0.187) — non-inferiority met, superiority not met
cards.summary: OVERTURE (Packer 2002): death or heart-failure hospitalisation in 914 patients on omapatrilat vs 973 on enalapril (hazard ratio 0.94, P = 0.187) — non-inferiority met, superiority not met
cards.type: Randomised double-blind trial (OVERTURE), omapatrilat 40 mg once daily vs enalapril 10 mg twice daily in chronic heart failure
cards.people: 5,770 patients with New York Heart Association class II to IV heart failure, randomly assigned to double-blind enalapril 10 mg twice daily (n=2,884) or omapatrilat 40 mg once daily (n=2,886) for a mean of 14.5 months.
cards.result: A primary endpoint event (death or hospitalisation for heart failure requiring intravenous treatment) was achieved in 973 patients in the enalapril group and 914 in the omapatrilat group (hazard ratio 0.94; 95% CI 0.86 to 1.03, P = 0.187) — a result that fulfilled prespecified criteria for non-inferiority but not for superiority. The omapatrilat group also had a 9% relative lower risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalisation (P = 0.024) and a 6% relative lower risk of death (P = 0.339); a post hoc analysis using the SOLVD definition (all heart-failure hospitalisations) showed an 11% relative lower risk on omapatrilat (nominal P = 0.012). The hazard ratio and the percentage differences drawn from it are relative measures; the absolute event counts are 914 vs 973 patients, as printed above.
cards.watchOut: The trial's own conclusion is non-inferiority, not superiority: the favourable secondary and post hoc analyses do not convert the primary result, and they are labelled post hoc/secondary on this card.
cards.source: Packer M et al. Comparison of omapatrilat and enalapril in patients with chronic heart failure: the Omapatrilat Versus Enalapril Randomized Trial of Utility in Reducing Events (OVERTURE). Circulation. 2002. PMID: 12186794. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: OCTAVE (Kostis 2004): omapatrilat lowered systolic blood pressure 3.6 mm Hg more than enalapril at week 8 — and caused angioedema in 2.17% vs 0.68%, the risk that ended the programme
cards.summary: OCTAVE (Kostis 2004): omapatrilat lowered systolic blood pressure 3.6 mm Hg more than enalapril at week 8 — and caused angioedema in 2.17% vs 0.68%, the risk that ended the programme
cards.type: Multicentre randomised double-blind active-controlled trial (OCTAVE), omapatrilat vs enalapril in hypertension
cards.people: 25,302 patients with untreated or uncontrolled hypertension in a multicentre randomised double-blind active-controlled 24-week trial at 3,298 office-based sites in 12 countries, randomised to omapatrilat or enalapril as initial therapy, as replacement for existing therapy, or in addition to existing therapy, force-titrated to a maximum of omapatrilat 80 mg or enalapril 40 mg once daily.
cards.result: Omapatrilat reduced systolic blood pressure 3.6 mm Hg more than enalapril at week 8, and was associated with less use of adjunctive antihypertensive therapy by week 24 (19% vs 27%; P < 0.001 for both comparisons); patients on omapatrilat were more likely to reach blood-pressure target. Angioedema was more frequent with omapatrilat than enalapril (2.17% vs 0.68% — absolute rates as printed). Two omapatrilat-treated subjects experienced angioedema with airway compromise, which was successfully treated; life-threatening angioedema was rare.
cards.watchOut: The efficacy and the decisive harm live in the same trial: superior blood-pressure lowering alongside a roughly threefold absolute angioedema excess (2.17% vs 0.68%). Omapatrilat was never marketed — its development was abandoned over this risk.
cards.source: Kostis JB et al. Omapatrilat and enalapril in patients with hypertension: the Omapatrilat Cardiovascular Treatment vs. Enalapril (OCTAVE) trial. American journal of hypertension. 2004. PMID: 14751650. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Single-dose haemodynamic study (Klapholz 2001) — support for mechanism only: single doses of omapatrilat 25 and 50 mg reduced mean pulmonary capillary wedge pressure by approximately 6 mm Hg at 4–6 hours vs placebo (not chronic efficacy)
cards.summary: Single-dose haemodynamic study (Klapholz 2001) — support for mechanism only: single doses of omapatrilat 25 and 50 mg reduced mean pulmonary capillary wedge pressure by approximately 6 mm Hg at 4–6 hours vs placebo (not chronic efficacy)
cards.type: Single-dose double-blind placebo-controlled sequential-panel haemodynamic study — mechanism support only, not an efficacy anchor
cards.people: Patients with heart failure (New York Heart Association class II to IV) and resting left ventricular ejection fraction at most 40%, enrolled in a double-blind placebo-controlled sequential-panel study of single oral doses of omapatrilat (1, 2.5, 5, 10, 25 or 50 mg) with haemodynamic assessment for 24 hours; the abstract prints no total N and none is claimed here.
cards.result: At 4 to 6 hours after dosing, the 25 mg and 50 mg doses of omapatrilat, compared with placebo, reduced mean pulmonary capillary wedge pressure by approximately 6 mm Hg (from 20 and 23 mm Hg at baseline to 14 and 16 mm Hg). The 50 mg dose maintained an approximately 2.5 mm Hg reduction vs placebo at 24 hours. Omapatrilat also improved cardiac index, systemic vascular resistance, stroke volume index and mean arterial pressure, with a trend to peak increases in plasma atrial natriuretic peptide and cyclic guanosine monophosphate by 2 hours at the 25 and 50 mg doses, and was well tolerated.
cards.watchOut: A single-dose study: it shows the drug moves haemodynamics acutely and supports the mechanism; it says nothing about chronic efficacy or safety and is never load-bearing on this shelf.
cards.source: Klapholz M et al. Effects of omapatrilat on hemodynamics and safety in patients with heart failure. The American journal of cardiology. 2001. PMID: 11564390. cards.headline: Synthesis: the omapatrilat programme in one place — superior blood-pressure lowering (OCTAVE), non-inferior but not superior heart-failure outcomes (OVERTURE), and an angioedema excess (2.17% vs 0.68%) that ended development; the drug was never marketed

cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Two questions live inside this one programme shelf, worded at programme level: hypertension efficacy and safety (OCTAVE, 25,302 patients) and heart-failure outcomes (OVERTURE, 5,770 patients). OVERTURE met non-inferiority against enalapril on death or heart-failure hospitalisation (914 vs 973 events; hazard ratio 0.94) without superiority; OCTAVE showed 3.6 mm Hg greater systolic lowering with less adjunctive therapy, at the cost of angioedema in 2.17% vs 0.68%. The single-dose haemodynamic study is mechanism support only. Omapatrilat, a combined ACE and neutral-endopeptidase (vasopeptidase) inhibitor, was never marketed — development was abandoned over the angioedema risk. The successor sacubitril–valsartan questions are homed on their own shelves and are not re-carded here.

shelves.title: Colestipol in hypercholesterolaemia: relative LDL reductions of 16.3–27.2% by dose vs 2.7% on placebo (n=152) — pre-statin-era, surrogate endpoints only; n=27 single-blind report labelled, not load-bearing
shelves.question: In adults with moderate-to-severe primary hypercholesterolaemia, does the bile-acid sequestrant colestipol, compared with placebo or clofibrate, lower total and LDL cholesterol?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Cholesterol · Colestipol · Double-Blind Method · Drug Evaluation · Female · Humans · Hypercholesterolemia · Lipoproteins · Male · Middle Aged · Triglycerides · United States
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit) on the surrogate lipid endpoint, on an old, pre-statin-era trial base (1981–1992) with no outcomes trial. The load-bearing trial is the double-blind dose-ranging study (152 randomised, 141 completing): relative LDL cholesterol reductions of 16.3%, 22.8% and 27.2% at 5, 10 and 15 g/day vs 2.7% on placebo (P < 0.001). The 65-patient comparison found mean total cholesterol falling from 333 to 266 mg/dL on colestipol at 6 months (P < 0.01), with more responders to colestipol than to clofibrate. The 1981 Metabolism comparison (n=27, single-blind) is labelled on its card and is never load-bearing; in it, colestipol lowered total cholesterol 25% relative and LDL cholesterol 31% relative while VLDL triglyceride rose — the triglyceride rise and gastrointestinal tolerability are the harm side of this class. All percentage reductions on this shelf drawn from relative measures are labelled relative, with absolute changes printed beside them where the reports give them.

cards.summary: Low-dose dose-ranging RCT (Superko 1992): relative LDL cholesterol reductions of 16.3%, 22.8% and 27.2% at 5, 10 and 15 g/day vs 2.7% on placebo (P < 0.001)
cards.type: Double-blind placebo-controlled randomised dose-ranging trial, low-dose colestipol 5, 10 or 15 g/day vs placebo
cards.people: 152 patients with moderate hypercholesterolaemia (54 women and 98 men; plasma LDL cholesterol greater than 4 mmol/L (155 mg/dL) and triglycerides less than 2.82 mmol/L (250 mg/dL)), placed on the American Heart Association step I diet for 6 weeks and then randomised to placebo or colestipol 5, 10 or 15 g/day in two divided doses for 12 weeks; 141 patients completed all aspects of the study. Double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial — the load-bearing anchor of this shelf.
cards.result: LDL cholesterol fell by 0.10 mmol/L (about 4 mg/dL) (2.7% relative reduction) on placebo, and by 0.65 mmol/L (about 25 mg/dL) (16.3% relative), 0.98 mmol/L (about 38 mg/dL) (22.8% relative) and 1.17 mmol/L (about 45 mg/dL) (27.2% relative) at 5, 10 and 15 g/day of colestipol (P < 0.001) — percentages are relative reductions, printed beside the absolute changes. Similar changes were observed in total cholesterol and apolipoprotein B. A dose of 5 g/day achieved 51% of the LDL reduction noted with 15 g/day. Modest but insignificant changes in plasma triglycerides occurred, and HDL cholesterol remained unchanged.
cards.watchOut: A 12-week surrogate-endpoint trial from 1992, before the statin era: it establishes dose-related LDL lowering, including at low doses, and says nothing about cardiovascular events.
cards.source: Superko HR et al. Effectiveness of low-dose colestipol therapy in patients with moderate hypercholesterolemia. The American journal of cardiology. 1992. PMID: 1626496. cards.headline: Randomised comparison vs clofibrate and placebo resin (Seplowitz 1981): mean total cholesterol fell from 333 to 266 mg/dL on colestipol at 6 months (P < 0.01), with more responders to colestipol than to clofibrate
cards.summary: Randomised comparison vs clofibrate and placebo resin (Seplowitz 1981): mean total cholesterol fell from 333 to 266 mg/dL on colestipol at 6 months (P < 0.01), with more responders to colestipol than to clofibrate
cards.type: Randomised comparison, colestipol vs clofibrate vs placebo resin over 9 months
cards.people: 65 patients with primary hypercholesterolaemia, randomly assigned to colestipol (in progressive doses of 15, 20 and 30 g/day), clofibrate 2 g/day, or placebo resin, with lipoprotein levels at months 0, 2, 4, 6 and 9; the colestipol group received both colestipol and clofibrate during months 7 through 9.
cards.result: After 6 months of treatment, mean plasma total cholesterol fell from 333 to 266 mg/dL on colestipol (P < 0.01) and from 329 to 270 mg/dL on clofibrate (P < 0.05); more patients responded to colestipol than to clofibrate. Both drugs also produced significant reductions in LDL cholesterol, and clofibrate lowered plasma triglycerides as well. HDL cholesterol did not change significantly on either medication, and the placebo group showed no change in any parameter. No significant difference was observed between 15 g/day of colestipol and the higher doses, and adding clofibrate to colestipol did not enhance its cholesterol-lowering action.
cards.watchOut: A 1981 pre-statin-era comparison against clofibrate, itself long superseded; the months 7–9 combination phase is a within-study add-on, not a separate trial, and the 6-month figures above precede it.
cards.source: Seplowitz AH et al. Comparison of the effects of colestipol hydrochloride and clofibrate on plasma lipids and lipoproteins in the treatment of hypercholesterolemia. cards.headline: Small single-blind comparison (Crouse 1981, n=27 — LABELLED, never load-bearing): colestipol 30 g/day lowered total cholesterol 25% relative and LDL cholesterol 31% relative over 8 months, while VLDL triglyceride rose

cards.type: Randomised single-blind comparison (n=27, LABELLED, never load-bearing), colestipol vs clofibrate vs placebo over 8 months
cards.people: 27 patients with hypercholesterolaemia and normal triglyceride concentrations, randomised into three groups comparing colestipol, clofibrate and avicel powder placebo in a SINGLE-BLIND protocol over 8 months. N = 27 and single-blind, both printed on the face: this report is labelled and is NEVER load-bearing — this shelf rests on the 152-patient dose-ranging trial and the 65-patient comparison above.
cards.result: Mean pretreatment LDL cholesterol was 250 mg/dL and VLDL triglyceride 68 mg/dL. Colestipol 30 g/day lowered total cholesterol by 25% relative and LDL cholesterol by 31% relative, while VLDL triglyceride rose. Overall, clofibrate lowered total cholesterol by 13% relative and LDL cholesterol by 12% relative, while lowering VLDL triglyceride 21% relative and VLDL cholesterol 50% relative; in seven of nine clofibrate patients the lowering was more pronounced (total cholesterol 17% relative, LDL cholesterol 19% relative), and two patients did not respond to clofibrate. HDL cholesterol was not affected by either drug. All percentages on this card are relative changes, as printed in the report.
cards.watchOut: Twenty-seven patients, single-blind, at a high dose (30 g/day): carded to complete the record and because its triglyceride-rise finding is part of the harm picture — it supports no part of this shelf's claim, which rests on the two larger reports.

cards.headline: Synthesis: a pre-statin-era base (1981–1992) shows dose-related LDL lowering with colestipol — relative reductions up to 27.2% at 15 g/day vs 2.7% on placebo — on surrogate lipid endpoints only, with no outcomes trial; the n=27 single-blind report is labelled and was never load-bearing
cards.summary: Synthesis: a pre-statin-era base (1981–1992) shows dose-related LDL lowering with colestipol — relative reductions up to 27.2% at 15 g/day vs 2.7% on placebo — on surrogate lipid endpoints only, with no outcomes trial; the n=27 single-blind report is labelled and was never load-bearing
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: The load-bearing evidence is the 152-patient double-blind dose-ranging trial (relative LDL reductions 16.3%, 22.8% and 27.2% at 5, 10 and 15 g/day vs 2.7% on placebo, with absolute falls of 0.65 mmol/L (about 25 mg/dL), 0.98 mmol/L (about 38 mg/dL) and 1.17 mmol/L (about 45 mg/dL) vs 0.10 mmol/L (about 4 mg/dL)), supported by the 65-patient comparison (total cholesterol 333 to 266 mg/dL at 6 months). The 27-patient single-blind 1981 report is carded, labelled, and never load-bearing. Triglyceride rise (seen at 30 g/day in the small report) and gastrointestinal tolerability are the harm side; HDL cholesterol did not change in any report. No trial in this base measured cardiovascular events — the endpoint level and the era are printed on the face of this shelf. The bile-acid-sequestrant neighbours are different questions (colesevelam in type 2 diabetes, live #2053; bile-acid diarrhoea shelves) and are cross-pointed only.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Istaroxime in acute heart failure: wedge pressure, E/e' and blood pressure all improved over 6-24 hours in three small trials (HORIZON-HF, SEISMiC) — no outcomes trial exists and the drug is unapproved
shelves.question: In patients hospitalised with acute heart failure — including heart-failure-related pre-cardiogenic shock, SCAI stage B — does the intravenous inotrope/lusitrope istaroxime, compared with placebo, improve haemodynamics, diastolic function and blood pressure?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Heart Failure · Shock, Cardiogenic · Cardiotonic Agents · Etiocholanolone · Double-Blind Method
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) — on short-term haemodynamics only. Three distinct randomised placebo-controlled trials, in three different acute-heart-failure populations that must not be pooled, all show the same 6- to 24-hour pattern: pulmonary capillary wedge pressure fell (-3.2, -3.3 and -4.7 mm Hg at 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 µg/kg/min vs 0.0 mm Hg on placebo in HORIZON-HF, n=120), the diastolic E/e' ratio improved at 24 hours (-4.55 vs -1.55 and -3.16 vs -1.08 in acute heart failure with LVEF ≤40%, n=120), and in SCAI stage B pre-cardiogenic shock systolic blood pressure rose more than on placebo (adjusted 6-hour AUC 53.1 vs 30.9 mm Hg·hour, P=0.017; SEISMiC, n=60) — with heart rate falling rather than rising, the opposite pattern to conventional inotropes. NO OUTCOMES TRIAL EXISTS: every endpoint is a haemodynamic or echocardiographic surrogate, and dyspnoea and NT-proBNP did not separate from placebo where measured. Istaroxime is investigational and unapproved. A 2025 prolonged-infusion (up to 60-hour) report from the same pre-shock programme is carded as programme support only and is not counted in the three-trial base.

cards.headline: HORIZON-HF RCT (Gheorghiade 2008): istaroxime lowered pulmonary capillary wedge pressure at all three doses (-3.2, -3.3 and -4.7 mm Hg vs 0.0 on placebo) over a 6-hour infusion, while raising systolic blood pressure and lowering heart rate
cards.summary: HORIZON-HF RCT (Gheorghiade 2008): istaroxime lowered pulmonary capillary wedge pressure at all three doses (-3.2, -3.3 and -4.7 mm Hg vs 0.0 on placebo) over a 6-hour infusion, while raising systolic blood pressure and lowering heart rate
cards.type: Randomised controlled trial (HORIZON-HF), istaroxime 0.5/1.0/1.5 µg/kg/min vs placebo, 6-hour infusion
cards.people: 120 patients admitted with heart failure and reduced systolic function, instrumented with a pulmonary artery catheter within 48 hours of admission; three sequential cohorts of 40 randomised 3:1 to istaroxime (0.5, 1.0 or 1.5 µg/kg/min) or placebo for 6 hours.
cards.result: All istaroxime doses lowered pulmonary capillary wedge pressure, the primary endpoint (mean -3.2 ± 6.8, -3.3 ± 5.5 and -4.7 ± 5.9 mm Hg vs 0.0 ± 3.6 mm Hg on placebo; P < 0.05 for all doses). Istaroxime significantly decreased heart rate and increased systolic blood pressure. Cardiac index increased and left ventricular end-diastolic volume decreased significantly only at 1.5 µg/kg/min. There were no changes in neurohormones, renal function or troponin I. Adverse events were not life-threatening and were dose-related.
cards.watchOut: A 6-hour haemodynamic study: every endpoint is a surrogate (wedge pressure, blood pressure, heart rate, volumes), and there is no mortality, hospitalisation or symptom outcome here or anywhere in this programme.
cards.source: Gheorghiade M et al. Hemodynamic, echocardiographic, and neurohormonal effects of istaroxime, a novel intravenous inotropic and lusitropic agent: a randomized controlled trial in patients hospitalized with heart failure. Journal of the American College of Cardiology. 2008. PMID: 18534276. Registry ID: NCT00616161. cards.headline: 24-hour infusion RCT (Carubelli 2020): istaroxime improved the diastolic E/e' ratio at 24 hours at both doses (-4.55 vs -1.55, P=0.029; -3.16 vs -1.08, P=0.009), but dyspnoea and NT-proBNP improved in all groups with no significant between-group difference
cards.summary: 24-hour infusion RCT (Carubelli 2020): istaroxime improved the diastolic E/e' ratio at 24 hours at both doses (-4.55 vs -1.55, P=0.029; -3.16 vs -1.08, P=0.009), but dyspnoea and NT-proBNP improved in all groups with no significant between-group difference
cards.type: Randomised placebo-controlled trial, 24-hour istaroxime infusion in acute heart failure with LVEF ≤40%
cards.people: 120 patients hospitalised for acute heart failure with LVEF ≤40% and E/e' >10, randomised to a 24-hour infusion of placebo or istaroxime 0.5 µg/kg/min (cohort 1: placebo n=19, istaroxime n=41) or 1.0 µg/kg/min (cohort 2: placebo n=20, istaroxime n=40).
cards.result: The primary endpoint, change in E/e' ratio from baseline to 24 hours, fell more with istaroxime than placebo in both cohorts (cohort 1: -4.55 ± 4.75 vs -1.55 ± 4.11, P=0.029; cohort 2: -3.16 ± 2.59 vs -1.08 ± 2.72, P=0.009). Both doses significantly increased stroke volume index and decreased heart rate; systolic blood pressure rose, significantly at the high dose. Self-reported dyspnoea and NT-proBNP improved in all groups without significant differences between istaroxime and placebo. Serious cardiac adverse events did not differ between groups; the most common adverse events were injection-site reactions and gastrointestinal events, the latter mainly at 1.0 µg/kg/min.
cards.watchOut: An echocardiographic surrogate primary endpoint over 24 hours; the patient-felt outcomes in the same trial (dyspnoea, NT-proBNP) did not separate from placebo.

cards.headline: SEISMiC RCT (Metra 2022): in acute-heart-failure-related pre-cardiogenic shock (SCAI stage B), istaroxime raised systolic blood pressure more than placebo over 6 hours (adjusted AUC 53.1 vs 30.9 mm Hg·hour, P=0.017), with more nausea, vomiting and infusion-site pain
cards.summary: SEISMiC RCT (Metra 2022): in acute-heart-failure-related pre-cardiogenic shock (SCAI stage B), istaroxime raised systolic blood pressure more than placebo over 6 hours (adjusted AUC 53.1 vs 30.9 mm Hg·hour, P=0.017), with more nausea, vomiting and infusion-site pain
cards.type: Phase 2a multicentre randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (SEISMiC), pre-cardiogenic shock (SCAI stage B)
cards.people: 60 patients hospitalised with acute heart failure without acute myocardial infarction and pre-cardiogenic shock — systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg without hypoperfusion, venous lactate ≥2 mmol/L (approx. 18 mg/dL) and/or mechanical or inotropic support — randomised to istaroxime 1.0-1.5 µg/kg/min or placebo for 24 hours.
cards.result: The primary endpoint, adjusted area under the curve for systolic blood pressure change to 6 hours, was 53.1 (SE 6.88) vs 30.9 (SE 6.76) mm Hg·hour on istaroxime vs placebo (P=0.017); the adjusted 24-hour AUC was 291.2 vs 208.7 mm Hg·hour (P=0.025). At 24 hours cardiac index (+0.21 L/min/m2, P=0.016), left atrial area (-1.8 cm2, P=0.008) and left ventricular end-systolic volume (-12.0 mL, P=0.034) improved with istaroxime. There were no significant differences in pulse pressure, laboratory measurements, serious adverse events or adverse events except more nausea, vomiting and infusion-site pain on istaroxime. This was a phase 2a study.
cards.watchOut: Only 60 patients and a 6-hour blood-pressure primary endpoint: this is a pre-shock population defined by blood pressure and lactate, not established cardiogenic shock, and no clinical outcome was tested.
cards.source: Metra M et al. Safety and efficacy of istaroxime in patients with acute heart failure-related pre-cardiogenic shock - a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group study (SEISMiC). cards.headline: Synthesis: three distinct randomised trials across the acute-heart-failure spectrum — decompensated HFrEF (HORIZON-HF, n=120), acute heart failure with diastolic dysfunction (n=120) and SCAI stage B pre-cardiogenic shock (SEISMiC, n=60) — all show the same short-term haemodynamic pattern (wedge pressure and heart rate down, systolic blood pressure up), and none tests a clinical outcome
cards.summary: Synthesis: three distinct randomised trials across the acute-heart-failure spectrum — decompensated HFrEF (HORIZON-HF, n=120), acute heart failure with diastolic dysfunction (n=120) and SCAI stage B pre-cardiogenic shock (SEISMiC, n=60) — all show the same short-term haemodynamic pattern (wedge pressure and heart rate down, systolic blood pressure up), and none tests a clinical outcome
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: The populations differ and are not pooled into one acute-heart-failure claim. Every primary endpoint is a haemodynamic or echocardiographic surrogate measured over 6 to 24 hours (wedge pressure -3.2 to -4.7 mm Hg vs 0.0; E/e' -4.55 vs -1.55 and -3.16 vs -1.08; systolic blood pressure AUC 53.1 vs 30.9 mm Hg·hour). Where patient-felt measures were taken, dyspnoea and NT-proBNP did not separate from placebo. No outcomes trial of istaroxime exists — no mortality, hospitalisation or length-of-stay result is carded anywhere on this shelf. Istaroxime is investigational and unapproved. The 2025 prolonged-infusion report is programme support for the same pre-shock programme, not a fourth trial.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: CMR chamber reference ranges: LV end-diastolic volume 160 ± 29 mL in men vs 135 ± 26 mL in women (SSFP), UK Biobank LV ejection fraction 61% women vs 58% men — ranges must be normalised to sex, body size and age
shelves.question: In healthy adults, what are the cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) reference ranges for cardiac chamber structure and function — left- and right-ventricular volumes, mass and ejection fraction, and atrial dimensions, indexed to body surface area — by age and sex, and how much do cohort, contouring convention and indexing move the limits of normal?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Age Factors · Aged · Female · Humans · Magnetic Resonance Imaging · Male · Middle Aged · Reference Values · Sex Factors · Stroke Volume · Ventricular Function, Left · Ventricular Function, Right
shelves.balance: Textbook framing: Guyton & Hall, cardiac muscle and circulation chapters — the framing is brief, and this shelf rests chiefly on the primary CMR reference literature, and says so. Three independent steady-state free-precession (SSFP) cohorts: 108 healthy volunteers with manually analysed LV, RV and left-atrial dimensions (Hudsmith 2005 — LV end-diastolic volume 160 ± 29 mL in men vs 135 ± 26 mL in women); a normalised-range modelling study whose fetched abstract prints no cohort N and no numeric ranges, carded for its normalisation principle only (Maceira 2006); and the UK Biobank cohort (Petersen 2017 — 5,065 scanned at 1.5 T, 804 in the healthy Caucasian reference cohort aged 45-74, LV ejection fraction 61 ± 5% in women vs 58 ± 5% in men, indexed LV mass 42 ± 7 vs 53 ± 9 g/m2). Contouring convention (papillary muscles and trabeculations) and indexing move the limits materially and are stated per card; SSFP CMR values are not interchangeable with echocardiographic volumes — the speckle-tracking strain shelf #7163 is the echo cross-point, a different modality and measure. The stamp is graded down: one of three records prints no numbers in its abstract, and the largest cohort is Caucasian and aged 45-74 only. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING.

cards.headline: Hudsmith 2005: SSFP CMR in 108 healthy volunteers — LV end-diastolic volume 160 ± 29 mL in men vs 135 ± 26 mL in women; RV end-diastolic volume 190 ± 33 vs 148 ± 35 mL
cards.summary: Hudsmith 2005: SSFP CMR in 108 healthy volunteers — LV end-diastolic volume 160 ± 29 mL in men vs 135 ± 26 mL in women; RV end-diastolic volume 190 ± 33 vs 148 ± 35 mL
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (SSFP CMR reference database, healthy volunteers)
cards.people: 108 healthy volunteers (63 men, 45 women) across a wide age range, imaged with steady-state free-precession CMR; manual analysis by two experienced observers, covering left- and right-ventricular volumes, LV mass and left-atrial dimensions.
cards.result: Ventricular volumes and LV mass were larger in men: LV end-diastolic volume 160 ± 29 mL vs 135 ± 26 mL, LV end-systolic volume 50 ± 16 vs 42 ± 12 mL, RV end-diastolic volume 190 ± 33 vs 148 ± 35 mL and RV end-systolic volume 78 ± 20 vs 56 ± 18 mL (p<0.05 for all). Normalising to body surface area removed the statistical sex differences for LV volumes, but not for LV mass or RV volumes. With age, men showed significant decreases in volume and mass indices for both ventricles, while women's values remained unchanged. Maximal left-atrial volume was 103 ± 30 mL in men vs 89 ± 21 mL in women (p=0.01) and left-atrial stroke volume 58 ± 23 vs 48 ± 15 mL (p=0.01), with no sex difference in left-atrial ejection fraction.
cards.watchOut: Manual contouring by two observers in the early SSFP era: whether papillary muscles and trabeculations are included in mass or volume moves both, so these ranges travel with their contouring convention and are not interchangeable with later automated or echocardiographic values.
cards.source: Hudsmith LE et al. Normal human left and right ventricular and left atrial dimensions using steady state free precession magnetic resonance imaging. Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance. 2005. PMID: 16353438. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Maceira 2006: normalised LV ranges must be modelled against sex, body surface area AND age together — the fetched record prints no cohort N and no numeric ranges, and none are claimed
cards.summary: Maceira 2006: normalised LV ranges must be modelled against sex, body surface area AND age together — the fetched record prints no cohort N and no numeric ranges, and none are claimed
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (SSFP CMR normalised LV reference ranges — modelling report)
cards.people: Healthy volunteers imaged with state-of-the-art SSFP cardiovascular magnetic resonance to define normal left-ventricular volumes and systolic and diastolic function; the cohort size is not printed in the fetched abstract.
cards.result: Normalised CMR reference ranges were modelled and displayed in graphical form for clinical use, with normalisation for body surface area, sex and age together. The authors' central point is methodological: determination of normality, or of the severity of abnormality, depends on using reference ranges normalised to all three variables. The fetched record states this modelling approach and its purpose; it does not print the cohort N or the numeric range limits, and this card claims none.
cards.watchOut: Carded for the normalisation principle only: a single pooled 'normal LV volume' that ignores sex, body size and age is exactly what this study argues against. Any numeric limit must come from the datasets that print numbers (the other two cards).
cards.source: Maceira AM et al. Normalized left ventricular systolic and diastolic function by steady state free precession cardiovascular magnetic resonance. cards.headline: UK Biobank (Petersen 2017): reference ranges for all four chambers from 804 healthy Caucasian adults aged 45-74 (of 5,065 scanned) — LV ejection fraction 61 ± 5% in women vs 58 ± 5% in men; indexed LV mass 42 ± 7 vs 53 ± 9 g/m2
cards.summary: UK Biobank (Petersen 2017): reference ranges for all four chambers from 804 healthy Caucasian adults aged 45-74 (of 5,065 scanned) — LV ejection fraction 61 ± 5% in women vs 58 ± 5% in men; indexed LV mass 42 ± 7 vs 53 ± 9 g/m2
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (UK Biobank CMR reference ranges, all four chambers)
cards.people: 5,065 UK Biobank participants underwent SSFP CMR at 1.5 T with manual analysis of all four chambers; after excluding non-Caucasian ethnicity, known cardiovascular disease and other conditions affecting chamber size and function, 804 participants (16.2%, as published) formed the healthy reference cohort, with ranges stratified by sex and age band (45-54, 55-64, 65-74 years).
cards.result: LV volumes were larger in men for absolute and indexed values and mostly smaller with advancing age in both sexes. LV ejection fraction was significantly greater in women than men (mean ± SD 61 ± 5% vs 58 ± 5%) and remained static with age. Indexed LV mass was significantly higher in men (53 ± 9 g/m2) than women (42 ± 7 g/m2); in older age groups LV mass was lower in men but virtually unchanged in women. RV volumes were significantly larger in men, absolute and indexed, and smaller with advancing age; RV ejection fraction rose with age in women only. Left-atrial maximal volume and stroke volume were larger in men in absolute values but not indexed values, with similar LA ejection fraction; right-atrial maximal volume was larger in men absolute and indexed, and RA ejection fraction higher in women.
cards.watchOut: The reference cohort is Caucasian and aged 45-74 only — these are not young-adult or multi-ethnic ranges, and the healthy subset (804) is far smaller than the scanned total (5,065); both numbers are printed so the subset is not mistaken for the whole.
cards.source: Petersen SE et al. Reference ranges for cardiac structure and function using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in Caucasians from the UK Biobank population cohort. Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance. 2017. PMID: 28178995. Registry ID: none in the record.
