cards.headline: Statin add-on trial (Ladenson 2010, NEJM): LDL fell from 141 mg/dL (3.6 mmol/L) to 127 mg/dL (3.3 mmol/L) on placebo and 113, 99 and 94 mg/dL (2.9, 2.6, 2.4 mmol/L) on eprotirome 25, 50 and 100 µg — mean reductions 7%, 22%, 28% and 32% relative
cards.summary: Statin add-on trial (Ladenson 2010, NEJM): LDL fell from 141 mg/dL (3.6 mmol/L) to 127 mg/dL (3.3 mmol/L) on placebo and 113, 99 and 94 mg/dL (2.9, 2.6, 2.4 mmol/L) on eprotirome 25, 50 and 100 µg — mean reductions 7%, 22%, 28% and 32% relative
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, eprotirome added to statin therapy in hypercholesterolaemia
cards.people: Patients with hypercholesterolaemia already receiving simvastatin or atorvastatin, in a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind multicentre trial of eprotirome 25, 50 or 100 µg daily or placebo added to statin treatment for 12 weeks. The fetched record prints no randomised N, and none is claimed on this card.
cards.result: Mean serum LDL cholesterol fell from 141 mg/dL (3.6 mmol/L) at baseline to 127 mg/dL (3.3 mmol/L) with placebo and 113, 99 and 94 mg/dL (2.9, 2.6 and 2.4 mmol/L) with eprotirome 25, 50 and 100 µg — mean reductions from baseline of 7%, 22%, 28% and 32% (relative changes as published). Similar reductions were seen in apolipoprotein B, triglycerides and Lp(a). No adverse effects on heart or bone were detected over 12 weeks; thyrotropin and triiodothyronine did not change, although thyroxine decreased.
cards.watchOut: Twelve weeks and a surrogate endpoint, in the pre-termination era of the programme: the clean heart/bone picture here is short-term, and the later AKKA trial added significant liver-enzyme and bilirubin rises.
cards.source: Ladenson PW et al. Use of the thyroid hormone analogue eprotirome in statin-treated dyslipidemia. The New England journal of medicine. 2010. PMID: 20220185. Registry ID: NCT00593047. cards.headline: Primary-hypercholesterolaemia trial (Angelin 2015): LDL fell 23 ± 5% and 31 ± 4% relative on eprotirome 100 and 200 µg vs 2 ± 6% on placebo (P < 0.0001) — with low-grade liver-enzyme increases in most patients
cards.summary: Primary-hypercholesterolaemia trial (Angelin 2015): LDL fell 23 ± 5% and 31 ± 4% relative on eprotirome 100 and 200 µg vs 2 ± 6% on placebo (P < 0.0001) — with low-grade liver-enzyme increases in most patients
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, eprotirome in primary hypercholesterolaemia
cards.people: 98 patients with primary hypercholesterolaemia in a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study of eprotirome 100 or 200 µg daily or placebo for 12 weeks, after drug wash-out and dietary run-in.
cards.result: Serum LDL cholesterol fell by 23 ± 5% on 100 µg and 31 ± 4% on 200 µg versus 2 ± 6% on placebo (P < 0.0001) — relative changes as published — with similar reductions in non-HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B, no change in HDL cholesterol or apolipoprotein A-I, and considerable reductions in triglycerides and lipoprotein(a), particularly where baseline levels were elevated. There was no evidence of adverse effects on heart or bone and no change in thyrotropin or triiodothyronine, although thyroxine decreased; low-grade increases in liver enzymes were evident in most patients.
cards.watchOut: A 98-patient, 12-week surrogate-endpoint trial published after the programme had already been terminated: its LDL effect is real but it cannot speak to safety over the durations AKKA was designed for.

cards.headline: Synthesis: consistent LDL lowering that never became a drug — three short trials agree on the surrogate, and the programme was ended by dog cartilage damage plus a human liver signal
cards.summary: Synthesis: consistent LDL lowering that never became a drug — three short trials agree on the surrogate, and the programme was ended by dog cartilage damage plus a human liver signal
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (AKKA phase 3 remnant, 69 analysable of 236 randomised; NEJM statin add-on trial, N not printed in its record; 98-patient primary-hypercholesterolaemia trial).
cards.result: Eprotirome lowered LDL cholesterol dose-dependently wherever it was tested: −22% relative at 100 µg in the terminated AKKA phase 3 at 6 weeks, −28% and −32% relative at 50 and 100 µg added to statins at 12 weeks, and −31% relative at 200 µg in primary hypercholesterolaemia. Against that stand the facts that ended the programme: cartilage damage in dogs (the stated reason AKKA was terminated), significant rises in AST, ALT, conjugated bilirubin and GGT in AKKA, low-grade liver-enzyme increases in most patients in the 2015 trial, and falls in free thyroxine of 19–27%. No cardiovascular-outcomes trial exists and no product was marketed. The stamp is POSSIBLE (benefit) on the LDL surrogate alone, with the termination on the face.
cards.watchOut: Never cite AKKA as a completed phase 3 or its 69-patient remnant as phase-3 evidence of safety: the analysable base is 6 weeks, and the animal cartilage signal — not a human efficacy failure — is what stopped development.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.question: In adults with advanced chronic heart failure (NYHA class III–IV, ejection fraction ≤35%), does the non-selective beta-blocker bucindolol, compared with placebo, reduce mortality — and how does its record differ from the beta-blockers that succeeded (the BEST programme)?

shelves.balance: The null headline leads. BEST is the large beta-blocker heart-failure trial that did NOT show a survival benefit, in a class where other agents did — the class effect must not be borrowed for this molecule. BEST randomised 2,708 patients with NYHA class III–IV heart failure and LVEF ≤35% and was stopped on its data and safety monitoring board's recommendation at the seventh interim analysis: deaths 30% on bucindolol versus 33% on placebo, not significant (adjusted P = 0.13), with favourable secondary endpoints (cardiovascular death HR 0.86; death-or-transplantation HR 0.87 — relative measures) printed after the primary null. The two supporting anchors are small, short LVEF / haemodynamic (surrogate) trials, labelled as such. Bucindolol was never marketed for heart failure in the US. BEST's companion subgroup and genotype reports are further reports of the same trial and are not carded as separate evidence. PROPOSED STAMP: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) on mortality.

cards.type: Multicentre randomised double-blind placebo-controlled outcomes trial (BEST), bucindolol in advanced chronic heart failure
cards.people: 2,708 patients with advanced chronic heart failure — NYHA functional class III in 92% and class IV in 8%, left ventricular ejection fraction 35% or lower — randomised double-blind to bucindolol (1,354) or placebo (1,354) and followed for the primary endpoint of death from any cause; average follow-up 2.0 years at study termination.
cards.result: The data and safety monitoring board recommended stopping the trial after the seventh interim analysis, at which point there was no significant difference in mortality (unadjusted P = 0.16). On complete follow-up at termination there were 449 deaths on placebo (33%) and 411 on bucindolol (30%) — adjusted P = 0.13, not significant. The secondary endpoints favoured bucindolol: death from cardiovascular causes, hazard ratio 0.86 (95% CI 0.74 to 0.99), and heart transplantation or death, hazard ratio 0.87 (95% CI 0.77 to 0.99) — hazard ratios are relative measures. The authors concluded bucindolol resulted in no significant overall survival benefit in this population.
cards.watchOut: The primary endpoint is the headline: a stopped-early, non-significant mortality result. The significant secondary endpoints (cardiovascular death; death-or-transplantation) are printed here in full but do not convert a null primary into a survival benefit, and BEST's AF-subgroup, blood-pressure and genotype companion reports are reports of this same trial, not new evidence.
cards.source: Beta-Blocker Evaluation of Survival Trial Investigators et al. A trial of the beta-blocker bucindolol in patients with advanced chronic heart failure. The New England journal of medicine. 2001. PMID: 11386264. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Dose-response trial (Bristow 1994): dose-related LVEF improvement over 12 weeks — +7.8 ejection-fraction units on high-dose bucindolol vs +1.8 on placebo (P < 0.05) in 139 randomised patients (small, short, surrogate — labelled)
cards.summary: Dose-response trial (Bristow 1994): dose-related LVEF improvement over 12 weeks — +7.8 ejection-fraction units on high-dose bucindolol vs +1.8 on placebo (P < 0.05) in 139 randomised patients (small, short, surrogate — labelled)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind dose-response trial, bucindolol in heart failure from dilated cardiomyopathy (small, short, LVEF surrogate)
cards.people: 141 subjects with class II or III heart failure and LVEF ≤0.40 on ACE inhibitors, digoxin and diuretics were given a 12.5 mg bucindolol test dose; 139 (99 with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, 40 with ischaemic cardiomyopathy) tolerated it and were randomised to placebo or bucindolol 12.5, 50 or 200 mg/day for 12 weeks.
cards.result: Left ventricular function improved dose-dependently on bucindolol: radionuclide LVEF rose by 7.8 ejection-fraction units in the high-dose group versus 1.8 units on placebo (P < 0.05), a greater percentage of bucindolol-treated subjects gained 5 or more LVEF units, and all three bucindolol doses prevented deterioration (an LVEF decline of 5 or more units).
cards.watchOut: Small (139 randomised), 12 weeks, and a surrogate endpoint (LVEF): an ejection-fraction gain of this kind is exactly what BEST later failed to convert into a mortality benefit, and this card is never load-bearing for any survival claim.

cards.headline: Aetiology trial (Woodley 1991): bucindolol improved ejection fraction, filling pressure and symptom score overall in 49 patients — but within the ischaemic subgroup only left ventricular size improved significantly (small — labelled)
cards.summary: Aetiology trial (Woodley 1991): bucindolol improved ejection fraction, filling pressure and symptom score overall in 49 patients — but within the ischaemic subgroup only left ventricular size improved significantly (small — labelled)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind trial by aetiology, bucindolol in ischaemic vs idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (small, short, haemodynamic/surrogate)
cards.people: 49 patients with congestive heart failure from ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy (27) or idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (22), randomised double-blind, stratified by aetiology, to bucindolol or placebo for 12 weeks, with invasive and noninvasive testing at baseline and study end.
cards.result: Across all subjects, bucindolol significantly improved ejection fraction, left ventricular size and filling pressure, stroke work index, symptom score and central venous norepinephrine versus placebo. Most of these differences were attributable to the idiopathic subgroup: in the ischaemic subgroup, the only parameter with a statistically significant improvement on bucindolol was left ventricular size. The authors concluded beta-blockade may produce quantitatively different degrees of response in different kinds of heart muscle disease.
cards.watchOut: The smallest card on this shelf (49 patients, 12 weeks, surrogate and symptom measures): it explains why early enthusiasm existed — an idiopathic-cardiomyopathy-driven signal — and carries no weight against BEST's 2,708-patient mortality null.
cards.source: Woodley SL et al. Beta-blockade with bucindolol in heart failure caused by ischemic versus idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy. Circulation. 1991. PMID: 1683602. cards.headline: Synthesis: one definitive trial, one answer — bucindolol did not significantly reduce mortality in advanced heart failure, whatever the small LVEF trials showed
cards.summary: Synthesis: one definitive trial, one answer — bucindolol did not significantly reduce mortality in advanced heart failure, whatever the small LVEF trials showed
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (BEST n=2,708; dose-response trial n=139 randomised; aetiology trial n=49).
cards.result: BEST is the record: 30% mortality on bucindolol versus 33% on placebo over an average 2.0 years, adjusted P = 0.13, in a trial its monitoring board stopped at the seventh interim analysis. The favourable secondary endpoints (cardiovascular death HR 0.86; death-or-transplantation HR 0.87, relative measures) and the dose-related LVEF gains in two small 12-week trials (+7.8 units at high dose) are the whole of the positive record — surrogates and secondaries, against a null primary in the only adequately powered trial. Bucindolol was never marketed for heart failure in the US, and its result must not be read across to the beta-blockers whose own large trials succeeded. The stamp is LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) on mortality.
cards.watchOut: Class-effect borrowing is the specific error this shelf exists to prevent: metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol and carvedilol have their own positive trials homed elsewhere; bucindolol has BEST, and BEST was null on its primary endpoint.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Oral enoximone in chronic heart failure: ESSENTIAL (n=1,854) null on mortality and hospitalisation — and the 1990 trial's 10 vs 3 deaths on intention-to-treat
shelves.question: In adults with chronic heart failure, does oral enoximone (a phosphodiesterase inhibitor), compared with placebo, improve exercise capacity, symptoms or clinical outcomes — and what did the earliest trial's mortality count show (the ESSENTIAL programme)?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Oral · Cardiotonic Agents/therapeutic use · Enoximone · Heart Failure/drug therapy,metabolism,mortality · Humans · Imidazoles/adverse effects,therapeutic use · Multicenter Studies as Topic · Oxygen Consumption/drug effects · Placebos · Severity of Illness Index · Survival Analysis · Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Clinical Trials, Phase II as Topic · Double-Blind Method · Electrocardiography, Ambulatory · Enoximone/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Exercise Test · Exercise Tolerance/drug effects · Female · Heart Failure/physiopathology · Male · Middle Aged · Phosphodiesterase Inhibitors/administration & dosage,adverse effects · Blood Pressure/physiology · Cardiotonic Agents/administration & dosage · Chronic Disease · Enoximone/administration & dosage · Exercise/physiology · Exercise Tolerance · Heart Failure/drug therapy,mortality,physiopathology · Heart Rate/physiology · Hospitalization/statistics & numerical data · Kaplan-Meier Estimate · Young Adult
shelves.balance: The mortality record is this row. The programme's arc is given in full: a small 1990 trial with significantly more deaths on enoximone (10 versus 3 on intention-to-treat analysis, P < 0.05, with dropout 46% versus 25%), a small 2000 low-dose trial with an exercise-capacity win and no arrhythmia signal, and the large modern ESSENTIAL programme (1,854 randomised) that was safe but null on outcomes — mortality HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.17) and mortality-or-cardiovascular-hospitalisation HR 0.98 (0.86 to 1.12), hazard ratios being relative measures. The cards are ordered so the largest trial comes last and carries the most weight. Enoximone was never marketed orally for chronic heart failure in the US, and the exercise-capacity result must not be presented as clinical benefit. PROPOSED STAMP: LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) on major clinical outcomes.

cards.headline: 1990 multicentre trial (Uretsky 1990): no symptom or exercise benefit — and deaths 10 vs 3 on intention-to-treat (P < 0.05), 5 vs 0 during therapy, with dropout 46% vs 25% (P < 0.02)
cards.summary: 1990 multicentre trial (Uretsky 1990): no symptom or exercise benefit — and deaths 10 vs 3 on intention-to-treat (P < 0.05), 5 vs 0 during therapy, with dropout 46% vs 25% (P < 0.02)
cards.type: Multicentre randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, oral enoximone in moderate heart failure (1990)
cards.people: 102 outpatients with moderate to moderately severe congestive heart failure (50 enoximone, 52 placebo), all on long-term digoxin and diuretics without vasodilators or converting-enzyme inhibitors, in a multicentre double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial with monthly symptom scoring and exercise testing for 4 months.
cards.result: There were no differences between groups in symptoms or exercise duration at 4 months (a transient anaerobic-threshold improvement at 1 month was not sustained). The dropout rate was significantly higher on enoximone (46% versus 25%; P < 0.02). During therapy, five deaths occurred on enoximone and none on placebo (P < 0.05) — two sudden, two from progressive heart failure, one from acute myocardial infarction. With intention-to-treat analysis including patients removed for lack of drug effect, 10 deaths occurred on enoximone versus 3 on placebo (P < 0.05). Adverse effects other than death were slightly but not significantly higher on enoximone (32% versus 22%).
cards.watchOut: Small (102 patients) and from the pre-beta-blocker era — but its mortality count is the programme's founding fact and is printed in full: 5 versus 0 deaths on therapy and 10 versus 3 on intention-to-treat, both statistically significant as published.
cards.source: Uretsky BF et al. Multicenter trial of oral enoximone in patients with moderate to moderately severe congestive heart failure. Lack of benefit compared with placebo. Enoximone Multicenter Trial Group. Circulation. 1990. PMID: 2144216. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Low-dose exercise trial (Lowes 2000): exercise capacity improved by 115 s (25 mg three times daily, P = 0.013) and 117 s (50 mg, P = 0.003) at 12 weeks, with no increase in ventricular arrhythmias and deaths 2 and 0 on enoximone vs 4 on placebo
cards.summary: Low-dose exercise trial (Lowes 2000): exercise capacity improved by 115 s (25 mg three times daily, P = 0.013) and 117 s (50 mg, P = 0.003) at 12 weeks, with no increase in ventricular arrhythmias and deaths 2 and 0 on enoximone vs 4 on placebo
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, low-dose oral enoximone and exercise capacity in chronic heart failure
cards.people: 105 patients with NYHA class II–III ischaemic or non-ischaemic chronic heart failure at nine US centres, in a prospective double-blind placebo-controlled multicentre trial of enoximone 25 or 50 mg orally three times daily versus placebo for 12 weeks, with treadmill testing, quality-of-life assessment and Holter monitoring.
cards.result: By the protocol-specified last-observation-carried-forward analysis, enoximone improved exercise capacity at 12 weeks by 115 s at 25 mg three times daily (P = 0.013) and 117 s at 50 mg (P = 0.003). No increases in ventricular arrhythmias were noted. Deaths were 2 in the 25 mg group and 0 in the 50 mg group, versus 4 on placebo. Dyspnoea and patient and physician assessments of clinical status favoured the enoximone groups.
cards.watchOut: Exercise capacity is a surrogate / soft endpoint in 105 patients over 12 weeks: this trial rehabilitated the drug's short-term tolerability at low dose, not its effect on outcomes — that question belongs to ESSENTIAL, the next card.
cards.source: Lowes BD et al. Low-dose enoximone improves exercise capacity in chronic heart failure. Enoximone Study Group. Journal of the American College of Cardiology. 2000. PMID: 10933364. cards.headline: ESSENTIAL I and II (Metra 2009): 1,854 randomised — mortality HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.17) and mortality-or-cardiovascular-hospitalisation HR 0.98 (0.86 to 1.12); NO difference on major outcomes
cards.summary: ESSENTIAL I and II (Metra 2009): 1,854 randomised — mortality HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.17) and mortality-or-cardiovascular-hospitalisation HR 0.98 (0.86 to 1.12); NO difference on major outcomes
cards.type: Two identical randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trials reported together (ESSENTIAL I and II), low-dose oral enoximone in advanced heart failure
cards.people: 1,854 subjects randomised at 211 sites in 16 countries in two identical randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (ESSENTIAL-I, North and South America; ESSENTIAL-II, Europe) of low-dose oral enoximone versus placebo in NYHA class III–IV heart failure with LVEF 30% or lower and a recent hospitalisation or two worsening-HF visits, on beta-blockers and other guideline-recommended therapy.
cards.result: In the combined trials, all-cause mortality did not differ between enoximone and placebo (hazard ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.17), nor did the composite co-primary endpoint of mortality or cardiovascular hospitalisation (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.86 to 1.12) — hazard ratios are relative measures. The 6-minute walk distance increased with enoximone in ESSENTIAL-I only (P = 0.025), not reaching the pre-specified significance criterion of P < 0.020, and not in ESSENTIAL-II; the Patient Global Assessment did not differ in either trial. The authors conclude that although low-dose enoximone appears safe in advanced heart failure, major clinical outcomes are not improved.
cards.watchOut: This is the heaviest card on the shelf and it is null: two trials, one programme, reported in a single paper — counted as one programme's combined result, exactly as published, not as two independent confirmations.
cards.source: Metra M et al. Effects of low-dose oral enoximone administration on mortality, morbidity, and exercise capacity in patients with advanced heart failure: the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group ESSENTIAL trials. European heart journal. 2009. PMID: 19700774. Registry ID: none in the record. essential-ii, europe) of low-dose oral enoximone versus placebo in nyha class iii–iv heart failure with lvef 30% or lower and a recent hospitalisation or two worsening-hf visits, on beta-blockers and other guideline-recommended therapy. in the combined trials, all-cause mortality did not differ between enoximone and placebo (hazard ratio 0.97, 95% ci 0.80 to 1.17), nor did the composite co-primary endpoint of mortality or cardiovascular hospitalisation (hr 0.98, 95% ci 0.86 to 1.12) — hazard ratios are relative measures. the 6-minute walk distance increased with enoximone in essential-i only (p = 0.025), not reaching the pre-specified significance criterion of p < 0.020, and not in essential-ii; cards.headline: Synthesis: an early death signal, a small exercise win, then a large null — oral enoximone does not improve major outcomes in chronic heart failure
cards.summary: Synthesis: an early death signal, a small exercise win, then a large null — oral enoximone does not improve major outcomes in chronic heart failure
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (1990 trial n=102; low-dose exercise trial n=105; ESSENTIAL I and II n=1,854 combined).
cards.result: Read in programme order: the 1990 trial found no symptom or exercise benefit and significantly more deaths on enoximone (10 versus 3 intention-to-treat); the 2000 low-dose trial found better exercise capacity (+115 to +117 s) with no arrhythmia signal and few deaths either way; ESSENTIAL, ten times larger than both combined and run on modern background therapy, found mortality HR 0.97 and composite HR 0.98 — no difference — with its walk-test signal confined to one of its two trials and below its own pre-specified threshold. Enoximone was never marketed orally for chronic heart failure in the US. The stamp is LIKELY (the treatment made no difference) on major clinical outcomes; the early mortality count stays on the face as the programme's history.
cards.watchOut: Do not average the three trials into reassurance: ESSENTIAL's safety at low dose on beta-blocker background does not erase the 1990 deaths, and neither trial set supports any claim of clinical benefit.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Pimobendan in human heart failure: PICO — exercise duration +121.6 s and quality of life better in HFrEF; MONACO in HFpEF null (+26.9 m vs +21.4 m, P = 0.402) and terminated early; not marketed for human HF in the US
shelves.question: In adults with heart failure, does the calcium-sensitising inotrope pimobendan, compared with placebo, improve exercise tolerance and quality of life in reduced-ejection-fraction disease — and does it help in HFpEF with right-ventricular–pulmonary-arterial uncoupling?

shelves.balance: Two phenotypes, two answers, never pooled. In reduced-ejection-fraction disease, the PICO trial (198 patients, 12 weeks) showed pimobendan 5 mg/day increasing exercise duration by 121.6 s and improving quality of life versus placebo, with deaths 5% on drug versus 6% on placebo (not significant) — exercise capacity and quality of life are surrogate / soft endpoints, and no mortality trial of pimobendan in human heart failure exists in this base. The Japanese evidence is a published programme SUMMARY (Kato 1997), labelled as such on its card — not a single trial report. In HFpEF with right-ventricular–pulmonary-arterial uncoupling, the MONACO trial (50 patients, single country) was terminated early after an invalid interim analysis and was null on 6-minute walk distance. Pimobendan is not marketed for human heart failure in the US; its veterinary trial record is animal evidence and is counted nowhere on this shelf. PROPOSED STAMP: SPLIT.

cards.headline: PICO multicentre trial (Kubo 1992): pimobendan 5 mg/day increased exercise duration by 121.6 ± 19.1 s (P < 0.001 vs placebo), peak VO2 by 2.23 ± 0.58 mL/kg/min and quality-of-life score by 8.5 ± 2.3 units over 12 weeks
cards.summary: PICO multicentre trial (Kubo 1992): pimobendan 5 mg/day increased exercise duration by 121.6 ± 19.1 s (P < 0.001 vs placebo), peak VO2 by 2.23 ± 0.58 mL/kg/min and quality-of-life score by 8.5 ± 2.3 units over 12 weeks
cards.type: Multicentre randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (PICO), pimobendan in moderate-to-severe heart failure
cards.people: 198 ambulatory patients with moderate-to-severe heart failure despite digitalis and diuretics (80% also on a converting-enzyme inhibitor), randomised double-blind to placebo (49) or pimobendan 2.5 mg/day (49), 5 mg/day (51) or 10 mg/day (49) for 12 weeks (the PICO trial).
cards.result: Exercise duration rose significantly on pimobendan 5 mg/day (+121.6 ± 19.1 s; P < 0.001 versus placebo) and borderline-significantly on 10 mg/day (+81.1 ± 19.5 s; P = 0.05). Peak VO2 rose by 2.23 ± 0.58 mL/kg/min on 5 mg (P < 0.01). Minnesota Living With Heart Failure score improved by 8.5 ± 2.3 units on 5 mg versus 1.3 ± 2.2 on placebo (P < 0.01). Total hospitalisations were 23 among the 49 placebo patients versus 33 across the 149 pimobendan patients — fewer per patient on drug (P < 0.01 as reported). Eleven patients died: 3 (6%) on placebo and 8 (5%) on pimobendan (P = NS). Ejection fraction and plasma norepinephrine did not differ significantly; headache became commoner with dose.
cards.watchOut: Twelve weeks, soft endpoints (exercise duration, peak VO2, questionnaire), 198 patients and a mortality count (8 vs 3) far too small to read either way: PICO supports an exercise/quality-of-life claim only. Its quality-of-life companion report is a further report of this same trial and is not carded separately.
cards.source: Kubo SH et al. Beneficial effects of pimobendan on exercise tolerance and quality of life in patients with heart failure. Results of a multicenter trial. The Pimobendan Multicenter Research Group. Circulation. 1992. PMID: 1537130. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Japanese programme summary (Kato 1997) — a published SUMMARY of the Japanese studies, not a single trial report: in its multicentre double-blind trial, 8 weeks of pimobendan 2.5 mg twice daily improved symptoms and signs in 52.6% and NYHA class in 64.1% of patients
cards.summary: Japanese programme summary (Kato 1997) — a published SUMMARY of the Japanese studies, not a single trial report: in its multicentre double-blind trial, 8 weeks of pimobendan 2.5 mg twice daily improved symptoms and signs in 52.6% and NYHA class in 64.1% of patients
cards.type: Programme summary report of the Japanese pimobendan studies (labelled as a summary — not a single trial report)
cards.people: The Japanese pimobendan programme as summarised in this report: acute heart failure patients given single oral doses; a multicentre, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial of pimobendan 2.5 mg twice daily for 8 weeks; a further double-blind placebo-controlled study of 1.25 and 2.5 mg twice daily; and a pooled multiple-dose safety set of 241 patients.
cards.result: As summarised: a single oral 2.5 mg dose in acute heart failure increased cardiac index by 27.9% and stroke volume index by 24.4% and decreased pulmonary capillary wedge pressure by 21.3% (relative changes as published). In the multicentre double-blind trial, 8 weeks of pimobendan 2.5 mg twice daily definitely improved symptoms and signs in 52.6% of patients and NYHA class in 64.1%, with a significantly greater increase in physical activity than placebo; another double-blind study suggested long-term benefit on morbidity and quality of life at 1.25 and 2.5 mg twice daily. Adverse reactions occurred in 26 of 241 patients (10.8%) on multiple doses, none serious.
cards.watchOut: Programme summary, single-region (Japan): percentages are the summary's own responder-style figures without a cardable per-trial denominator set, so this card supports the programme's existence and direction only and is never load-bearing beside PICO.
cards.source: Kato K Clinical efficacy and safety of pimobendan in treatment of heart failure--experience in Japan. Cardiology. 1997. PMID: 9142433. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: MONACO trial in HFpEF (Nakagawa 2026): 6-minute walk distance changed +26.9 m on pimobendan vs +21.4 m on placebo at 30 days (P = 0.402) — NOT significant; enrolment terminated after an invalid interim analysis
cards.summary: MONACO trial in HFpEF (Nakagawa 2026): 6-minute walk distance changed +26.9 m on pimobendan vs +21.4 m on placebo at 30 days (P = 0.402) — NOT significant; enrolment terminated after an invalid interim analysis
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (MONACO), pimobendan in HFpEF with RV–PA uncoupling — terminated early
cards.people: 50 hospitalised patients with HFpEF (LVEF 50% or greater) and right-ventricular–pulmonary-arterial uncoupling (TAPSE/PASP below 0.57 mm/mmHg) at 12 Japanese centres, randomised 1:1 to pimobendan 1.25 mg twice daily (24) or placebo (26) for 30 days; median age 82 years, 46% women.
cards.result: Mean change in 6-minute walk distance at day 30 was +26.9 m (95% CI −2.0 to +55.8) on pimobendan versus +21.4 m (95% CI −14.3 to +57.2) on placebo — not significantly different (P = 0.402). Enrolment was terminated because of the invalid result of the planned interim analysis. The authors conclude pimobendan for 30 days did not significantly improve exercise capacity in HFpEF with RV–PA uncoupling.
cards.watchOut: A different phenotype from PICO (preserved, not reduced, ejection fraction; 30 days, not 12 weeks; n=50, single country, stopped early): a separate, negative slice that must never be pooled with the HFrEF result in either direction.

cards.headline: Synthesis: pimobendan's human record is a 12-week exercise/quality-of-life benefit in HFrEF, a labelled Japanese programme summary, and a null, terminated HFpEF trial — no mortality evidence exists
cards.summary: Synthesis: pimobendan's human record is a 12-week exercise/quality-of-life benefit in HFrEF, a labelled Japanese programme summary, and a null, terminated HFpEF trial — no mortality evidence exists
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (PICO n=198; Japanese programme summary, pooled safety set n=241; MONACO n=50).
cards.result: In reduced-ejection-fraction heart failure, PICO showed pimobendan improving exercise duration (+121.6 s at 5 mg/day), peak VO2 and quality-of-life scores versus placebo over 12 weeks, with no significant mortality difference in a trial far too small to judge one. The Japanese programme summary points the same way on symptoms and NYHA class and is labelled a summary, not a trial. In HFpEF with RV–PA uncoupling, MONACO found no significant walk-distance benefit and was terminated early. No mortality trial of pimobendan in human heart failure exists in this base, and the drug is not marketed for human heart failure in the US (its well-known trial record in dogs is veterinary evidence, counted nowhere here). The stamp is SPLIT by phenotype and endpoint.
cards.watchOut: Do not import the veterinary pimobendan record (EPIC, PROTECT) into this shelf, and do not read PICO's soft-endpoint win as outcome benefit: the human outcomes question was never trialled at scale.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Vupanorsen (ANGPTL3 antisense, discontinued): triglycerides down 41–57% relative and non-HDL cholesterol down 22–28% relative — but a dose-dependent hepatic-fat increase of up to 76% relative ended development
shelves.question: In adults with hypertriglyceridaemia or elevated non-HDL cholesterol, does the ANGPTL3 antisense oligonucleotide vupanorsen, compared with placebo, lower triglycerides and atherogenic lipoproteins — and what hepatic harm ended its development?
shelves.mesh: Angiopoietin-Like Protein 3 · Angiopoietin-like Proteins/genetics · Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2/drug therapy,genetics · Double-Blind Method · Galactosamine · Humans · Hypertriglyceridemia/drug therapy,genetics · Lipoproteins · Pharmaceutical Preparations · RNA, Messenger · Triglycerides · Adult · Apolipoproteins B · Cholesterol · Cholesterol, HDL · Cholesterol, LDL · Female · Hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA Reductase Inhibitors/adverse effects · Hypercholesterolemia · Injection Site Reaction · Male · Middle Aged · Angiopoietin-like Proteins/metabolism · Oligonucleotides, Antisense/therapeutic use,pharmacology · Liver/metabolism,drug effects,pathology · Hyperlipidemias/drug therapy,metabolism · Aged · Triglycerides/blood,metabolism
shelves.balance: Discontinued agent — this flag leads. Vupanorsen's development was discontinued after TRANSLATE-TIMI 70: the dose-dependent increase in hepatic fat fraction (up to 76% relative; absolute increase up to 7.0 percentage points) and the transaminase elevations (over 3× the upper limit of normal in up to 44.4% at higher doses) printed in its own primary report are the central fact of the programme and lead this balance, ahead of the lipid wins. Programme labelling: three reports but only TWO distinct trials — the hepatic-fat paper (Zimerman 2024) is a companion report of TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 (227 of its 286 participants), counted as a report of one programme, not independent evidence. All endpoints are lipid (surrogate) measures; no outcomes trial exists. Percent changes are relative measures and are labelled as such throughout. PROPOSED STAMP: SPLIT.

cards.headline: Phase 2 trial in T2D with hepatic steatosis (Gaudet 2020): triglycerides fell 36%, 53% and 47% relative on vupanorsen vs 16% on placebo over 6 months — with NO improvement in glycaemic parameters or hepatic fat fraction
cards.summary: Phase 2 trial in T2D with hepatic steatosis (Gaudet 2020): triglycerides fell 36%, 53% and 47% relative on vupanorsen vs 16% on placebo over 6 months — with NO improvement in glycaemic parameters or hepatic fat fraction
cards.type: Phase 2 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial, vupanorsen in type 2 diabetes with hepatic steatosis and hypertriglyceridaemia
cards.people: 105 patients with fasting triglycerides over 150 mg/dL (1.7 mmol/L), type 2 diabetes and hepatic steatosis (median baseline triglycerides 2.84 mmol/L [252 mg/dL]), in a double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging phase 2 study of vupanorsen 40 or 80 mg every 4 weeks or 20 mg weekly, or placebo, subcutaneously for 6 months.
cards.result: Triglycerides fell by 36%, 53% and 47% (relative changes as published) on the three vupanorsen regimens versus 16% on placebo, and ANGPTL3 fell by 41%, 59% and 56% versus an 8% rise on placebo. Versus placebo, vupanorsen 80 mg every 4 weeks reduced apolipoprotein C-III by 58%, remnant cholesterol by 38%, total cholesterol by 19%, non-HDL cholesterol by 18%, HDL cholesterol by 24% and apolipoprotein B by 9% (relative changes). There was no improvement in glycaemic parameters or hepatic fat fraction. The commonest adverse events were generally mild injection-site reactions, with no clinically significant platelet-count changes.
cards.watchOut: The hepatic-fat sentence cuts both ways and is printed whole: no improvement in hepatic fat fraction in a population selected for steatosis — the later, larger trial showed the fat fraction actively rising with dose (cards below).
cards.source: Gaudet D et al. Vupanorsen, an N-acetyl galactosamine-conjugated antisense drug to ANGPTL3 mRNA, lowers triglycerides and atherogenic lipoproteins in patients with diabetes, hepatic steatosis, and hypertriglyceridaemia. European heart journal. 2020. PMID: 32860031. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 (Bergmark 2022): placebo-adjusted non-HDL cholesterol down 22.0–27.7% relative and triglycerides down 41.3–56.8% relative — but >3× transaminase elevations in up to 44.4% and a dose-dependent hepatic-fat increase of up to 76% relative
cards.summary: TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 (Bergmark 2022): placebo-adjusted non-HDL cholesterol down 22.0–27.7% relative and triglycerides down 41.3–56.8% relative — but >3× transaminase elevations in up to 44.4% and a dose-dependent hepatic-fat increase of up to 76% relative
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (TRANSLATE-TIMI 70), vupanorsen in statin-treated hypercholesterolaemia with hypertriglyceridaemia
cards.people: 286 adults with non-HDL cholesterol 100 mg/dL or over and triglycerides 150–500 mg/dL on statin therapy, randomised double-blind to placebo (44) or one of seven vupanorsen dose regimens (242; 80, 120 or 160 mg every 4 weeks, or 60, 80, 120 or 160 mg every 2 weeks) for 24 weeks; median age 64 years, 44% women, median non-HDL cholesterol 132.4 mg/dL and median triglycerides 216.2 mg/dL.
cards.result: Placebo-adjusted non-HDL cholesterol fell by 22.0% to 27.7% relative across doses (all P < 0.001), triglycerides by 41.3% to 56.8% relative (all P < 0.001), with more modest LDL cholesterol (7.9–16.0%) and apolipoprotein B (6.0–15.1%) effects and ANGPTL3 reductions of 69.9% to 95.2%. Against this: injection-site reactions in up to 33.3% and alanine/aspartate aminotransferase elevations over 3× the upper limit of normal in up to 44.4% at higher total monthly doses, and a dose-dependent increase in hepatic fat fraction of up to 76% relative. No confirmed significant decline in renal function or platelet count occurred.
cards.watchOut: The harm is in the primary report itself, dose-dependent, and it is what ended the programme: any citation of this trial's lipid effects without its hepatic-fat and transaminase figures misrepresents the trial.
cards.source: Bergmark BA et al. Effect of Vupanorsen on Non-High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels in Statin-Treated Patients With Elevated Cholesterol: TRANSLATE-TIMI 70. Circulation. 2022. PMID: 35369705. Registry ID: NCT04516291. cards.headline: Hepatic-fat companion report of TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 (Zimerman 2024) — a companion report of the trial above, NOT an independent trial: hepatic fat fraction rose up to 76% relative (absolute up to +7.0 percentage points), only moderately correlated with AST/ALT (rho ≈ 0.49–0.50)
cards.summary: Hepatic-fat companion report of TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 (Zimerman 2024) — a companion report of the trial above, NOT an independent trial: hepatic fat fraction rose up to 76% relative (absolute up to +7.0 percentage points), only moderately correlated with AST/ALT (rho ≈ 0.49–0.50)
cards.type: Companion report of TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 (same trial as the previous card — labelled, not independent evidence)
cards.people: 227 of the 286 TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 participants with hepatic fat fraction measured at baseline and 24 weeks (median baseline hepatic fat fraction 8.5%) — the same trial as the previous card, analysed for the hepatic-fat question.
cards.result: Vupanorsen produced dose-dependent relative increases in hepatic fat fraction of up to 76% at 24 weeks (P < 0.001), corresponding to an absolute increase of up to 7.0 percentage points at the highest dose (P < 0.001); increases were numerically greater in patients with elevated baseline hepatic fat, body-mass index, triglycerides or diabetes. Changes in hepatic fat correlated only moderately with changes in AST (rho = 0.49; P < 0.001) and ALT (rho = 0.50; P < 0.001) — liver enzymes are an imperfect detector of the fat increase, as the authors conclude.
cards.watchOut: Companion report, counted as a report of one programme: it deepens the harm characterisation of TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 (enzymes under-detect the fat rise) and adds no new patients and no independent confirmation.
cards.source: Zimerman A et al. Hepatic fat changes with antisense oligonucleotide therapy targeting ANGPTL3. Journal of clinical lipidology. 2024. PMID: 38158248. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: two trials, three reports — lipid lowering that was real, and a hepatic-fat harm that was decisive; development discontinued
cards.summary: Synthesis: two trials, three reports — lipid lowering that was real, and a hepatic-fat harm that was decisive; development discontinued
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (phase 2 trial n=105; TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 n=286, with its hepatic-fat companion covering 227 of the same participants).
cards.result: Vupanorsen lowered atherogenic lipids dose-dependently in both trials — triglycerides by up to 53% relative in phase 2 and by 41.3–56.8% relative (placebo-adjusted) in TRANSLATE-TIMI 70, non-HDL cholesterol by 22.0–27.7% relative — all surrogate endpoints, with no outcomes trial. The same programme showed no hepatic-fat improvement in steatotic patients in phase 2 and then a dose-dependent hepatic-fat increase of up to 76% relative (up to +7.0 percentage points absolute) with transaminase elevations over 3× normal in up to 44.4% at higher doses; development was discontinued after TRANSLATE-TIMI 70. The stamp is SPLIT, with the hepatic harm leading: on this record the harm, not the lipid effect, decided the programme's fate.
cards.watchOut: Programme counting matters: three reports, two trials. The phase 1 single-dose pharmacokinetic studies and the remnant-cholesterol re-analysis of TRANSLATE-TIMI 70 are not carded and must not be counted as further evidence.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Perhexiline in chronic HFrEF: exactly 2 results reports (106 patients) — exercise capacity and energetics improved, ejection fraction disagreed, no outcomes trial
shelves.question: In adults with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, does the metabolic modulator perhexiline, compared with placebo, improve exercise capacity, ejection fraction and cardiac energetics?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Cardiovascular Agents · Chronic Disease · Echocardiography, Stress · Fatty Acids · Female · Glucose · Heart Failure · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Myocardial Ischemia · Myocardium · Oxygen Consumption · Perhexiline · Quality of Life · Stroke Volume · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) on a FLOOR-RISK base of exactly 2 results reports totalling 106 randomised patients, both short-term. In the 2005 chronic heart failure trial, peak oxygen consumption, ejection fraction and quality of life all improved significantly on perhexiline. In the 2015 dilated-cardiomyopathy trial, the myocardial phosphocreatine/ATP ratio rose 30% relative and NYHA class improved, but ejection fraction did NOT change — the two trials disagree on ejection fraction, and both readings are printed. Every endpoint is a surrogate or soft measure; no outcomes trial exists. The HFpEF paper in this programme is a hypothesis/design abstract only and is never counted or carded as a report. Perhexiline is an old antianginal with a narrow therapeutic index: therapeutic drug monitoring is required where it remains available (Australia/New Zealand), and it is not marketed in the US.

cards.headline: Chronic heart failure RCT (Lee 2005): perhexiline improved peak VO2 (16.1 to 18.8 mL/kg/min), ejection fraction (24% to 34%) and quality of life over short-term treatment
cards.summary: Chronic heart failure RCT (Lee 2005): perhexiline improved peak VO2 (16.1 to 18.8 mL/kg/min), ejection fraction (24% to 34%) and quality of life over short-term treatment
cards.type: Double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial, perhexiline vs placebo, chronic heart failure (short-term)
cards.people: 56 patients with optimally medicated chronic heart failure, randomised double-blind to perhexiline (n=28) or placebo (n=28); regional myocardial function was assessed by stress echocardiography in ischaemic disease and skeletal-muscle energetics by 31P spectroscopy in non-ischaemic disease.
cards.result: Peak exercise oxygen consumption rose from 16.1 +/- 0.6 to 18.8 +/- 1.1 mL/kg/min on perhexiline (P<0.001), left ventricular ejection fraction rose from 24 +/- 1% to 34 +/- 2% (P<0.001), and the Minnesota quality-of-life score fell from 45 +/- 5 to 34 +/- 5 (P=0.04). Resting and peak stress regional myocardial function increased, and skeletal-muscle phosphocreatine recovery normalised. There were no adverse effects during the treatment period, and the authors note the dosage must be adjusted according to plasma levels.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK base: one of exactly two results reports (106 patients in total across both). Short-term treatment, surrogate and soft endpoints only, and its ejection-fraction gain was not reproduced in the 2015 trial carded below.
cards.source: Lee L et al. Metabolic modulation with perhexiline in chronic heart failure: a randomized, controlled trial of short-term use of a novel treatment. Circulation. 2005. PMID: 16301359. cards.headline: Dilated-cardiomyopathy energetics RCT (Beadle 2015): myocardial phosphocreatine/ATP ratio rose 30% relative and NYHA class improved on perhexiline — but ejection fraction did not change
cards.summary: Dilated-cardiomyopathy energetics RCT (Beadle 2015): myocardial phosphocreatine/ATP ratio rose 30% relative and NYHA class improved on perhexiline — but ejection fraction did not change
cards.type: Double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial, perhexiline vs placebo, non-ischaemic systolic heart failure (1 month)
cards.people: 50 patients with non-ischaemic systolic heart failure (mean LVEF 27.0%, NYHA class II-IV), randomised double-blind to perhexiline 200 mg or placebo for 1 month; a substudy of 22 patients underwent cross-heart blood sampling.
cards.result: The myocardial phosphocreatine/ATP ratio rose 30% relative on perhexiline (1.16 +/- 0.39 to 1.51 +/- 0.51, P<0.001) versus a 3% fall on placebo (1.36 +/- 0.31 to 1.34 +/- 0.31, P=0.37). NYHA functional class improved versus placebo (P=0.036). Left ventricular ejection fraction did not change, and cross-heart measures of cardiac substrate uptake and respiratory exchange ratio did not differ between groups.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK base: the second of exactly two results reports. One month of treatment; the primary measure is a cardiac-energetics surrogate, and the ejection-fraction result contradicts the 2005 trial — both are printed on this shelf.
cards.source: Beadle RM et al. Improvement in cardiac energetics by perhexiline in heart failure due to dilated cardiomyopathy. JACC. Heart failure. 2015. PMID: 25650370. Registry ID: NCT00841139. shelves.title: Gemcabene for lipids: 2 randomised trials — HDL/triglycerides up at low doses, LDL down at high doses and on a statin; the HoFH report is sub-floor (N=8, uncontrolled)
shelves.question: In adults with hypercholesterolaemia or low HDL cholesterol, does gemcabene, compared with placebo (alone, added to a statin, or added to standard care in homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia), lower LDL cholesterol and triglycerides and raise HDL cholesterol?
shelves.mesh: Abdominal Pain · Adolescent · Adult · Apolipoproteins B · Asthenia · Blood Urea Nitrogen · C-Reactive Protein · Caproates · Cholesterol, LDL · Double-Blind Method · Drug Therapy, Combination · Female · Humans · Hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA Reductase Inhibitors · Hypercholesterolemia · Male · Middle Aged · Placebo Effect · Treatment Outcome · Young Adult
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE (benefit) on a FLOOR-RISK base of exactly 3 reports, only 2 of them randomised. In the low-HDL dose-response trial (161 patients), the lipid effect split by dose: at 150-300 mg, HDL cholesterol rose up to 18% relative and triglycerides fell up to 39% relative in the high-triglyceride stratum, while at 600-900 mg LDL cholesterol fell 15-25% relative in both strata. Added to a statin (66 patients, 8 weeks), gemcabene lowered LDL cholesterol by 23.4% and 27.7% relative versus 6.2% relative on placebo. The third report, COBALT-1 in homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, is sub-floor (N=8, open-label, uncontrolled) and is never load-bearing. All endpoints are lipid (surrogate) measures; no outcomes trial exists, and no marketed product resulted from these trials.

cards.headline: Low-HDL dose-response RCT (Bays 2003): gemcabene raised HDL cholesterol 18% relative and cut triglycerides up to 39% relative at low doses (high-TG stratum); at 600-900 mg it lowered LDL cholesterol 15-25% relative
cards.summary: Low-HDL dose-response RCT (Bays 2003): gemcabene raised HDL cholesterol 18% relative and cut triglycerides up to 39% relative at low doses (high-TG stratum); at 600-900 mg it lowered LDL cholesterol 15-25% relative
cards.type: Double-blind randomised dose-response trial, gemcabene vs placebo, low HDL cholesterol (12 weeks)
cards.people: 161 patients with HDL cholesterol <35 mg/dL and triglycerides either >=200 mg/dL (n=94) or <200 mg/dL (n=67), randomised double-blind after a 6-week placebo/dietary lead-in to gemcabene 150, 300, 600 or 900 mg or placebo once daily for 12 weeks.
cards.result: In the triglycerides >=200 mg/dL stratum, HDL cholesterol rose significantly by 18% relative at 150 mg (apolipoprotein A-I and A-II each up 6% relative), and triglycerides fell significantly by 27% and 39% relative at 150 and 300 mg; the 12% relative HDL rise at 300 mg was not significant. No significant HDL or triglyceride differences were found at 600-900 mg in that stratum, or at any dose in the low-triglyceride stratum. At 600 and 900 mg, LDL cholesterol fell significantly by 15% to 25% relative in both triglyceride strata, with proportionate apolipoprotein B decreases. Adverse-event frequency was similar to placebo. All percent changes are relative measures, as reported.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK base: one of only two randomised gemcabene trials. The HDL/triglyceride wins are confined to the high-triglyceride stratum and to the lower doses; the LDL effect appears only at the higher doses — the dose split is on the face, not averaged away.
cards.source: Bays HE et al. Effectiveness and tolerability of a new lipid-altering agent, gemcabene, in patients with low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. The American Journal of Cardiology. 2003. PMID: 12943873. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Statin add-on phase 2 RCT (Stein 2016): gemcabene on a statin lowered LDL cholesterol by 23.4% and 27.7% relative versus 6.2% relative on placebo over 8 weeks
cards.summary: Statin add-on phase 2 RCT (Stein 2016): gemcabene on a statin lowered LDL cholesterol by 23.4% and 27.7% relative versus 6.2% relative on placebo over 8 weeks
cards.type: Phase 2 double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial, gemcabene vs placebo added to stable statin therapy (8 weeks)
cards.people: 66 patients (men and postmenopausal women aged 18-65) with LDL cholesterol >=130 mg/dL (3.4 mmol/L) on stable low- to high-intensity statin therapy (the majority moderate intensity), randomised 1:1:1 to gemcabene 300 mg, 900 mg or placebo once daily for 8 weeks.
cards.result: Mean LDL cholesterol change was -23.4 +/- 4.7% relative on gemcabene 300 mg (P=0.005) and -27.7 +/- 4.3% relative on 900 mg (P<0.001), versus -6.2 +/- 4.3% relative on placebo. Median C-reactive protein change was -26.1% relative at 300 mg (P=0.196) and -53.9% relative at 900 mg (P<0.001) versus -11.1% relative on placebo. Gemcabene was well tolerated, with no significant difference in adverse events versus placebo. All percent changes are relative measures, as reported.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK base: the second of only two randomised trials (66 patients, 8 weeks). Lipid and CRP measures are surrogates; there is no cardiovascular-outcomes trial of gemcabene.

cards.headline: COBALT-1 in homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (Gaudet 2019): mean LDL cholesterol fell 26-30% relative over 12 weeks — SUB-FLOOR report (N=8, open-label, no control arm), never load-bearing
cards.summary: COBALT-1 in homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (Gaudet 2019): mean LDL cholesterol fell 26-30% relative over 12 weeks — SUB-FLOOR report (N=8, open-label, no control arm), never load-bearing
cards.type: Open-label single-arm dose-escalation study (COBALT-1), gemcabene added to standard care in HoFH — sub-floor (N=8), labelled, never load-bearing
cards.people: 8 patients with a clinical or genetic diagnosis of homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia on stable standard care including statins, ezetimibe and PCSK9 inhibitors, treated open-label with gemcabene 300 mg for 4 weeks, then 600 mg for 4 weeks, then 900 mg for 4 weeks. SUB-FLOOR: N=8 is below the library's 10-human reference floor.
cards.result: All 8 patients completed the 12 weeks. Mean LDL cholesterol change from baseline was -26% relative at week 4 (300 mg, P=0.004), -30% relative at week 8 (600 mg, P=0.001) and -29% relative at week 12 (900 mg, P=0.001). With no control arm, these within-patient changes cannot separate a drug effect from background variation and concurrent standard care. All percent changes are relative measures, as reported.
cards.watchOut: SUB-FLOOR (N=8, open-label, uncontrolled): carded only to show the programme reached the homozygous-FH population. This shelf stands or falls on the two randomised trials above; COBALT-1 supports no efficacy claim.

cards.headline: Synthesis: 2 randomised trials show dose-dependent lipid effects (HDL/triglyceride at low doses, LDL at high doses and on a statin); the only HoFH report is sub-floor and uncontrolled
cards.summary: Synthesis: 2 randomised trials show dose-dependent lipid effects (HDL/triglyceride at low doses, LDL at high doses and on a statin); the only HoFH report is sub-floor and uncontrolled
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Across 161 low-HDL patients and 66 statin-treated patients, gemcabene moved lipid surrogates in a dose-dependent pattern over 8-12 weeks, and was tolerated like placebo in both trials. COBALT-1's 8-patient open-label LDL falls are consistent in direction but prove nothing on their own. No trial measured cardiovascular outcomes, and no marketed product resulted from this programme.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Eculizumab in PNH — the founding slice (PARTIAL beside #1804/#845): TRIUMPH 49% vs 0% haemoglobin stabilisation, 0 vs 10 median units; SHEPHERD and the pre/post TE analysis
shelves.question: In patients with paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, does the terminal-complement (C5) inhibitor eculizumab reduce intravascular haemolysis, stabilise haemoglobin and cut transfusion requirements versus placebo (TRIUMPH) — and are the effects maintained in a broader, openly treated population (SHEPHERD), including on thromboembolism, the disease's leading cause of death?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Antibodies, Monoclonal/adverse effects/therapeutic use · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized · Complement C5/immunology · Double-Blind Method · Erythrocyte Transfusion · Fatigue · Female · Hemoglobins/analysis · Hemoglobinuria, Paroxysmal/blood/drug therapy/therapy · Hemolysis/drug effects · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Quality of Life
shelves.balance: PARTIAL beside live #1804 and live #845 — only the founding slice is carded here: eculizumab versus placebo (TRIUMPH) and versus the pre-treatment course (SHEPHERD and the pooled analyses). LIKELY (benefit) on that slice: TRIUMPH, the one placebo RCT (n=87), found haemoglobin stabilisation without transfusion in 49% (21/43) vs 0% (0/44) and a median of 0 vs 10 transfused units, with the LDH area under the curve 85.8% lower (a relative measure beside its absolutes). SHEPHERD (n=97, single-arm) extended the effect to a broader population (LDH down 87% against baseline; 51% transfusion-independent for 52 weeks). The thromboembolism figure (1.07 vs 7.37 events per 100 patient-years; 85% relative, 6.3 absolute) is a pre/post contrast, not a randomised endpoint. Meningococcal infection risk on terminal-complement blockade is the pricing harm. Ravulizumab vs eculizumab is live #1804 and proximal inhibitors are live #845 — neither re-carded.

cards.headline: TRIUMPH (Hillmen 2006, the only placebo RCT): eculizumab stabilised haemoglobin without transfusion in 49% (21/43) vs 0% (0/44) on placebo; median transfused units 0 vs 10
cards.summary: TRIUMPH (Hillmen 2006, the only placebo RCT): eculizumab stabilised haemoglobin without transfusion in 49% (21/43) vs 0% (0/44) on placebo; median transfused units 0 vs 10
cards.type: Double-blind randomised placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (TRIUMPH), eculizumab vs placebo in PNH
cards.people: 87 patients with paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria randomised double-blind to eculizumab (600 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 900 mg, then 900 mg every other week through week 26) or placebo, multicentre phase 3. The two primary endpoints were stabilisation of haemoglobin levels and units of packed red cells transfused.
cards.result: Stabilisation of haemoglobin in the absence of transfusions was achieved in 49% (21 of 43) on eculizumab versus 0% (0 of 44) on placebo (P<0.001). A median of 0 units of packed red cells was transfused on eculizumab versus 10 units on placebo (P<0.001). Intravascular haemolysis fell, with the median lactate dehydrogenase area under the curve 85.8% lower on eculizumab (58,587 vs 411,822 U per litre; P<0.001) — a relative measure beside its absolute values. Fatigue and quality-of-life scores improved significantly. Serious adverse events occurred in 4 eculizumab and 9 placebo patients, none considered treatment-related.
cards.watchOut: PARTIAL shelf: the placebo-controlled claim for eculizumab in PNH rests on this one small trial (n=87) alone — everything else on this shelf is single-arm or pre/post. Later PNH questions are homed elsewhere: ravulizumab vs eculizumab at live shelf #1804 and proximal inhibitors beyond eculizumab at live shelf #845 — neither is re-carded here. Terminal-complement blockade carries meningococcal infection risk, the pricing harm of this drug class, which belongs on the face of any eculizumab shelf.
cards.source: Hillmen P et al. The complement inhibitor eculizumab in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria. The New England Journal of Medicine. 2006. PMID: 16990386. Registry ID: NCT00122330. cards.headline: SHEPHERD (Brodsky 2008, open-label single-arm): haemolysis (LDH) fell 87% against baseline; median transfused units fell from 8.0 before treatment to 0.0 during the study; 51% transfusion-independent for 52 weeks
cards.summary: SHEPHERD (Brodsky 2008, open-label single-arm): haemolysis (LDH) fell 87% against baseline; median transfused units fell from 8.0 before treatment to 0.0 during the study; 51% transfusion-independent for 52 weeks
cards.type: Open-label single-arm phase 3 study (SHEPHERD), eculizumab in a broader PNH population — pre/post comparisons
cards.people: 97 patients with PNH at 33 international sites — a broader population than TRIUMPH — treated openly with eculizumab (600 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 900 mg, then 900 mg every 14 days) for 52 weeks, phase 3, with no placebo arm; comparisons are against each patient's pre-treatment course.
cards.result: Haemolysis, measured by lactate dehydrogenase, fell by 87% against baseline (P<0.001) — a relative measure beside the transfusion absolutes. The median transfused units fell from 8.0 per patient before treatment to 0.0 during the study (P<0.001); mean transfused units fell from 12.3 to 5.9 (a 52% reduction in total transfusions). Forty-nine patients (51%) achieved transfusion independence for the entire 52 weeks. Fatigue improved by 12.2 FACIT-Fatigue points (P<0.001), and quality-of-life measures improved broadly; benefits were independent of baseline haemolysis and thrombocytopenia.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm, open-label: every figure here is a before/after contrast in the same patients, not a randomised comparison, and regression to the mean and selection cannot be excluded. It extends TRIUMPH's result to a broader population; it does not independently prove it.

cards.headline: Thromboembolism analysis (Hillmen 2007, pooled pre/post, NOT a randomised contrast): TE rate 1.07 vs 7.37 events per 100 patient-years on vs before eculizumab — an 85% relative reduction, 6.3 events/100 patient-years absolute
cards.summary: Thromboembolism analysis (Hillmen 2007, pooled pre/post, NOT a randomised contrast): TE rate 1.07 vs 7.37 events per 100 patient-years on vs before eculizumab — an 85% relative reduction, 6.3 events/100 patient-years absolute
cards.type: Pooled pre/post thromboembolism analysis across the three eculizumab PNH studies (n=195) — not a randomised contrast
cards.people: All 195 patients from the three eculizumab PNH clinical studies (recruited 2002–2005) who continued into the multinational open-label extension; each patient's thromboembolism (TE) rate on eculizumab was compared with their own pre-treatment rate. TE is the leading cause of disease-related death in PNH.
cards.result: The TE event rate was 1.07 events per 100 patient-years on eculizumab versus 7.37 events per 100 patient-years before eculizumab (P<0.001) — an 85% relative reduction, printed beside its absolute reduction of 6.3 TE events per 100 patient-years. With exposure duration equalised within each patient, TE events fell from 39 before eculizumab to 3 during treatment (P<0.001). In antithrombotic-treated patients (n=103) the rate fell from 10.61 to 0.62 events per 100 patient-years (P<0.001).
cards.watchOut: This is a before/after comparison in the same patients, NOT a trial endpoint and not a randomised contrast — survivorship and era effects cannot be excluded, and the 85% figure must never be quoted without its absolute rates (1.07 vs 7.37 per 100 patient-years) and its design label. Pooled analysis of the eculizumab programme, not a fourth trial.
cards.source: Hillmen P et al. Effect of the complement inhibitor eculizumab on thromboembolism in patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria. Blood. 2007. PMID: 17702897. cards.headline: Anaemia analysis of TRIUMPH + SHEPHERD (Schubert 2008): haemoglobin and transfusion benefits held regardless of pre-treatment transfusion requirement
cards.summary: Anaemia analysis of TRIUMPH + SHEPHERD (Schubert 2008): haemoglobin and transfusion benefits held regardless of pre-treatment transfusion requirement
cards.type: Anaemia analysis of TRIUMPH and SHEPHERD (the two studies carded above) — not an additional trial
cards.people: Patients from the two studies carded above — the double-blind placebo-controlled TRIUMPH study and the open-label SHEPHERD study, the latter a more heterogeneous population — analysed for anaemia measures by pre-treatment transfusion stratum.
cards.result: Eculizumab reduced haemolysis regardless of pre-treatment transfusion requirements and regardless of whether patients became transfusion-dependent during treatment (P<0.001 for each). Reduced haemolysis was associated with increased PNH red-cell counts (P<0.001) while reticulocyte counts remained elevated. Haemoglobin levels were significantly higher with eculizumab than with placebo in TRIUMPH and relative to baseline in SHEPHERD (P<0.001 for each study). Transfusion requirements fell across multiple pre-treatment transfusion strata, and transfusion support was eliminated in a majority of both TRIUMPH and SHEPHERD patients (P<0.001).
cards.watchOut: A secondary analysis of the same two studies — it answers 'does the benefit depend on how transfusion-heavy a patient was?' (it does not), and adds no new randomised evidence. Note the record for this report carries no registry ID — printed as 'none in the record' in its source line.

cards.result: Synthesis: PARTIAL — this shelf cards only the founding eculizumab-versus-placebo / pre-treatment slice, beside live shelf #1804 (ravulizumab vs eculizumab) and live shelf #845 (pegcetacoplan and iptacopan beyond eculizumab), which presuppose this benefit and are not re-carded. The evidence shape is printed plainly: one small double-blind placebo RCT, TRIUMPH (n=87; haemoglobin stabilisation without transfusion 49% vs 0%; median transfused units 0 vs 10), one open-label single-arm companion, SHEPHERD (n=97; LDH down 87% against baseline; 51% transfusion-independent for 52 weeks), a pooled pre/post thromboembolism analysis (1.07 vs 7.37 events per 100 patient-years — 85% relative, 6.3 absolute, not a randomised contrast), and an anaemia analysis showing the benefits held across pre-treatment transfusion strata. Meningococcal infection risk on terminal-complement blockade is the pricing harm.

shelves.title: Creatine kinase population distribution: upper limits 2–5× the manufacturer's — 97.5th percentile 1,001 U/L in black men vs 382 U/L in white men, and 49% of healthy black participants misclassified
shelves.question: In healthy general populations, what is the distribution of serum creatine kinase (CK) activity — the upper reference limits (97.5th percentile) by sex and ancestry — how far do population-derived upper limits sit above assay manufacturers' limits, and what fraction of healthy people are misclassified as having 'hyperCKaemia' by manufacturer limits?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Asian People · Black People · Creatine Kinase · Female · Health Status · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Netherlands · Reference Standards · Reference Values · Suriname · White People · Aged · Body Composition · Body Mass Index · Comorbidity · Demography · Hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA Reductase Inhibitors · Muscular Diseases · Nutrition Surveys · Racial Groups · Sex Factors · United States · Young Adult · Body Height · Body Weight · Urban Population · Ethnicity · Physical Exertion · South Africa
shelves.balance: Textbook framing: Guyton & Hall, muscle / enzyme sections — brief, and this shelf rests chiefly on the primary population-distribution literature, and says so. Datasets: 3 independent populations, plus one supporting dataset with its N not documented in its abstract (labelled, not counted). Population-derived upper limits sit 2–5 times above assay manufacturers' limits (random sample of 1,444 rested adults), so manufacturer limits misclassify 13% of white Europeans, 23% of South Asians and 49% of black participants as having 'hyperCKaemia'. NHANES (10,096 adults) gives 97.5th percentiles of 382 U/L (white men), 1,001 U/L (black men), 295 U/L (white women) and 487 U/L (black women); ancestry differences are not explained by body composition, though age differences largely are. Ancestry partitioning is the content, not a caveat. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED.

cards.headline: Stratified random population sample (1,444 adults aged 34–60, after 3 days' rest): calculated upper reference limits were 2–5 times the manufacturer's, and 13% of white Europeans, 23% of South Asians and 49% of black participants sat above the manufacturer limits
cards.summary: Stratified random population sample (1,444 adults aged 34–60, after 3 days' rest): calculated upper reference limits were 2–5 times the manufacturer's, and 13% of white Europeans, 23% of South Asians and 49% of black participants sat above the manufacturer limits
cards.type: Primary human physiology dataset (stratified random population sample after 3 days' rest, 1,444 adults)
cards.people: A stratified random sample of 1,444 individuals aged 34–60 years — mainly white European (n = 503), South Asian (n = 292) or of African descent (n = 580) — with serum creatine kinase measured after 3 days of rest; reference intervals were determined to National Committee on Clinical Laboratory Standards / Nordic Reference Interval Project guidelines. The 3-day rest condition is part of this dataset's method and prints beside its limits.
cards.result: The calculated upper reference limits (97.5th percentile) for nonblack and black women and men were 2 to 5 times higher than recommended by the assay manufacturer. Respectively 13% of the white Europeans, 23% of the South Asians and 49% of the black participants had serum CK activities above the manufacturer-provided limits — that is, up to half of healthy black participants were misclassified as having 'hyperCKaemia' by the manufacturer's limit. The authors infer that upward adjustment of the upper reference limit is necessary for all population subgroups studied.
cards.watchOut: The rest condition matters: CK is activity-sensitive, so these limits describe rested people, and the misclassification percentages describe the manufacturer's limit, not disease — this shelf gives population distributions only and makes no claim about any drug's muscle safety.
cards.source: Brewster LM et al. Distribution of creatine kinase in the general population: implications for statin therapy. American heart journal. 2007. PMID: 17892987. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: NHANES 2011–2014 (10,096 nonpregnant adults): black race strongly associated with CK (odds ratios for an 'abnormal' CK of 5.08 in women and 8.39 in men); 97.5th percentiles 382 U/L (white men), 1,001 U/L (black men), 295 U/L (white women), 487 U/L (black women)
cards.summary: NHANES 2011–2014 (10,096 nonpregnant adults): black race strongly associated with CK (odds ratios for an 'abnormal' CK of 5.08 in women and 8.39 in men); 97.5th percentiles 382 U/L (white men), 1,001 U/L (black men), 295 U/L (white women), 487 U/L (black women)
cards.type: Primary human physiology dataset (national population survey, NHANES 2011–2014, 10,096 adults)
cards.people: 10,096 nonpregnant adults aged ≥20 years from the cross-sectional National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011–2014; linear and logistic regression stratified by sex identified factors associated with CK, adjustment for anthropometric measures tested whether age and race-ethnicity differences were explained by body composition, and 95th / 97.5th percentiles were calculated by sex and race-ethnicity subgroup excluding patients with recent strenuous exercise.
cards.result: Black race was strongly associated with CK: the odds ratio of having an abnormal CK was 5.08 (95% CI 3.65 to 7.08) for black women and 8.39 (95% CI 6.11 to 11.52) for black men — odds ratios, labelled as such. CK was substantially lower in older men; differences by age, but not by race-ethnicity, were largely explained by body composition. Women with low body-mass index were less likely to have an elevated CK, and overweight or obese men had almost 2-fold greater odds of an elevated CK. The 97.5th percentile of CK was 382 U/L (95% CI 295 to 469) in white men, 1,001 U/L (718 to 1,284) in black men, 295 U/L (216 to 374) in white women and 487 U/L (310 to 664) in black women.
cards.watchOut: Ancestry partitioning is the content of this card, not a caveat: a single unpartitioned upper limit would classify a large share of healthy black men (97.5th percentile 1,001 U/L) as abnormal; 'abnormal' in the odds ratios means above the conventional limit, not diseased.
cards.source: George MD et al. Creatine kinase in the U.S. population: Impact of demographics, comorbidities, and body composition on the normal range. Medicine. 2016. PMID: 27537560. cards.headline: Employee-population dataset (1,537 individuals, 1983): three practical race / sex groups with reference ranges of 52–520 U/L (black men), 35–345 U/L (nonblack men and black women) and 25–145 U/L (nonblack women), mean levels doubling from group to group
cards.summary: Employee-population dataset (1,537 individuals, 1983): three practical race / sex groups with reference ranges of 52–520 U/L (black men), 35–345 U/L (nonblack men and black women) and 25–145 U/L (nonblack women), mean levels doubling from group to group
cards.type: Primary human physiology dataset (employee population, 1,537 individuals, 1983)
cards.people: 1,537 individuals in a hospital employee population, measured to develop reference ranges appropriate for the patient population the hospital served; race / gender subgroups were compared by analysis of variance for mean, median and range of serum CK.
cards.result: The subgroups fell into three broad groups: a high CK group composed solely of black men; an intermediate group of nonblack men plus black women; and a low group of nonblack women. Mean CK of the high group was twice that of the intermediate group, which in turn was twice that of the low group; differences within the intermediate and low groups were not significant. Practical reference ranges: 52–520 U/L for the high group, 35–345 U/L for the intermediate group and 25–145 U/L for the low group.
cards.watchOut: The oldest dataset (1983) and an employee population rather than a random population sample — but its three-group structure and doubling pattern are the same finding the two later, larger datasets reproduce, which is why it is carded as a dataset and not as history.
cards.source: Wong ET et al. Heterogeneity of serum creatine kinase activity among racial and gender groups of the population. American journal of clinical pathology. 1983. PMID: 6837521. cards.type: Supporting physiology dataset (South African race / sex comparison; N not documented in its abstract — labelled, not counted)
cards.people: A study among South Africans comparing total serum creatine kinase activity by race and sex. N NOT DOCUMENTED in the fetched abstract — printed on the face per the reference-floor labelling rule; this dataset is supporting only and is not counted among this shelf's three population datasets.
cards.result: Higher levels of total serum CK activity had been reported in black compared with white North Americans of the same sex; in this South African study such an interracial difference was notable only for males, and the difference was heightened by physical activity. The authors affirm the importance of sampling the indigenous population when developing a reference range for total CK activity. The fetched abstract prints no N and no numeric range, and this card claims neither.
cards.watchOut: Never load-bearing: with no N and no numbers in its record, this card can only corroborate the direction of the ancestry / sex pattern and the activity effect — it must not be cited for any limit or count.

cards.headline: Synthesis: 3 independent population datasets (+ 1 labelled N-not-documented supporting dataset) — population upper limits sit 2–5 times above manufacturer limits, ancestry and sex partition the distribution, and up to 49% of healthy black participants are misclassified by manufacturer limits
cards.summary: Synthesis: 3 independent population datasets (+ 1 labelled N-not-documented supporting dataset) — population upper limits sit 2–5 times above manufacturer limits, ancestry and sex partition the distribution, and up to 49% of healthy black participants are misclassified by manufacturer limits
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: Textbook framing: Guyton & Hall, muscle / enzyme sections — brief, and this shelf rests chiefly on the primary population-distribution literature, and says so. Three independent populations: the stratified random sample of 1,444 adults after 3 days' rest (upper limits 2–5 times the manufacturer's; 13% of white Europeans, 23% of South Asians and 49% of black participants above manufacturer limits); NHANES 2011–2014 (10,096 adults; 97.5th percentiles 382 U/L in white men, 1,001 U/L in black men, 295 U/L in white women, 487 U/L in black women; age differences largely explained by body composition, ancestry differences not); and the 1,537-person employee population (three groups, 52–520 / 35–345 / 25–145 U/L, means doubling group to group). Plus one supporting dataset with its N not documented in its abstract (South African comparison; labelled, not counted in the three). This shelf gives population distributions only and makes no claim about any drug's muscle safety. Cross-point only: the statin-myopathy shelves presuppose a CK upper limit without asking what it is; no dataset is shared.
cards.watchOut: CK is activity- and rest-sensitive — the 3-day rest condition of the random-sample dataset and the strenuous-exercise exclusion in NHANES print beside their limits; values print in U/L as published.
